【19】After an uneventful stay in the postoperative care unit， the pa-tient was discharged to the high-dependency unit (HDU) of the Department of Gynecology and Obstetrics. Over the next5 days， her factor X levels were assessed regularly ， and SD-FFP was adminis-tered as needed. Post-operatively， the patient received a total of 15 units of SD-FFP， with no significant blood loss. She and her healthy son were discharged from the hospital on day 7， with subsequent ambulatory follow-ups.

【20】Discussion

【21】The perioperative blood management approach used by our multidisciplinary team resulted in a successful term delivery and uneventful peripartum period in a patient with factor X defi-ciency， without significant bleeding or thrombotic complications.

【22】Factor X deficiency is a rare inherited coagulopathy， manifest-ed as various degrees of bleeding diathesis . The amount of factor X required to accomplish hemostasis is unknown， but levels of 10-35% are thought to be sufficient . In severe cases of factor X deficiency， bleeding complications can arise cases ending with massive hemorrhage necessitating hyster-ectomy . Moreover， data show a greater incidence of pre-term birth and neonatal death in pregnancies that reached the stage of fetal viability . In summary， women with factor X deficiency have a higher risk for greater hemorrhage during their menstrual cycle， unfavorable pregnancy outcomes， and peripartum bleeding.

【23】The first case of a pregnant woman with factor X deficiency was reported by Brody et al. in 1960 . Konje et al. commented on a young woman with this coagulopathy who developed retroplacental hematomas during pregnancy. During her hos-pitalization， she was treated with Bioproduct Laboratory fac-tor X and there were no complications during her delivery by a cesarean section . Kumar and Mehta described a factor X-deficient woman during her 4 pregnancies who was treated with prophylactic substitute of coagulation factors. Her preg-nancy and delivery ended with a positive outcome with no postpartum complications . Bofill et al. described a factor X-deficient patient in her early twenties who did not receive replenishment with coagulation factors， and the decision was made to treat her with FFP while she was in labor and during the first day after giving birth to her child； there was no sig-nificant blood loss and she delivered a healthy newborn . The present case management was similar to that reported by Venkatesh et al.， in which a young patient with severe fac-tor X deficiency underwent emergency cesarean section after a retroplacental bleed of approximately 50 mL was observed by ultrasound . The patient was at 37 weeks of gestation and was treated with FFP and i.v. tranexamic acid preopera-tively and in the early postoperative period after a healthy baby boy was delivered . In the present case， an elective cesare an section was planned at 39 weeks' gestation. Because the patient had low levels of factor X (0.19 kIU/L)， she was sched-uled to receive 4 units of SD-FFP 1 h before the cesarean sec-tion to elevate her levels of factor X above 50%. In the postop-erative period (during the next 3 days)， she received 15 units of SD-FFP. During the operation and in the postoperative pe-riod， her blood loss was within normal limits . She was discharged from the hospital after 7 days with a healthy baby boy.

【24】Due to limited reported data， there is no agreement regard-ing the recommendation for antenatal prophylaxis in all preg nant women with factor X deficiency. Each pregnant wom-an with factor X deficiency has a unique clinical course and should be managed and treated individually. Antenatal pro-phylaxis should be well planned in each pregnancy with se-vere deficiency， particularly for cases with obstetric complica-tions or bleeding during pregnancy. The hemostatic strategy during delivery should be planned individually considering the level of factor X， maternal loss of blood， and the obstetric pos-sibility of bleeding .

【25】The American Society of Anesthesiologists Task Force on Perioperative Blood Management states that FFP is indicated for correction of excessive microvascular bleeding (i.e.， coagu-lopathy) in the presence of an INR greater than 2.0 or for cor-rection of excessive microvascular bleeding secondary to coag-ulation factor deficiency in patients transfused with more than1 unit of blood volume (approximately 70 ml/kg) and when PT， INR， or PTT cannot be obtained in a timely fashion .

【26】Conclusions

【27】The present case involved a woman with severe factor X de-ficiency who was scheduled for a planned cesarean section. To optimize outcome and minimize the patient's risk for hem-orrhage， a multidisciplinary approach was used： factor Xlev-els were monitored during pregnancy， as well as in the pre-operative and early postoperative period， a predefined labor plan was devised， and intraoperative and early postoperative SD-FFP was used.

【0】Background

【1】Hydrocephalus is one of the most commonly encountered dis-orders involving the pediatric population， underlying a wide spectrum of pathological entities， including congenital malfor-mations， subependymal hemorrhage of prematurity， posterior fossa tumors， infectious diseases or spinal dysraphic states.

【2】It is postulated that hydrocephalus appears when there is a dis crepancy between the normal cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) produc-tion rate and the relative absorption capacity of the brain .

【3】The optimal imaging modality for the detection of hydroceph-alus， as well as for the investigation- prediction of success of any applied treatment modality is magnetic resonance imag-ing (MRI)， as it provides anatomical details along with infor-mation about flow of CSF .

【4】Children suffering from hydrocephalus display a spectrum of signal changes detectable on MRI， notably dilatation of the lat-eral ventricles， mainly of the frontal and temporal horns the temporal horns， CSF flow voids ， effacement of the cortical sulci and inability to distinguish gray-white matter junction， and in severe cases subependymal edema (transependymal flow) in the white matter adjacent to the frontal and occipital horns . Another well recognized imaging finding is the ap-pearance of a rim of hyperintensity in the lateral periventric-ular white matter， more steadily detectable on MRI with fluid-attenuated inversion recovery (FLAIR)  or diffusion imaging.

【5】More precisely， increased CSF pressure within the ventricu-lar cavities is coupled with reversal of normal centripetal bulk flow of CSF into the ventricular system . The resulting pres-sure gradient directs obligatory the CSF of the intraventricu lar compartment into the extracellular brain compartment， via the ependymal lining of the ventricles. The resultant increased water content encountered within the brain parenchyma can be radiologically detected via the aid of MRI. This depicts the aforementioned hyperintense rim in the vicinity of the lateral ventricular system， via the aid of FLAIR sequences .

【6】Indeed， it is well described that FLAIR sequence is a valuable screening tool for the evaluation of periventricular intersti-tial edema attributed to hydrocephalus or relevant second-ary white matter changes， underlying long-standing pediat-ric hydrocephalus .

【7】Case Report

【8】We report the case of a 7-year-old male of Greek ethnicity with a previous medical history of an ependymoma of the poste-rior fossa， which was operated on 4 years before， who had received adjuvant post-operative radiotherapy and chemo-therapy. The patient underwent regular follow-up，which veri-fied the absence of recurrent disease. The patient was treated with a ventriculoperitoneal (VP) shunt due to hydrocephalus that developed after the operation.

【9】The patient's final follow-up MRI was normal， depicting no signs of shunt malfunction or recurrent disease . A few days after， he developed symptomatology indicative of shunt malfunction， which was verified by the findings of a new

【10】MRI . More precisely， it depicted a comparative enlargement of the lateral and third ventricles， with accom-panying high signal intensity at FLAIR sequences surround-ing the lateral ventricles， indicative of subependymal edema.

【11】Besides， although the fourth ventricular size remained with-in normal limits， abnormal， high signal intensity on T2W se-quences was revealed at the posterior surface of the pons and at the mesencephalon， genu and splenium of the corpus cal-losum， posterior limb of the internal capsule bilaterally， and at the posterior commissure. The aforementioned lesions did not reveal restriction of diffusion or abnormal contrast en-hancement， so there is a remote probability to represent re-currence of disease.

【12】Current image is compatible with acute hydrocephalus， with accompanying periventricular edema. The most difficult find-ing to interpret is the abnormal signal characteristics in the region of the brainstem， as there was a remote possibility to be related to focal recurrence.

【13】Immediately after the MRl， patient underwent revision of the VP shunt， and the immediate post-operative computed to-mography (CT) scan showed improvement in the ventricular size .

【14】Patient postoperative course was uneventful and 7 days lat-er a repeat MRI scan was performed in order to discriminate the offending pathology in the region of the brain stem. There was no abnormal contrast uptake in the region of the surgical cavity， thus arguing against the possibility of local recurrence.

【15】T： 5.5mm L：-86.1mm 9：42：34np

【16】Although high signal intensity alterations were recognized at T2W sequences into the periventricular-peri-atrium cerebral white matter， right superior cerebellar peduncle and sple-nium， the signal intensity of the brainstem is normal， and the dimensions of the ventricular system are within normal lim-its .

【17】Our patient was suffering from non-obstructive， communicat-ing hydrocephalus， treated with a ventriculoperitoneal (VP) shunt. The specific pathophysiologic substrate underlying com-municating non-obstructive hydrocephalus is not well under-stood and the offending mechanisms undermining its patho-genesis are related insufficient CSF absorption， pathologically diminished brain compliance， as well as undefined obstruc-tion of CSF circulation .

【18】The unobstructed exchange of water molecules performed across the interface of brain ependyma and interstitial space， or， subsequently with the circulating blood， is a well-recog-nized phenomenon . The possibility that the pulsatile cho-roid plexuses contribute significantly to the enlargement of the ventricular system has been proposed.

【19】Water transport channels， namely aquaporins， and recognition of aquaporin-4 expression in ependymal cells and astrocytic end feet processes advocates over the scenario that water is transferred from ventricular cavities to the interstitial and the leptomeningeal surface. This could constitute an alternative hydrodynamic model of hydrocephalus . In this case， the rel-evant significance of abnormal intracranial pulsations in the occurrence and evolution of this disease entity is enhanced.

【20】Intracranial compliance is calculated based on the relevant vol-ume change， attributable to unit change in pressure. Under physiologic circumstances，that is normal volume of intracra-nial compartments and intracranial pressure， the degree of compliance determines the ability of the intracranial compart-ment to compensate effectively to an increase in brain volume， without producing an associated increase in intracranial pres-sure. The pathologically diminished compliance plays a cru-cial role in the pathophysiology of hydrocephalus， either by restricting the dampening force or by increasing impedance to CSF displacement 

【21】MRI is an invaluable tool in the evaluation of hydrocephalus·it assesses the dimensions of the ventricles， as well as oth-er parameters， such as the existence or absence of periven-tricular interstitial edema， stretching of the corpus callosum， effacement of cerebral sulci， and absence of the aqueductal CSF flow void phenomenon. FLAIR sequence can be used for the determination of the existence of periventricular intersti-tial edema secondary to hydrocephalus or of alterations of the white matter signal characteristics， secondary to long-stand-ing pediatric hydrocephalus .

【22】The exact underlying mechanism of communicating non-ob-structive hydrocephalus is not completely understood and the offending pathogenic mechanisms may include poor CSF absorption， decreased brain compliance and obstruction unable to be elucidated， which are difficu lt to be certified in every in-dividual case. Despite that， no specific signal changes referred to the floor of the fourth ventricle are noticed， as are depict-ed in our patient who suffers from the same pathologic entity.

【23】The other potential point of controversy referrers to the pos-sibility that the signal changes occurring in the region of the floor of the fourth ventricle represent tumor recurrence. It is well described that intracranial ependymomas are characterized by low TiW and high T2W signal intensity characteristics， as well as intermediate-to-high FLAIR signal intensity on MRI im-ages， relative to both gray and white matter . Signal char-acteristics of the solid part of the tumor demonstrate signifi-cant heterogeneity depicting foci of calcification，hemorrhage， or cystic degeneration. More cellular components of ependy-momas can dictate increased signal on diffusion weighted im-aging (DWI) sequences . Moreover， they are usually identifi-able on unenhanced T1-weighted ， findings that are not in correspondence with the imaging data of our patient.

【24】Moreover， when intravenous gadolinium enhancement is un-dertaken， Tl-weighted images， most commonly demonstrate intense enhancement of the soft tissue components of the tumor， intermingled with areas depicting limited enhance-ment or even not at all . Additionally， cellular， solid compo-nents of ependymomas may show increased signal intensity on DWI . None of the aforementioned imaging patterns was verified from our imaging sequences.

【25】Also， the fact that the imaging findings are reversible， as the hy-drocephalus of our patient was successfully treated， is against the scenario that the edematous changes regarding the floor of the fourth ventricle could be attributed to tumor recurrence.

【26】Conclusions

【27】When MRl is selected as the imaging modality of choice to evaluate hydrocephalus， besides the radiological investigation of the dimensions of the ventricles， more specific features can be looked for， such as the presence or absence of edema of the periventricular interstitial space， stretching of the corpus callosum， effacement of cerebral sulci， and disappearance of the aqueductal CSF flow void phenomenon.

【28】More precisely， it is important to examine for the dimensions of the temporal horns， the existence and extent of perisylvian atrophy， the transependymal flow and absence of the CSF flow void phenomenon .

【29】In our case， the interstitial edema is not restricted to the peri-ventricular white matter， as is reported from the majority of studies referred to the imaging characteristics of MRI in the evaluation of any subtype of hydrocephalus. Instead， it appears to incorporate the structures composing the floor of the fourth ventricle， as it also depicts an ependymal lining. It may be as-sociated to the raised venous pressure and cerebral swelling in the vicinity of the fourth ventricle， further impeding CSF ab-sorption by fourth ventricular ependyma. Probably， compression of the subependymal veins enhances periventricular intersti-tial edema in the floor of the fourth ventricle， as it is reversed once hydrocephalus is treated effectively. It does not seem that the outflow of the fourth ventricle is responsible for the hy-drocephalus， as no tumor recurrence was detected， as in the regions of the lateral recesses of the fourth ventricle， which they could represent a site of regrowth of the ependymoma.

【30】To the best of our knowledge， there is no other report of such a finding of reversible interstitial edema of the floor of the fourth ventricle that should be attributed to the occurrence of hydro-cephalus and disappears with its reversal. In our case， MRI， along with the neurological investigation， composes an invalu-able tool in the investigation of our patient， as the sequence of signal changes is on absolute correspondence with the clin-ical evolution of the hydrocephalus of our patient.

【31】Summarizing， the highlight of this case is the disappearance of signal abnormalities located on the brain stem， after suc-cessful treatment of hydrocephalus. This change should be attributed to that， because the possibility of being related to disease progression could not be supported (no patholog-ic contrast uptake and disappearance without treatment). To the best of our knowledge， similar radiographic findings are encountered only in the white matter in the vicinity of the su-pratentorial ventricular system， and not in the region of the brainstem， which abuts the fourth ventricle. The clinical sce-nario was more complicated from the previous medical his-tory of the operated ependymoma， in which case the possi-bility that the offending lesion could be attributed to tumor recurrence should be excluded.

【32】Declarations of interest

【0】ABSTRACT Introduction： Methemoglobinemia is an emergency condition which is the result of the oxidization of iron into ferric form. It can be congenital or acquired. Acquired methemoglobinemia due to drug toxicity， in rural areas most commonly due to intentional self-poisoning and the most common compounds， are plant growth enhancers， herbicides and indoxacarb which is a non-organophosphorus insecticide. Methods： This is a retrospective observational study of patients who are admitted in an emergency with methemoglobinemia from 2018 to the present. Results： A total of 10cases were found in the hospital records with toxic methemoglobinemia and the sex ratio is equally distributed. Farmers were predominant with 60. Ingestion was the mode of consumption in all cases. The most common compound was seaweed extract followed by plant alkaloids all cases presented to emergency initial saturation was less than 80% with the most common presenting feature being breathlessness and cyanosis and irritability in cases presenting late. Out of the 10 cases， 30% cases required mechanical ventilation at initial presentation. Despite 100% oxygen supplementation saturation levels did not improve indicating a problem with oxygen binding and unloading. All the cases were given methylene blue as the antidote of choice. 6 patients required 1 dose. In all cases saturation levels improved after ingestion of methylene blue， but 4 patients required repeat dosing， and 3 patients required exchange transfusion. Conclusion：Methemoglobinemia is a potential complication of ingestion of herbicides， plant growth extracts and plant alkaloid compounds. The presence of breathlessness，cyanosis， and persistent hypoxemia should raise suspicion of the disorder. Early institution of easily available antidote methylene blue can save lives and avert potential complications.

【1】KEYWORDS toxins， herbicides， biofertilizers， methemoglobinemia， seaweed extract

【2】Introduction

【3】Methemoglobinemia is the condition where RBCs contain more than 1% methemoglobin. Methemoglobin is the result of the oxidization of iron in the haemoglobin from ferrous (Fe+) to ferric (Fe) form. It can be either congenital or acquired. Congenital Methemoglobinemia occurs specifically due to ge-netic mutations that alter the structure or composition of haemoglobin. Acquired Methemoglobinemia is mainly due to drug toxicity. Drug-induced Methemoglobinemia is com- monly caused by local anaesthetics (benzocaine， prilocaine)， dapsone， disulfiram-alcohol reaction， celecoxib， chloroquine， cyclophosphamide， clotrimazole， flutamide and rarely by ac-etaminophen and ibuprofen. In rural areas， it appears that Methemoglobinemia is caused due intentional self-poisoning through compounds like indoxacarb (non-organophosphorus insecticide)，plant growth enhancers and herbicides. The current study aims to present an account of acquired methemoglobine-mia due to toxin ingestion.

【4】Methodology

【5】This is a retrospective observational study from 2018 to the present. The study is conducted at the emergency department of a teaching hospital situated in the tri-state region of southern India. The ED and the hospital mainly cater rural population whose main occupation is cultivation.

【6】Hospital records will be searched using the term Methe-moglobinemia and all the data collected for all the variables like demographic profile， socioeconomic factors， compounds， diagnostic methods， treatment， and outcomes. Descriptive statis-tics are used for presenting the data.

【7】Results

【8】A total of 10 cases were found in the hospital records with toxic methemoglobinemia， and the sex ratio is equally distributed in males and females. Farmers were predominant at 60%， followed by housewives at 20%.

【9】Ingestion was the mode of consumption in all cases.

【10】Seaweed extract used as biofertilizer was the most common compound， followed by plant alkaloids， 1 case had a history of consumption of urea， and another compound is unknown.

【11】Suicidal intent is the most (90%)， with 1 case having acciden tal exposure.

【12】The average time gap between consumption and presentation was 2.5 hours， ranging from 1 to 4 hours.

【13】All the patients had methemoglobinemia at the time of pre- sentation. Airway was patent in 5 patients and maintainable in 2 patients and not patent due to secretions in the remaining cases. Spo2 was less than 80% in all the cases.3 cases presented with ventilator failure and 2 patients had bradycardia，and 1 patient had a shock at the presentation time.4 patients had cyanosis rest of the patients did not show any cyanosis. pH and PCO2 measured PO2 were normal in all the cases， while bicarbonate was decreased in 60% of cases. Lactate was very high in 2 patients， high in 7 patients and normal in 1.

【14】Methemoglobinemia is identified based on the colour of blood in all cases. However， investigations like co-oxymetry or the direct measurement of methemoglobinemia are unavail-able.

【15】Electrolytes were normal in all the patients， while urea was raised in 2 patients， 1 of whom consumed urea， and creatinine was within the normal range at the time of presentation.

【16】Hepatic markers were normal at the time of presentation.

【17】All the cases were given methylene blue as the antidote of choice， 6 patients required 1 dose， 4 patients required repeat dosing， 3 cases did not recover even after repeat dosing， 6 cases recovered with the initial dose and 1 case recovered with repeat dose.

【18】3 cases required mechanical ventilation， and the rest recov-ered without the need for mechanical ventilation.

【19】The average need for an ICU stay was 7.2 days， with the least being 2 days and with highest being 15 days.

【20】The average duration of hospital stay was 12.8 days， with the least being 4 days and the highest being 36 days.

【21】7 cases were discharged home without any consequences， 1case was referred for plasmapheresis， and 1 case who developed femoral vein thrombosis was referred to a vascular surgeon， 1case was left against medical advice.

【22】Discussion

【23】Methemoglobinemia is the presence of disordered haemoglobin in the blood due to higher-than-normal levels of the ferrous form of iron. Methemoglobinemia can be congenital or acquired； congenital methemoglobinemia occurs due to genetic disorders leading to the prevention of Ferrous iron to ferric form in the haemoglobin. Acquired methemoglobinemia occurs as a result of exposure to oxidising agents. The standard compounds caus-ing this type include drugs like local anaesthetics like benzocaine and prilocaine， drugs containing nitrate compounds， dapsone and well-water high in nitrates. Toxic methemoglobinemia is a form of acquired methemoglobinemia due to exposure to oxi-dizing chemicals like certain insecticides， herbicides and plant alkaloids.

【24】The current study presents a series of cases due to exposure to plant growth enhancers. Plant growth enhancers are natural compounds extracted from a variety of algae and fungi. The exact composition of these compounds is not known. However， they contain Nitric oxide and other plant growth hormones； they act as oxidizing agents and convert ferrous iron to ferric iron in haemoglobin. The presence of ferric iron in haemoglobin leads to a conformational change to taut forms. As a result， congenital methemoglobinemia occurs mainly in infants， while toxic methemoglobinemia occurs at any age； the same is reflected in the current study， with the averageage being 45 and the lowest being 12， and the highest being 70.

【25】There are no gender differences， with equal distribution of males and females. Literature shows most of the cases presented as the result of therapeutic misadventure. In contrast， the current study has cases of intentional suicidal consumption of poisonous substances， which lead to the disease. 1 case in the study is due to accidental ingestion.

【26】Methemoglobinemia appears to develop almost immediately after compound consumption， as the average time gap between consumption and presentation was 2.5 hours. It can be identified even in cases presented as early as 1 hour. In all the previous studies from available data， the presentation was late， usually referred from other hospitals due to non-improvement. In the current study， the hospital being a rural tertiary care hospital， patients presented relatively early and directly. The exact time gap between exposure and methemoglobinemia development is difficult to identify.

【27】Breathlessness is the most common presentation in pa-tients presenting early after consumption， while irritability and cyanosis are observed in patients who presented to the hospital late.

【28】Previous studies have shown that cyanosis is the most com-mon symptom leading to suspicion of methemoglobinemia. Both symptoms indicate the blood's reduced oxygen-carrying capacity， leading to anaerobic metabolism. Other late signs and symptoms have been presented in table 1. Methemoglobinemia should be suspected in all patients with breathlessness， cyanosis and altered mental status after consuming a potentially poi-sonous substance.

【29】Moreover， 30% of patients required mechanical ventilation. In a study conducted in CMC， Vellore， out of the 5 patients， 2patients required mechanical ventilation. The presence of methe- moglobinemia per se did not lead to the requirement of mechan-ical ventilation. The presence of other factors like reduced GCS and oropharyngeal secretions compromising the airway are the main factors involved in deciding the requirement for mechani-cal ventilation. Mechanical ventilation in methemoglobinemia helps to maintain the airway. It does not help improve oxygena-tion or alter the disease process. Persistent hypoxia， even with100 % oxygen， is the indicator of methemoglobinemia. All the patients in the current study presented with saturation levels less than 85%， and saturation did not increase even after ade-quate oxygen supplementation. Patients who lately have low saturation levels at initial presentation had a poor prognosis and increased need for exchange transfusion. Patients who pre-sented to the emergency with low GCS  and cyanosis have a poor prognosis. This can be explained by prolonged anaerobic metabolism and by-products damaging the tissues. The longer the duration of anaerobic metabolism， the greater the end-organ damage.

【34】All patients were given methylene blue in the current study.30% of patients required a second dose of methylene blue， and20% required an exchange transfusion； one patient was referred for plasmapheresis， another for the need of a vascular surgeon， and one patient who did not have cyanosis was discharged. Methylene blue is the antidote of choice. It acts rapidly and ef-fectively through the NADPH-method reductase pathway. The initial dose of methemoglobin is 1 mg/kg body weight infused in 5% dextrose over 1 hour. The effect can be seen almost im-mediately. If there is no effect， a repeat dose of 0.5 mg/kg body weight can be given. It reduces ferric iron to ferrous iron and converts methemoglobin to functional haemoglobin. Other treat-ment modalities when methemoglobin is unavailable include high doses of ascorbic acid， exchange transfusion， plasmaphere-sis and hyperbaric oxygen therapy. Ascorbic acid is an effec- tive alternative， especially in cases with GPD deficiency where hemolysis is a serious complication with methylene blue.

【35】Both methemoglobinemia and its antidote， methylene blue， can induce hemolysis. However， it appears to be a rare compli-cation. Only one patient had hemolytic complications.

【36】Hepatic markers were normal in all cases， and renal function tests were also observed normally in 80% of cases， and in 20% of cases， urea was elevated in whom the consumption compound was urea and isoflavones.

【37】Conclusion

【38】Methemoglobinemia is a potential complication of ingesting her-bicides， plant growth extracts and alkaloid compounds. The presence of breathlessness， cyanosis， and persistent hypoxemia should raise suspicion of the disorder. Early institution of eas-ily available antidote methylene blue can save lives and avert potential complications. Every emergency physician should be aware of this condition and be ready to identify and treat it immediately.

【0】ABSTRACT Normal anatomical variations in the oral cavity involving blood vessels may pose an emergency for dentists. Oral procedures resulting in iatrogenic trauma are common， especially in educational settings. We present a case of an elderly male patient who reported for fabrication of a complete denture prosthesis. Routine clinical examination revealed the presence of large， dilated， tortuous， blue/ purple coloured， bilaterally distributed varicose veins on the undersurface of the tongue. Lesion blanched on the application of pressure. The complete denture fabrication was done after consultation with a physician who instructed to be careful while performing dental procedures. Sharp edges of instruments， materials and procedures were avoided during the fabrication of the prosthesis. A complete denture with balanced occlusion was fabricated and delivered to the patient， who reported being satisfied with the outcome of the denture.

【1】KEYWORDS varicose vein， hypertension， aging， ranula， internal haemorrhage

【2】Introduction

【3】The tongue is a strong muscular organ， the strength of which is perhaps the most influencing factor in the successful outcome of a complete denture prosthesis. Recent advances in ageing biol-ogy implicate that the prosthodontist needs to understand oral changes associated with ageing to handle them properly. Venous drainage of the tongue is primarily done by ranine or profunda V1S veins (vena comitans of the hypoglossal nerve). They usually begin at the tongue tip and run posteriorly under the mucous membrane joining the lingual vein or pass backwards on the hypoglossus vein draining ultimately into the common facial vein.  When a vein elsewhere in the body is swollen， enlarged， twisted is making the vessel visible； it is called a varicose vein. In the oral cavity， oral venous varix is a common and routine finding of an acquired vascular malformation. According to World Health Organization (WHO) in 1980，  it is a normal variation and represents a physiological process， therefore， re-ferred to as a condition. The condition has been presented under many names in the past that include Caviar tongue， phlebectasia linguae， lingual and sublingual varicosities.  Presently， it is called oral varix (varices) since they can occur in any region of the oral cavity with a predisposition to the ventral surface of the tongue.

【4】Believed to be a developmental anomaly， its prevalence in-creases with age， and its clinical significance is that the condition has been linked with several medical diseases， which makes it mandatory for prosthodontists to identify the condition before proceeding for prosthetic treatment. In addition， trauma due to a sharp denture is a potential possibility， however rare. This article presents a case report of an elderly patient seeking com-plete denture treatment who was found to have oral varix on the tongue and other areas.

【5】Case report

【6】An elderly male patient aged 68 years reported to the under-graduate clinic of the Department of Prosthodontics with a chief complaint of inability to chew due to the state of com-plete edentulism. The patients medical， social and drug history were noncontributory to his existing condition and patiently did not disclose any sign or symptom of regular systemic disorders. Dental history disclosed patient got most of his teeth extracted since they were mobile， and few had decayed in the earlier part of his life. Recent extractions were that of anterior maxillary teeth， which were removed eight months back. The sequence of edentulism in the ascending order was mandibular posterior followed by maxillary posteriors and then mandibular anteri-ors. The extraoral examination did not disclose any negative findings.

【7】Intraoral examination revealed a well-formed maxillary resid-ual alveolar ridge (RAR) while mandibular RAR was severely re-sorbed. Examination of the ventral surface of the tongue showed the presence of large， dilated， tortuous， blue/ purple coloured， bilaterally distributed varicose veins that started from the tip of the tongue and continued till the posterior part of the tongue . Isolated round and superficial venous varicosities were also observed on the right lateral tongue border ， the lingual vestibule  and buccal mucosa . All the lesions on palpation felt soft， depressible， and painless that blanched on finger pressure. General examination of the patient showed similar varicose veins in the lower legs and hands. However， the patient could not recall whether his parents or anyone in the family had similar conditions. Complete denture rehabilitation was initiated after taking an opinion from a general physician. The physician ruled out any underlying cardiovascular disease， portal hypertension or chronic venous insufficiency. Routine clinical and laboratory procedures were used to fabricate the complete denture prosthesis with special care taken to prevent physical or chemical injury to the oral mucosa during routine use of dental techniques and dental materials.

【8】Discussion

【9】Oral varices should be differentiated from melanotic or pur-puric lesions like hereditary haemorrhagic telangiectasia (do not change colouration on pressure)， hemangiomas， lymphangioma UrV and Kaposi sarcoma by a thorough history and detailed clinical evaluation. differentiation is easily done with proper history， location and the clinical picture. Vascular malformations (VM) are congenital that is present at birth， growing proportionately with children age. Therefore， they are distinguished quickly based on the time of onset of the condition.  Oral varices have been linked to cardiopulmonary diseases，and intense cyanotic emphysemas。 however， many studies have denied its association The broad consensus is only on its higher incidence in old age， but not so with its etiopathogenesis that links cardiovascular problems being the cause. Three its link-age to portal hypertension has been reported by Jassar et al.， but in medical literature， no recognized anastomosis between lingual venous drainage and portal circulation exists. In ad-dition， the incidence of OV has been discussed in relation to nutritional disorders like vitamin C deficiency， superior vena cave syndrome and chronic hepatitis 3 with no clear evidence to support the association.

【10】For a prosthodontist and every general dentist， one needs to be aware of the condition and special care in handling sharp objects like syringe needles， surgical blades， denture borders and chemical agents used in the oral cavity during routine den-tal procedures observed. Special care is required if the lesion is at a place where the denture will rest since denture move-ment may lacerate the mucosa and puncture the vein. Generally， oral varices need no treatment except educating and reassuring the patient about their benign existence. Treatment is consid-ered only if they are present at worksites (like buccal vestibule， residual alveolar ridge borders) or if and when they are aes-thetically objectionable. Treatment modalities include surgery(cryosurgery， Electrosurgery， laser therapy)， Sclerotherapy and coagulation therapy.

【11】Conclusion

【12】The present view on oral varices is that it is associated with aging， and future research is needed to explain its association with systemic diseases. However， its high prevalence in the elderly population makes the prosthodontist a likely candidate to look out for its presence during a clinical examination.

【0】ABSTRACT Chronic myeloid leukaemia (CML) is a myeloproliferative neoplasm characterized by Philadelphia chromo-some with excessive tyrosine kinase activity leading to uncontrolled proliferation of mature and maturing granulocytes， predominantly neutrophils. If left untreated CML goes though chronic phase， accelerated phase and ultimately blast crises. Accelerated phase is characterized by features of disease progression without meeting criteria for chronic phase or blast crises. We present a case of young male with CML， who presented with acute bilateral proptosis and rapidly rising white cell count. On work up he was found to have progressed to accelerated phase of CML on the basis of rapidly rising WCC and clonal evolution with new cytogenetic finding of 3q deletion in Philadelphia positive cells. He was treated with high dose Cytarabine with complete resolution of proptosis and hematologic remission.

【1】KEYWORDS CML， Clonal Evolution， Accelerated Phase

【2】Introduction

【3】Chronic myeloid leukaemia (CML) is a myeloproliferative neo-plasm characterized by rearrangement of the long arms of chro-mosome 9 and 22， resulting in Philadelphia Chromosome， creat-ing the fusion oncogene BCR-ABL . There are three distinct phases of CML， namely chronic，accelerated， and blast phase. The transition from chronic phase of CML to the accelerated phase followed by the blast phase may take a vear or more， or it may appear abruptly leading to blast crisis with an annual rate of progression from chronic phase to blast crisis of 5-10%in the first two years and 20% in subsequent years . Clinical features indicating progression include progressive leukocytosis， thrombocytosis or thrombocytopenia， anaemia， progressive or painful splenomegaly or hepatomegaly， fever， bone pain or de structive bone lesions， thrombotic or bleeding complications . Eye involvement is uncommon with CML in any phase. How-ever， when present， it can vary from incidental finding during an eye examination to blurred vision and partial or total loss of vision . Criteria meeting progression of chronic phase to accelerated phase and blast crisis are well defined by ELN and WHO . Prognosis is much worse， and hence treatment rec-ommendations for accelerated phase CML include appropriate tyrosine kinase inhibitor AML type intensive chemotherapy and allogeneic hematopoietic progenitor cell transplantation (HPCT).

【4】Case report

【5】We present a case of 39 years old male who developed se-vere orbitopathy while receiving Nilotinib for Chronic Myeloid Leukaemia (CML). He was diagnosed with CML just over two years ago. Bone marrow biopsy at diagnosis was consistent with CML in chronic phase with cytogenetics confirming pres-ence of Philadelphia Chromosome and BCR/ABL1 by FISH and PCR. His Sokal score was 1.6. He was initially treated with Ima-tinib 400 mg once daily. By three months， he was in complete hematologic response and by six months partial cytogenetic re-sponse with BCR-ABL1 ratio of 6.4%. Imatinib was increased to 400mg twice daily， but over the ensuing months， he could only maintain complete hematologic response without achiev-ing complete cytogenetic or major molecular response. He was switched over to Nilotinib 400 mg twice daily. After six months of being on Nilotinib， he presented with a one-week history of fever， headache and marked proptosis of both eyes with the blurring of vision. He had the conjunctival injection， chemosis and periorbital oedema with no eye movement. He had bilat-eral cervical and axillary lymphadenopathy and splenomegaly. Thyroid was not enlarged. His WCC was significantly raised to128x10//ul with predominant neutrophilia， monocytosis and basophilia. An urgent MRI scan of brain and orbits  revealed extensive hypertrophy and oedema of the extraocular muscles sparing tendons with no involvement of optic nerves. Thyroid profile was normal， but TSH-receptor antibodies came back positive at 6.06 U/L (normal <1U/L). The differential di-agnoses considered included TSH receptor antibody-mediated Graves' ophthalmopathy， orbitopathy secondary to Nilotinib or CML with infiltration of extraocular muscles. As an emer-gency， Nilotinib was stopped， and he was commenced on ⅣMethylprednisolone and Hydroxycarbamide 3 grams daily. Af-ter a good transient response in orbital oedema， redness and eye movement along with a reduction in WCC， his proptosis， however， worsened upon steroid wean  and WCC shot up to 297x10/ul within two weeks. Bone marrow biopsy showed 1% blasts with an increase in BCR-ABL1 ratio by PCR to 47%， and Cytogenetics revealed a new paracentric inversion of chromosome 3g along with BCR-ABL translocation. Based on rapidly rising white cell counts and clonal evolution with a new inversion in chromosome 3q， he was diagnosed to have progressed to accelerated phase of CML. High dose Cytarabine was administered with excellent clinical response evidenced byc Vis1omplete resolution of proptosis， diplopia and visual loss . WCC also normalized. He is currently post-second cycle of AML -type intensive chemotherapy and has an HLA-matched sibling with plans for an allogeneic Hematopoietic progenitor cell transplant.

【6】Discussion

【7】In summary， our patient is known for CML， poorly responsive to TKIs， presented with bilateral proptosis and rising leukocyte counts， and diagnosed to have accelerated phase on finding new inversion in chromosome 3q. On treatment with high dose Cytarabine， he went in to complete remission hematologically along with the clinical resolution of orbitopathy. Bilateral prop-tosis， though less commonly encountered in the accelerated phase of CML or blast crises， should prompt the clinicians to look for disease progression when presenting along with rising leukocyte counts and failed response to treatment. Although ocular complications of CML and Tyrosine Kinase inhibitors， particularly Imatinib are， reported， acute proptosis with oph-thalmoplegia is very rare. Nilotinib has not been reported to cause Graves Ophthalmopathy， but thyrotoxicosis and other au-toimmune disorders have been reported with CML and Tyrosine Kinase inhibitors. The diagnostic challenge in our patient was whether his orbitopathy was due to Graves'disease or Nilotinib or secondary to progression of CML to accelerated phase with infiltration of extraocular muscles. Presence of TSH-receptor an-tibody makes Graves'Ophthalmopathy an important differential diagnosis along with the progression of CML with infiltration of extra-ocular muscles. Treatment targeting these possibilities needs to be commenced early to avoid permanent visual loss. In our patient， because of rapid response to AML-type intensive chemotherapy， his proptosis and ophthalmoplegia were thought to be more likely due to accelerated phase CML rather than Nilotinib related orbitopathy or Graves' disease.

【0】Background：

【1】Endometriosis is a common gynecological disorder occurring in around 10% of women of reproductive age. Inguinal endometriosis is a rare condition； however， it should be considered in the differential for inguinal masses in women of reproductive age. Usually， it occurs after implantation of endometrial tissue during previ-ous surgical procedures. Patients with inguinal endometriosis are often multiparous women with a history of previous gynecological or obstetric surgery. It represents a diagnostic dilemma， as it is often misdiagnosed as other inguinal pathologies.

【2】Case Report： Herein， we report a case of a 33-year-old nulliparous woman with left groin pain for 2 years increasing in the severity during menstruation. A physical examination revealed a 1.5-cm left inguinal mass. Ultrasound showed an ill-defined speculated solid hypoechoic left inguinal mass measuring 1.6x1.4 cm. Computed tomography(CT) of the pelvis revealed a left inguinal mass measuring 1.7x1.2 cm， demonstrating central hypo-attenuation with thickening of the round ligament. Exploration of the inguinal region revealed an adherent mass to the round ligament and floor of the canal， which was excised completely with a safety margin. The inguinal canal floor was strengthened using proline mesh. Histopathological examination of the mass confirmed the diagno-sis of left inguinal endometriosis.

【3】Conclusions： Inguinal endometriosis is a rare clinical entity mimicking other common inguinal conditions. A high index of suspicion is crucial for its preoperative diagnosis， especially in the presence of an inguinal mass associated with cyclic changes in size and pain severity. Its standard management is surgical excision.

【4】Keywords： Chronic Pain·Endometriosis · Hernia， Inguinal·Menstruation· Parity Endometriosis is a common gynecological disorder， with an es-timated incidence of 10% in women of reproductive age . It typically involves intra-pelvic organs and peritoneum， but can also affect any extra-pelvic organs . It commonly occurs af-ter implantation of endometrial tissue during previous pelvic surgical procedures .

【5】Inguinal endometriosis is a rare clinical entity that was first reported in 1896 by Cullen. Its incidence is not estimated，as there are only around 50 cases reported in the literature. It represents a diagnostic dilemma as it is often misdiagnosed as other inguinal pathologies such as inguinal hernia， soft tis-sue tumors， and inguinal lymphadenopathy . Most of the reported cases are managed surgically without preoperative imaging or biopsy . Herein， we report a case of left ingui-nal endometriosis in a virgin nulliparous middle-age woman with no previous gynecological procedures， mimicking an in-guinal hernia.

【6】Case Report

【7】A 33-year-old nulliparous woman reported having left groin pain radiating to the left thigh and aggravated by menstrua-tion that lasted for 2 years prior to her presentation. She had regular menstrual cycles and denied any gynecological symp-toms suggestive of endometriosis such as dysmenorrhea or dyspareunia. She was otherwise healthy with no previous ab-dominal or pelvic surgeries or any gynecological interventions. She never received hormonal therapy or contraception and she was not on any regular medications. Upon physical examina-tion， she had a 1.5-cm left inguinal mass， tender on palpa-tion and adherent to the underlying tissue. Ultrasonography of the abdomen and pelvis showed an ill-defined speculated solid hypoechoic left inguinal mass measuring 1.6x1.4 cm in diameter. The uterus and ovaries were within normal limits. Computed tomography (CT) of the pelvis revealed a central hypo-attenuation left inguinal mass measuring 1.7x1.2 cm in diameter and thickening of the left round ligament . There were no other identified lesions， or suspicion for endo-metriosis， malignancy， or inguinal lymphadenopathy. Based on the presentation， examination， and imaging， left inguinal her-nia was one of our differential diagnoses.

【8】The patient underwent left inguinal canal exploration that re-vealed a 1.5-cm mass adherent to the round ligament and floor of the canal. The mass was excised completely with a0.5-cm safety margin. The inguinal canal floor was repaired and strengthened with proline mesh. The patient tolerated the procedure well and was discharged in good condition.

【9】The mass was sent for histopathological examination. Macroscopically， the excised mass was 3.5x3x1.5 cm in size， and consisted of fibrous tissue， with a cut section showing hemorrhagic areas. Histopathological examination showed multiple foci of endometrial glands surrounded by endome-trial stroma embedded within the fibrous tissue . Postoperatively， the patient was followed up in surgery and gynecology out-patient clinics. She had no recurrences. There was no need for further imaging or postoperative hormonal therapy according to the consultant gynecologist.

【10】Discussion

【11】Endometriosis is characterized by the presence of normal endo-metrial tissue including glands and stroma at sites other than the uterine cavity. The ovaries are the most commonly affected organ， accounting for 96% of cases. Extra-pelvic endometrio-sis is much less commonly seen but can involve any organ .

【12】Patients with inguinal endometriosis are often multiparous women with a history of previous gynecological or obstet-ric surgery . We performed an extensive review of the English literature using the search terms "inguinal endome-triosis"， “groin endometriosis"and/or “extra-pelvic endome-triosis" in the title， abstract， and/or keywords of articles in-dexed in the Medline， Scopus， and Google Scholar databases， which is summarized in Table 1. Only 29 cases of inguinal en-dometriosis have been reported in nulliparous women simi-lar to our case .

【13】Patients usually present with a palpable inguinal swelling that is often associated with cyclic pain and change in size. Cyclic exacerbation of symptoms is a typical feature for endometri-osis that is often missed during the initial assessment . A history of dysmenorrhea， dyspareunia， and infertility may also be present， indicating concomitant pelvic endometrio-sis . However， most patients， including this case， have regular menstrual cycles， which can be a misleading point in the clinical assessment . Inguinal endometriosis is more common on the right side. This is believed to be associated with the presence of the sigmoid， which places pressure on the left inguinal area， acting as a preventive measure . Our patient had left-sided inguinal endometriosis， which is less common， as only 13 cases in the literature review were re-ported on the left side .

【14】Inguinal endometriosis mimics a wide variety of inguinal con-ditions such as inguinal hernia， hemangioma，lymphadenopa-thy， and hydrocele of canal of Nuck . The preoperative di-agnosis of inguinal endometriosis is difficult owing to its rarity and inconclusive imaging findings. In the literature， there is no comparative study assessing the efficacy of different imaging modalities in such cases. On ultrasonography， inguinal endo-metriosis often shows a hypoechoic unilocular or multilocular cyst that is difficult to distinguish from other inguinal region pathologies such as lymph nodes and simple cysts .

【15】CT may not be helpful in confirming the diagnosis of ingui-nal endometriosis， but it can be used to exclude other possi-ble differentials diagnoses . However， it did not confirm the diagnosis of -inguinal endometriosis in this case. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRl) is the most specific and sensitive im-aging modality for the diagnosis of endometriosis in gener-al. MRI can detect iron particles in the hemosiderin present in the endometrioma， making it a better tool for diagnosing en-dometriosis than the other modalities . The typical ap-pearance ofinguinal endometriosis is similar to pelvic endome-triosis on MRI， showing high intensity on T1-weighted images and hypointensity on T2-weighted images . However， the majority of reported cases in the literature have reported inconclusive MRI results for diagnosing inguinal endometriosis. The MRI findings were commonly atypical and non-specific for endometriosis； therefore， the diagnosis of inguinal endome-triosis cannot be established . A case series involving 20patients diagnosed with inguinal endometriosis showed that the majority of patients have a mixed hyper- and hypointen-sity of both T1- and T2-weighted images (61.1% and 50%，re-spectively) .

【16】Preoperative fine-needle aspiration cytology (FNAC) is diagnos-tic for endometriosis . However， it is rarely performed， as most patients are treated surgically with a preoperative di-agnosis of incarcerated inguinal hernia or other inguinal pa-thologies. The final diagnosis is confirmed by histopathological examination of the excised mass showing endometrial glands and stroma . In our patient， CT findings did not suggest endometriosis， and an inguinal hernia was still one of the dif-ferential diagnoses. Therefore， preoperative FNAC was not done， as it could have injured the contents of the hernial sac.

【17】It is common for patients with inguinal endometriosis to have co-existing inguinal hernia or hydrocele of canal of Nuck. The management of both conditions is surgical . The surgical management for inguinal endometriosis requires rad-ical excision to decrease the rate of recurrence . However， most patients are managed surgically before being diagnosed with endometriosis； therefore， the radical surgical resection is not done in most cases without evidence of recurrence on follow-up.

【18】Patients with inguinal endometriosis often have concomitant pelvic endometriosis. It is recommended to refer patients for complete gynecological assessment postoperatively . Laparoscopic evaluation of pelvic endometriosis in patients with inguinal endometriosis is recommended if there is clin-ical evidence of pelvic endometriosis such as dysmenorrhea， dyspareunia， or infertility . The use of hormon-al therapy for inguinal endometriosis is controversial. Its role is more prominent in patients with concomitant pelvic endo-metriosis. It is sometimes recommended in patients with in-guinal endometriosis as an adjuvant therapy after surgical in-tervention to decrease the risk of reoccurrence . In our case， the patient did not have any clinical evidence of pelvic endometriosis， so she was only given follow-ups with gynecology without the need for diagnostic laparoscopy and hormonal therapy.

【38】Conclusions

【39】Inguinal endometriosis is a rare clinical entity mimicking oth-er common inguinal conditions. A high index of suspicion is crucial for its preoperative diagnosis， especially in the presence of an inguinal mass associated with cyclic changes in size and pain severity. FNAC is diagnostic but rarely performed. FNAC for a patient in whom there is a high suspicion of inguinal hernia can injure the contents of the hernia sac. Its standard management is surgical excision. Gynecological assessment is needed pre- and postoperatively to exclude the presence of pelvic endometriosis.

【0】Background：

【1】Ehlers-Danlos syndrome， hypermobility type is characterized by increased extensibility， permeability， and fra-gility of the affected cartilaginous tissues， including the trachea， larynx， and skin. Anesthetic considerations for patients with this syndrome include intubation difficulties secondary to the collapse of fibro-elastic tissues in the trachea and a reported resistance to local anesthetics.

【2】Case Report：

【3】Our patient was a 22-year-old G4P0030 woman with a history of morbid obesity， seizures， Barrett’s esophagus， hypermobility being evaluated for Ehlers-Danlos syndrome， and anaphylaxis to an unknown local anesthetic who was scheduled for cesarean delivery. She refused allergy testing After rapid-sequence induction of gen-eral anesthesia， video laryngoscopy facilitated endotracheal intubation. Delivery and recovery were uneventful for the mother and child.

【4】Conclusions： No guidelines for neuraxial or general anesthesia exist for patients with Ehlers-Danlos syndrome， hypermobility type. Increased rates of cervical spine instability and local anesthetic resistance have been reported in this pop-ulation and should be considered when developing the anesthetic plan.

【5】MeSH Keywords： Anesthesia， Local ·Anesthesia， Obstetrical·Ehlers-Danlos Syndrome Ehlers-Danlos syndrome (EDS) is group of connective tissue disorders characterized by mutations in the genes encoding fibrillar collagen or enzymes related to the post-translational modification of collagen . This results in increased exten-sibility， permeability， and fragility of the effected tissues. Beighton et al.  described diagnostic criteria for six distinct EDS subtypes based on the spectrum of tissue involvement； of these， the hypermobility subtype (EDS-HT) is the most com-mon. EDS-HT is defined by skin hyperextensibility and gener-alized joint hypermobility (major criteria)， as well as recurring joint dislocations， chronic joint pain， and a positive family his-tory (minor criteria). A heritable， autosomal dominant colla-gen gene mutation has been implicated in the pathogenesis of EDS-HT . Although the specific gene responsible for this subtype is unknown， it appears to affect the cartilaginous tis-sues of the trachea， larynx， and skin. As such， the syndrome presents a unique set of anesthetic challenges. Intubation dif-ficulties can arise secondary to the collapse of fibro-elastic tis-sues in the trachea. Additional issues relevant to anesthetic care include difficu lt vascular access and positioning secondary to skin hyperextensibility and fragility， as well as a reported resistance to local anesthetics .

【6】Although EDS is relatively common， with an incidence of approx-imately 1 in 5000， no specific recommendations for anesthetic management exist . Some sources advocate the avoidance of neuraxial anesthesia for obstetric patients with EDS due to risk of local anesthetic resistance， but successful cases have been reported . This case report presents the effective anesthetic management of an obstetric patient presumed to have EDS-HT in addition to a local anesthetic allergy. The pa-tient has provided written consent to publish this case report.

【7】Case Report

【8】A 22-year-old G4P0030 woman with a history of morbid obesity(BMI 39)， seizures， Barrett’s esophagus， joint hypermobility， and anaphylaxis to an unknown local anesthetic was sched-uled for elective cesarean delivery at 39 weeks gestation at Penn State Health Milton S. Hershey Medical Center. Upon fur-ther questioning during her pre-operative appointment， she could only recall that she “stopped breathing" following ad-ministration of local anesthetic for a dental procedure， and she had never received local anesthetic since that time. Her hypermobility syndrome was being evaluated for EDS-HT； her family history was positive for a sister with EDS-HT. The pa-tient's history was also significant for postural hypotension， chronic pain， heroin addiction， bipolar disorder， and difficult intravenous (Ⅳ) access.

【9】After discussion of the risks and benefits of formal allergy testing prior to delivery， the patient ultimately refused this procedure. The risks of general endotracheal anesthesia for cesarean delivery and her comorbidities were discussed， and the patient provided informed consent.

【10】EDS-HT placed her at increased risk for intubation difficul-ties secondary to potential cervical spine hypermobility or instability， collapse of the fibro-elastic tissues and cartilagi-nous rings of the trachea with minimal pressure， TMJ dysfunc-tion， and spontaneous pneumothorax. Awake fiberoptic intu-bation was considered and discussed given these risks， but would have been extremely challenging without local anes-thetic， and the patient refused. Pre-operative evaluation re-vealed ASA class III， Mallampati class Il， right non-tender jaw click， and a supple neck with normal range of motion including flexion and extension.

【11】General anesthesia was induced with the lV administration of propofol (250 mg) and succinylcholine (200 mg). Intubation was performed using video laryngoscopy (GlideScope) assisted by cricoid pressure. Neutral neck position was maintained throughout the induction and intubation processes. Following endotracheal intubation， anesthesia was maintained with ni-trous oxide and sevoflurane (minimum alveolar concentration0.9). A healthy male infant was delivered shortly thereafter. Intraoperatively， the patient received fentanyl (75 mcg)， ket-amine (50 mg)， morphine (10 mg)， and ketorolac (30 mg)V for multimodal analgesia. I midazolam (2 mg) was also given to decrease the risk of distressing hallucinations secondary to ketamine. Rocuronium (10 mg) was used to maintain neuro-muscular blockade， which was reversed with glycopyrrolate(0.6 mg) and neostigmine (3 mg) Ⅳ. During the procedure， phenylephrine (200 mcg) was administered for transient hy potension. She also received dexamethasone and ondansetron(4 mg each) lV for post-operative nausea and vomiting pro-phylaxis. I oxytocin (40 units) was given to improve uterine tone. Estimated blood loss was 800 mL. The patient was extu-bated and transported to the post-anesthesia care unit， where she recovered uneventfully.

【12】Discussion

【13】Pregnancy places EDS-HT patients at increased risk for obstetric complications related to increased stress on abnormal connec-tive tissues. Augmented laxity of the joints， skin， and other connective tissues at baseline is worsened by the increased weight of pregnancy； this can lead to nerve impingement sec-ondary to hypermobile facet joints of the spine， separation of the pubis symphysis during labor， or pre-term delivery sec-ondary to an incompetent cervix . Uterine prolapse also occurs with higher frequency in EDS-HT patients during the post-partum period . Dysautonomia in the form of postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome (POTS) is particularly com-mon in EDS-HT patients. Orthostatic hypotension usually occurs secondary to abnormal aortic baroreceptor responses and can cause dizziness， nausea， palpitations， fatigue， and tachycardia. During labor， these symptoms are worsened by pain and stress. Additionally，neuraxial anesthesia necessarily results in periph-eral vasodilation and hypotension， thus worsening the dysau-tonomia and furthering hemodynamic instability . Despite these potential complications， pregnancy and delivery appear to be relatively safe in EDS-HT patients compared to patients with other forms of EDS .

【14】Endotracheal intubation can be challenging in EDS-HT pa-tients. Difficulties can arise secondary to collapse of the tra-cheal cartilage or joint hypermobility with respect to the cer-vical spine instability， and TMJ dysfunction in particular. The application of cricoid pressure in the backward， upward， and rightward directions is frequently used during direct laryngos-copy to aid in visualization of the vocal cords. In a patient with EDS-HT， however， even a minimal amount of pressure may oc-clude the trachea and further obscure the view. Mechanically ventilated EDS-HT patients are at higher risk of orolaryngeal hematomas and spontaneous pneumothoraxes secondary to increased airway pressures . Cervical spine examination with flexion and extension x-rays are generally sufficient to rule out instability. When available， this can facilitate intuba-tion by allowing for normal manipulation of the cervical spine rather than a requirement to maintain a neutral spine position throughout the process. Patients predisposed to ligamentous laxity， such those with EDS-HT， are at increased risk of TMJ dislocation. TMJ dislocation can occur when the mandibular condyle prolapses anteriorly during the jaw thrust maneuver necessary for direct laryngoscopy. When the mouth is opened widey， the supportive ligaments are at their highest level of laxity . Generally， these complications can be minimized， but not eliminated， with the use of video laryngoscopy， intubating laryngeal mask airway devices， or fiberoptic bronchoscopes.

【15】In this case， general anesthesia was utilized instead of neur-axial anesthesia due to the patient's reported allergy to local anesthetics， as well as the reported potential for local anes-thetic failure in EDS-HT patients. Sood et al. found that this risk can be as high as 1 in 3 . Other studies have found that EDS-HT patients can obtain total analgesia from intradermal lidocaine injection， but the effects do not last as long as in patients without EDS-HT despite the use of epinephrine for vasoconstriction. The underlying mechanism for the shorter duration of local anesthetic effect could be swift removal of the anesthetic from the dermis， most likely via vascular up-take and leakage through highly permeable connective tis-sues. These patients frequently report a history of anxiety and pain secondary to inadequate analgesia during minor procedures . Hakim et al. asked a group of hypermobile patients the following question： “If you have ever had a local anesthetic injection (dentist/minor surgery/epidural)， did you think that it was as effective as it should have been?”Fifty-eight percent of patients answered in the negative compared to 21% of control subjects . Previous cases of successful local and neuraxial anesthetic use have been described，how-ever， and it appears that the success of these interventions varies greatly on a case-by-case basis . When neuraxial anesthesia is selected for patients with EDS， it is probably best to use either a combined spinal epidural or epidural catheter in order to allow for additional doses of local anesthetic to be administered in case of local anesthetic resistance.

【16】No specific guidelines or indications for specific general anes-thetic techniques exist with regard to patients with EDS-HT. Local anesthetics， volatile anesthetics， nitrous oxide， total in-travenous anesthesia， depolarizing agents， and non-depolar-izing agents are all assumed to be safe and effective unless an additional contraindication exists. Recommendations for local anesthesia are similarly lacking. Dolan et al. published“general recommendations for the anesthetic management of patients with Ehlers-Danlos syndrome” in 1980 ， but these were non-specific to the type of EDS involved. More recent updates， notably by Wiesmann et al. ， have made improve-ments， but do not provide details concerning pharmacologic options. In patients undergoing sub-umbilical surgeries， the combined spinal epidural technique， with the addition of mor-phine to bupivacaine， has been shown to enhance the efficacy of the neuraxial blockade and allow for fine titrations to a de-sired sensory level. Similarly， in elderly patients，adjuvants such as epinephrine and clonidine have been shown to pro-long the duration of spinal or regional blockade . It is pos-sible that similar strategies could be effective in EDS-HT pa-tients， but further studies are needed to explore these options.

【17】Conclusions

【18】No guidelines for neuraxial or general anesthesia exist for patients with Ehlers-Danlos syndrome， hypermobility type. Increased rates of cervical spine instability and local anesthetic resistance have been reported in this population and should be considered when developing the anesthetic plan. If a local an-esthetic resistance is identified， the combined spinal epidural technique and/or pharmacologic neuraxial adjuvants such as epinephrine and clonidine may provide an alternative solu-tion， but more research is needed to explore these options.

【0】Background：

【1】The formation of a saphenous vein graft aneurysm is an extremely rare event. It can cause the potential complications similar to arterial aneurysms， such as rupture， thrombosis， distal embolisation and ischemia leading to limb loss.

【2】Case report：

【3】We present a case ofa 76-year old man with multiple saccular aneurysms of the femoropopliteal saphenous vein graft， inserted 22 years ago. The echo-Doppler revealed aneurismal dilatations ranging from 2 to 3 cm in diameters， they had endoluminal thrombus. Angiography confirmed the diagnosis which revealed multiple aneurysmatic dilatations of the saphenous vein graft with severe generalized atherosclerotic changes in the remainder of the graft. At operation， the aneurysmatic saphenous vein graft was removed under spinal anesthesia and the arterial continuity reestablished with an inverted saphenous vein， taken from the contralateral limb. He was perfectly well at the follow-up after nine months.

【4】Conclusions：

【5】Venous graft aneurysms should be removed to prevent possible complications， and the arterial continuity reestablished with a contralateral saphenous vein or synthetic graft. Lifelong follow-up is mandatory following surgery.

【6】Key words： Venous aneurysm· saphenous vein graft

【7】Long saphenous vein is the preferred conduit for an infrainguinal below-knee arterial bypass. The formation of a saphenous vein graft aneurysm is an extremely rare event but known complication after femoropopliteal bypass surgery and is mainly due to atherosclerotic degeneration .

【8】In this report， we describe the case of a patient with multiple aneurysms formed in a saphenous vein bypass graft， 22 years after the initial operation.

【9】CASE REPORT

【10】We present a case of a 76-year old man with multiple saccular aneurysms of the femoropopliteal saphenous vein graft， inserted 22 years ago. At another hospital he underwent femoropopliteal bypass operation. During the next 22 years， he had enjoyed excellent healt. In February 2004， while taking a bath， he unexpectedly noticed abnormal subcutaneous swellings in the left thigh. On admittance to our service， he reported having difficulty in walking at 100 meters because of a pain in the left leg. He has been receiving hypertension treatment for 28 years， 48 years of smoking one pack of cigarettes per day， and a family history of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease in history.

【11】On physical examination， his blood pressure was150/90 mmHg， with a regular pulse of 80/min. Heart sounds were normal. Subcutaneous pulsatile masses over the left median thigh were palpated. Laboratory data included a hematocrit value of 46%， blood glucose level of 199 mg/dl， serum creatinin value of 1，20 mg/dl， and total cholesterol level of 239mg/dl. The patient underwent echo-Doppler and angiography. The echo-Doppler revealed aneurismal dilatations ranging from 2 to 3 cm in diameters in the vein graft. Angiography confirmed the diagnosis which revealed multiple aneurysmatic dilatations of the saphenous vein graft with severe generalized atherosclerotic changes in the remainder of the graft.

【12】At operation， the aneurysmatic saphenous vein graft was removed under spinal anesthesia and the arterial continuity reestablished with an inverted saphenous vein， taken from the contralateral limb(saphenous vein graft was tunneled subfascially and anastomosed to the superficial femoral artery proximally and the popliteal artery distally). The patient made good recovery postoperatively and had good peripheral pulses. The histological examination revealed absence of the elastic tissue， collections of cholesterol cleft and lipid laden macrophages. In microbiological cultures， none of the common pathologic microorganisms grew.

【13】At follow-up nine months after surgery， he was in good health and control echo-Doppler showed a patent saphenous vein graft of normal caliber.

【14】DISCUSSION

【15】Saphenous vein has remained the preferred conduit for femoropopliteal bypass grafting since Holden reported its use in atherosclerotic disease .Over the past 40 years autologous saphenous vein bypass grafts have come into widespread use for many arterial districts， because they provide an exceedingly effective arterial substitute even in the long term .

【16】Aneurysm of saphenous vein graft has been classified as true aneurysm and pseudoaneurysm. Pseudo-aneurysm formation is usually related to disruption of the proximal or distal suture line due to technical failure or infectious processes 31. True venous aneurysms can be defined as abnormal saccular dilatations of veins characterized histologically by an increase in fibrous connective tissue in the vein wall. Although large numbers of patients have undergone coronary or peripheral vascular surgery using saphenous vein grafts， there is only a small number of case reports of aneurismal dilatation in these conduits .

【17】True aneurysm in a vein graft was first described by Davidson in 1972 . The cause of true aneurysms of venous graft is still unclear . The etiology of aneurismal changes in vein grafts has been reported by some authors to be related to the development of atherosclerosis . Such process leads to weakening of the vessel wall owing to the destruction of the elastic and connective tissue elements of the media and adventia. However， Taurino et al  reported a case without atherosclerotic degeneration. Saphenous veins exposed to the arterial circulation develop arterialization of the walls， and thus in the presence of other risk factors may become aneurismal. Atherosclerosis， smoking， low-grade infection(mycotic aneurysm)， hyperlipidemia should be considered as etiological factors. It has been suggested that graft aneurysm may be the manifestation of a systemic dilating process .

【18】Saphenous vein graft aneurysms have the potential complications similar to arterial aneurysms， such as rupture， thrombosis， distal embolisation and ischemia leading to limb loss. Additionally， they may cause skin ulceration.

【19】Histological features in a vein graft include endothelial disruption and subendothelial transformations such as medial necrosis， loss of elastic elements， cholesterol de-posits and fibrous proliferation . Elastase activity and the integrity of elastic tissue in the arterial wall may play a role in the development of atherosclerotic aneurysms.The loss of elastic tissue seen in our patient’s vein graft may have predisposed to the development of aneurismal change similar to Cloud et al report .

【20】Peer et al  suggested synthetic graft to avoid the long-term sequelae of aneurysm formation in patients with hypercholesterolemia. In their report hypercholesterolemia and hypertriglyceridemia were common denominators as well as cigarette smoking while hypertension was not a significant element.

【21】CONCLUSIONS

【22】Venous graft aneurysms should be removed to prevent possible complications， and the arterial continuity reestablished with a contralateral saphenous vein or synthetic graft. Careful follow-up of all treated graft aneurysms throughout the patient’s life is mandatory6，111.

【0】Background： Late cerebral metastasis more than 10 years after the diagnosis of cutaneous melanoma is very rare. This re-port is of a woman with late cerebral metastasis 16 years after an initial diagnosis of cutaneous melanoma.

【1】Case Report：

【2】A 41-year-old woman had been diagnosed with malignant melanoma 16 years prior from a biopsy of a dish-pattern tumor on the back， for which she received chemotherapy for 5 times (therapeutic regimen and med-ications were not available). She had not had a diagnosis of skin melanoma in the past 16 years. Before pre-sentation to the Emergency Department， she had a progressive disturbance of consciousness for 6 weeks and sudden coma for 6 h. A head computed tomography scan indicated intracranial masses located at the right frontal and temporal lobes. The patient underwent surgery for tumor and hematoma removal. During surgery dural metastasis with widespread dissemination in adjacent temporal bone，temporalis， and hypodermis was confirmed. Postoperative histopathology analysis confirmed the diagnosis of malignant melanoma metastasis. On the second day after surgery， the patient developed recurrent bleeding in the right frontal lobe， which led to deteriorated consciousness. She received hematoma evacuation and craniectomy and lived in a poor con-dition with drowsiness and hemiplegia of the left limb for 3 months and died 5 months after craniectomy.

【3】Conclusions： This report has presented a rare occurrence of late cerebral metastasis 16 years after the initial diagnosis of a primary cutaneous melanoma. More recent primary melanoma of the skin was not identified， which supports the need for long-term follow-up of patients with a history of primary cutaneous melanoma.

【4】Keywords： Intracranial Hemorrhages· Melanoma·Neoplasm Metastasis·Coma Melanoma is the third most common source of brain metasta-ses， following lung and breast cancers ， and has one of the highest tendencies to develop brain metastases， with a prev-alence of nearly 45% in patients with stage l melanoma and75% upon autopsy . For most patients newly diagnosed with melanomas， wide excision， sentinel lymph node biopsy， and additional treatment of regional or distant metastatic dis-ease are essential procedures according to the updated National Comprehensive Cancer Network (NCCN) guidelines for melano-ma . Regular clinical follow-up is recommended as the most important means of detecting cutaneous melanoma recurrence. The American Academy of Dermatology guidelines recommend surveillance intervals and follow-up tests， physical examination with emphasis on assessment of local recurrence， particularly for the lentigo maligna subtype， and a full skin check to eval-uate for new primary cutaneous melanoma at least every 6 to12 months for 1 to 2 years and annually thereafter for patients with stage 0 (melanoma in situ). For stages IA to lIA cutaneous melanoma， comprehensive history， review of systems， and phys-ical examination with specific emphasis on the skin and region-al lymph nodes are recommended at least every 6 to 12 months for 2 years and at least yearly thereafter. For stages IlB to IIC， the recommended follow-up interval is every 3 to 6 months for2 years， then at least annually thereafter . Generally， patients who are disease-free 10 years after diagnosis are considered nearly synonymous with cure and are discharged from follow-up. However， late recurrences， defined as occurrences 10 years or more after diagnosis， have been reported in several stud-ies， with incidence rates ranging from 1.01% to 12.75%. Owing to the limited population of patients and lack of extensive longitudina! follow-up， it is difficult to estimate the frequency， predisposing factors， and prognostic implications of late recur-rence of melanoma. Among all the recurrent locations， very few publications have described late cerebral metastasis (late recur-rences involving the brain) . In a cohort of 1372 patients with stage I-II melanoma who were disease-free 10 years after diagnosis， only 10 patients (7.3%) were found to have distant metastases involving the brain . In another collection of 1881patients with stage l or Il melanoma， only 1 patient (0.5%) was identified as having late cerebral metastasis .

【5】Late cerebral metastasis that occurs more than 10 years after the diagnosis of cutaneous melanoma is very rare. This report is of a 41-year-old woman with a diagnosis of late cerebral metas-tasis 16 years after an initial diagnosis of cutaneous melanoma.

【6】Case Report

【7】A 41-year-old woman was sent to the Emergency Department(ED) because of progressive disturbance of consciousness for 6 weeks and sudden coma for 6 h. The patient was diagnosed with malignant melanoma 16 years before from the biopsy of a dish-pattern tumor on the back， for which she received che-motherapy for 5 times (therapeutic regimen and medications were not available). She had not had any other diagnoses of skin melanoma in the past 16 years.
