【0】ABSTRACT Epistaxis is a common problem in otolaryngology emergencies. It can get the patient's life at risk， and different causes must be taken into account for proper diagnosis and prevention of complications. Hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia is a recurrent and abundant cause of epistaxis. We present a case of a 72-year-old male patient who experienced recurrent and abundant epistaxis and oesophagal bleeding requiring blood transfusions on multiple occasions， being diagnosed as hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia.

【1】KEYWORDS Hereditary-hemorrhagic-telangiectasia， epistaxis， nasal-bleeding，Osler-Weber-Rendu

【2】Introduction

【3】Recurrent epistaxis is a common problem in Otolaryngology emergencies. In most cases are mild， but in some others can be difficult to control due to the nasal irrigation from both the internal and external carotid branches .

【4】The most frequent epistaxis etiologies are cold and dry cli-mate， trauma， structural malformations， inflammatory patholo-gies and congenital syndromes like Osler Weber Rendu syn-drome . Treatment of epistaxis can change by the aetiology and quantity of bleeding from simple nasal compression ma-noeuvres， medications， modifying habits， and avoiding risk fac-tors， to surgical treatments.

【5】Clinical case

【6】A 72-year-old male patient， farmer， without chronic degenerative diseases， denied alcoholism and smoking. Appendectomy 55years ago， hernioplasty 17 years ago， with a history of blood transfusions due to anaemic syndrome secondary to bleeding from the upper gastrointestinal tract， 6 months ago and required blood transfusion. Gastroesophageal endoscopy was performed，

【7】Three days before his evaluation in our department， he pre-sented intense epistaxis on the right side， which he was attended at his locality hospital where nasal packing was placed and was hospitalized for observation； at the third day， he presented recur-rence of bleeding， for this reason， he is referred to our hospital.

【8】He was hypotensive， with tachycardia， with moderate right epistaxis， with telangiectasia lesions in the skin of the nose， lips， chin， and tongue. A haemoglobin level of 5，5 gr/dL was found. Right anterior nasal packing was placed and was blood transfused. Hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia (Osler-Weber-Randu Sx) was diagnosed. The patient was left under observa-tion . Nasal tamponade was removed on the third day， the bleeding was not present， he returned to evaluation after a week and a month did not present epistaxis again during this time. The treatment carried out later by the gastroenterology department consisted of argon coagulation of the lesions in the oesophagus three months later of the last epistaxis.

【9】Discussion

【10】The Osler Weber Rendu syndrome， also called hereditary hem-orrhagic telangiectasia (HHT)， is inherited in an autosomal dom-inant syndrome. The patient suffers from epistaxis， mucocuta-neous telangiectasia， and arteriovenous malformations (AVM) in the gastrointestinal tract，lung， liver， and brain. Worldwide， the prevalence of HHT varies depending on the country and even its region， from 1 in 5，000 to 1 in 10，000. The frequency between genders is equal.

【11】Its aetiology classifies HHT， it is an autosomal dominant disease， and an allele from the parents will be affected in one of their genes. HHT type 1 is caused by the mutation of the Endoglin gene (ENG) on chromosome 9， while HHT type 2 has a mutation in the activin receptor-like kinase-1(ACVRL1) gene on chromosome 12. Mutations in these two genes explain up to90% of symptomatic HHT.

【12】The most often due to a defect in the ENG， ACVRL1， or SMAD4 genes . The proteins that these genes encode are in-volved in the transforming growth factor-beta (TGFB) signalling pathway， responsible for the development and maintenance of arteries and veins. When one of these genes is damaged， several proteins with poor functions are made (the most common is that it is due to a premature terminal codon， which leads to an impairment of mRNA transcription and，therefore， an affected protein) . In some patients with HHT， mutations have been found in the MAHD4 gene that encodes the transcription factor Smad4， and this mutation is rare in HHT (it is only 1% of HHT). However， when found， it is associated with Juvenile Polyposis Syndrome.

【13】Although the mechanism by which vascular defects are ex-pressed in HHT is known， it is not known exactly why this does not happen in vessels throughout the body or why there are different patterns within the same families with the same type. However， some studies suggest that environmental factors and other genetic factors could influence the predilection of the affected vessels. 

【14】The most common clinical findings in HHT are epistaxis (re-current， earliest sign， up to 90% of patients present it at an early age)， iron deficiency anaemia， and telangiectasia in the gastroin-testinal tract， lips， oral mucosa， and tips of the fingers. Mu-cocutaneous and gastrointestinal telangiectasia are not present at birth but rather develop with age and frequently appear in childhood.

【15】More aspects of the disease are often overlooked with late symptoms and are not treated， which can lead to complications. These other conditions include： pulmonary arteriovenous mal-formations (present in 50% or more of patients， usually appear-ing after puberty)， cerebral vascular abnormalities， hepatic arte-riovenous malformations (present in more than 33% of cases)

【16】As a consequence of these conditions， which are usually later(although screenings have been done where the image is used more than the clinic， where some of the patients presented ar-teriovenous malformations first than telangiectasias)， we can have complications such as pulmonary hypertension， throm-boembolism and alterations in hemodynamics when bleeding is abundant. 

【17】The second international guideline on HHT recommends di-agnosing either with the Curacao criteria or by identifying the pathogenic variant in one of the genes that cause HHT. The Cu-racao criteria include the following： Recurrent and spontaneous epistaxis； Telangiectasias at characteristic sites of the disease； Visceral affection such as gastrointestinal telangiectasias， arte-riovenous malformations in the liver， brain， and or lung； First-degree relative with HHT. When the patient presents 3 or more of these criteria， it is considered diagnostic. If he has only 2 it is considered suspicious. If he only has one， it is unlikely that he suffers from the disease .

【18】Although it is not considered a requirement for diagnosis， genetic tests can be done to detect an abnormality in the ENG， ACVRL1， or SMAD4 genes. This serves to confirm the diagnosis of a patient with 3 or more Curacao criteria， also for suspected patients (only 2 criteria)， and to detect the affected gene， as conditions vary from one gene to another. For example， in type1 THH， more frequent pulmonary and cerebral arteriovenous malformations.

【19】While in type 2 HHT， hepatic arteriovenous malformations occur more frequently and， consequently， pulmonary hyperten-sion Treatment is primary prevention， regardless of severity. It consists of the patient avoiding circumstances or factors that may facilitate epistaxis. These factors will change from one patient to another. However， generally， they are avoidance： lifting very heavy objects， blowing your nose too much， bending over to grab an object， and even some foods like blueberries， red wine， chocolate， and spicy foods. The use of medications or remedies that have antiplatelet function should also be avoided， such as NSAIDs， aspirin， omega-3， garlic， ginkgo， among others.

【20】The dryness of the nasal mucosa due to cold and not very humid weather is the most common initiator of epistaxis. So patients are advised to take steps such as using nighttime hu-midifiers in their room applying topical moisturizer to the nasal mucosa (gel or ointment moisturizers are preferred).

【21】In addition to all these， some measures are taken depending on the severity of the epistaxis. An epistaxis severity score (ESS) is commonly classified as mild， moderate， and severe. This scale is based on 6 parameters of epistaxis that occurred in the last3 months. The parameters include frequency， characteristics， duration of bleeding， presence of anaemia， need for medical attention， and transfusion. Patients with a score of less than or equal to 4 have mild epistaxis. Scores greater than 4 but less than or equal to 7 are moderate， and those greater than 7 are considered severe. However， the ESS has its limitations， as it does not consider parenteral iron replacement or anaemia due to other causes such as digestive system (DS) bleeding.

【22】The medical therapy of HHT can include hormonal therapy， Bevacizumab， a vascular endothelial growth factor inhibitor， and its intranasal use can reduce the frequency and severity of epistaxis . Coblation， coagulation with Nd： YAG laser， and sclerotherapy had been used in the HHT therapy. Septodermo-plasty is a useful treatment in refractory epistaxis， and Young’s procedure that involves closing nasal vestibule is a radical but ef-fective surgery in selected patients when employed as unilateral treatment61.

【23】Conclusion

【24】Epistaxis is a frequent cause of attention in the emergency room and often requires specialist treatment. In cases of abundant and recurrent epistaxis， the diagnosis of hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia must be taken into account in patients who present data of concomitant digestive bleeding and the characteristic skin lesions.

【0】Background：

【1】Autoimmune polyglandular syndrome type 1 (APS-1) is an extremely rare autoimmune disorder with an auto-somal recessive inheritance pattern. Its manifestations present in chronological sequence of the components mucocutaneous candidiasis， Addison disease， and hypoparathyroidism. Vascular calcification is a very rare man-ation of the disease， and it may be severe， causing critical lower-limb ischemia and significant morbidity.

【2】To the best of our knowledge， this is the first such case to be reported in Jordan and the Arab region.

【3】Case Report： We present the case of a 29-year-old patient diagnosed with autoimmune polyglandular syndrome type 1(APS-1). He has Addison disease， hypoparathyroidism， and mucocutaneous candidiasis. He presented with fea-tures of critical lower-limb ischemia and bacterial infection of the left foot. The patient underwent a successful angioplasty and received management of his bacterial and fungal infections and the chronic endocrinopathies.

【4】Conclusions：

【5】Autoimmune polyglandular syndrome type 1 (APS-1) is a very rare disorder. Recognizing its syndromic nature will facilitate an active search for the component diseases and the possible complications， which would allow early diagnosis and management. This applies to the rare vascular complications， which can lead to significant morbidity.

【6】MeSH Keywords： Addison Disease · Angioplasty · Candidiasis， Chronic Mucocutaneous· Hypoparathyroidism·Peripheral Arterial Disease ·Polyendocrinopathies， Autoimmune

【7】Abbreviations：

【8】APS-1 - autoimmune polyglandular (or polyendocrine) syndrome type 1； APECED- autoimmune polyen-docrinopathy-candidiasis-ectodermal dystrophy； AIRE gene - autoimmune regulator gene Autoimmune polyglandular syndromes (APS) are rare syndromes diagnosed by the coexistence of at least 2 autoimmune endo-crinopathies. In addition， nonendocrine autoimmune manifes tations may be present . Autoimmune polyglandular syn-drome type 1 (APS-1) is defined by the coexistence of at least2 of 3 major component diseases： chronic mucocutaneous can-didiasis， autoimmune adrenal insufficiency， and primary hy-poparathyroidism，or only 1 if a sibling has the disease . The syndrome is a rare disorder with an autosomal recessive inheritance pattern . Vascular calcification is a rare manifestation of the syndrome ， and it can be severe， caus-ing significant lesions and ischemia . We present the case of a young patient with mucocutaneous candidiasis and mul-tiple endocrinopathies who presented with features of criti-cal lower-limb ischemia.

【9】A 29-year-old male patient presented with acute left-foot red-ness， swelling ， and chronic dystrophic nails of hands and feet with discoloration . The distal pulses were diminished， with monophasic signals on Doppler examination， and he previously had amputation of left fourth toe due to gan-grene. He was a known case of adrenal insufficiency and hy-poparathyroidism， taking hydrocortisone，fludrocortisone， and calcium supplements and alphacalcidol. The patient had no in-termittent claudication or resting pain， he was not diabetic， and he was a non-smoker. Treatment was started with an intrave-nous antibiotic (Piperacillin/Tazobactam) and antifungal med-ications (intravenous Fluconazole and Miconazole ointment). Bacterial and fungal cultures showed Morganella morganii and Candida albicans sensitive to the given medications. Lab inves-tigations showed elevated WBC count 21.3/mm，elevated ESR and CRP， low parathyroid hormone 1.2 ng/l (N 13-54)， hypo-calcemia Ca 1.7 mmol/l(N 2.1-2.6)， and hyperphosphatemia P1.69 mmol/l (N 0.8-1.6). Otherwise， he had normal kidney， liv-er， and thyroid function tests， and normal adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH)， follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH)， prolactin， and testosterone levels.

【10】A CT angio showed diffuse calcified atherosclerotic changes of the abdominal aorta and lower-limb arteries， with significant stenosis of the left popliteal artery and poor bilateral distal run off . He underwent an angioplasty with drug-eluting balloons for the left popliteal and tibial vessels. He lab test re-sults and clinical condition improved， and he was discharged after a hospital stay of 2 weeks， with prescription of oral med-ications (prednisolone， fludrocortisone， calcium supplements， alphacalcidol， and voriconazole) in addition to miconazole oint-ment. On follow-up， he had improvement of lower-limb vas-cularity and the bacterial and fungal infections were cured.

【11】Discussion

【12】Polyglandular autoimmune syndromes are a rare heteroge-neous group of genetic diseases of the immune system lead-ing to multiple endocrinopathies. Three types are described in the literature： type 1 (juvenile type)， type 2 (adult type)， and type 3 (the rarest). APS-1 is also known as Whitaker syndrome and autoimmune polyendocrinopathy-candidiasis-ectodermal dystrophy (APECED) . It is a very rare disorder inherited in a sporadic autosomal. recessive pattern and caused by genetic mutations affecting the autoimmune regulator (AIRE) gene on chromosome 21 . Studies have demonstrated the pres-ence of various circulating tissue-specific autoantibodies that cause dysfunction of the target endocrine glands . Also， the mutations lead to defective T cells and neutralizing auto antibodies against IL-22， IL-17A， and/or IL-17F， leading to the immunodeficiency underlying candidiasis .

【13】The syndrome clusters in certain ethnic populations， includ-ing Iranian Jews， Sardinians， and Finns . The highest prev-alence was reported in Iranian Jews with 1 case per 9000， Sardinians with 1 case per 14 400， and Finns with 1 case per25 000 . Low incidences (1： 90 000 to 1： 200 000) had been reported in Norway， Sweden， Poland， Slovenia， Slovakia， Russia， Great Britain， Ireland， and Italy . To the best of our knowledge， the present case is the first to be reported in Jordan and the Arab region. It is suspected that this disorder is underdiagnosed because of a lack of knowl-edge of the condition， the long intervals between the devel-opment of manifestations， the variability of disease severity， and the wide spectrum of clinical presentation .

【14】In APS-1， which is the focus of the present report， 2 out of 3 main components are sufficient for diagnosis，or only 1 if a sibling has the disease . In our patient， all 3 components were present：chronic mucocutaneous candidiasis， hypoparathyroidism， and ad-renal insufficiency or Addison disease. Classically，these compo-nents occur in chronological order， with mucocutaneous candidi-asis usually occurring earliest， followed by hypoparathyroidism， then adrenocortical failure . Additional endocrine and nonen-docrine manifestations may be present， including diabetes type1， hypothyroidism， gonadal failure， alopecia， vitiligo， nail dystro-phy， enamel hypoplasia， pure red cell aplasia. pernicious anemia， asplenia，malabsorption， and autoimmune hepatitis .

【15】Vascular calcification is an extremely rare manifestation of the syndrome. Our patient presented with critical lower-limb isch-emia due to significant stenosis of popliteal and tibial vessels and diffuse calcifications of the abdominal aorta and lower-limb vasculature. Vascular calcification in general is an active cellular process that occurs in response to metabolic insults causing disturbance in the balance between inhibiting and pro-moting factors of vascular calcification . It is suggested that certain cells in the vessel wall can be triggered to differen-tiate into osteoblast-like cells， including vascular smooth mus-cle cells， stem cells， and pericytes . Proposed triggers include oxidative stress， hyperphosphatemia， bone morpho-genetic protein， vitamin D， and parathyroid hormone . Proposed inhibitors include fetuin， osteotegrin， osteopontin， and pyrophosphate .

【16】Vascular calcification is usually associated with ag-ing， atherosclerosis， diabetes mellitus， and chronic kidney disease . One study found coronary artery calcifica-tion in 3 out of 30 cases of sporadic idiopathic hypoparathy-roidism . There are few reported cases in the literature of aortic and/or lower-limb arterial calcification associated with APS-1 ， and only 2 of them had critical lower-limb ischemia . Shikata et al.  proposed the progressive vascular calcification as a peculiar non-random part of APS-1. Also， Ohga et al.  proposed that progressive vascular calci-fication will eventually be recognized as a rare， unexplained， but grave component of APS-1.

【17】The management of our patient included a revascularization procedure for limb salvage， and correction of serum calcium and phosphate disturbances. In APS-1， hypocalcemia is due to hypoparathyroidism and the gastrointestinal manifestations of the syndrome， including intestinal malabsorption， pancre-atic exocrine failure， celiac disease， and intestinal lymphangi-ectasia. Calcium levels should be monitored on follow-up and maintained in the low-normal range .

【18】Autoimmune polyglandular syndrome type 1 (APS-1) is a very rare disorder. Recognizing its syndromic nature will facilitate an active search for the component diseases and possible compli-cations， which would allow early diagnosis and management. This applies to the rare vascular complications， which can lead to significant morbidity.

【0】ABSTRACT Introduction： Lymphoma is a group of lymphoproliferative malignancies that can originate in B lympho-cytes， T lymphocytes， or natural killer (NK) lymphocytes. They account for 3% of all cancer types. The WHO's 2008World Health Organization (WHO) classification of hematopoietic and lymphoid tumours was refined in 2016. This study screened surgically excised or biopsied specimens for lymphoma in lymphadenopathy. This research aimed to classify lymphomas in India based on histopathological and immunohistochemical findings. Methods： The study included 71 cases suspected/probable/ proven to have lymphomas and H&E-suggestive lymphoid malignancies were recruited. Clinical details， histopathological reports， and lymphoma panel IHC status were analyzed. Age， sex， biopsy site， B-symptom history， and clinical findings were recorded. Paraffin blocks were prepared from biopsy specimens in buffered formalin using standard automated methods. All cases’ slides were examined to confirm lymphoma. Tissue blocks were selected for IHC staining. All the slides were evaluated and classified as per the WHO 2016 lymphoma classification. Results： The mean age of the patients was 44.58 years， and 54 patients were males， while 17 were females.61 of 71 cases were detected to be of NHL and 10 cases were of HL. The majority of NHL cases were formed by B cell neoplasms， constituting 72.1%， whereas T cell neoplasms constituted 24.6%.2 of 61 cases showed CD56 positivity apart from T-cell markers and were categorized as T/NK cell NHL. As per WHO classification， different types of NHL and HL were classified. Among NHL， follicular lymphoma (FL) was predominant with 15 cases， while in CHL， mixed cellularity CHL prevalence was high. Ki67 expression in 15 cases of FL showed 1 case of grade 1， 3 cases of grade 2and 2 cases of grade 3 follicular lymphoma with a Ki67 index of more than 40%. Conclusion： Histomorphology and immunohistochemistry helps diagnose lymphoma. NHL was more common among nodal and extranodal lymphomas. The NHL and HL were dominated by men. Follicular lymphoma (FL) was the most common subtype of B-cell NHL. Most HL patients had mixed-cellularity CHL.

【1】KEYWORDS Lymphoma， Immunohistochemistry， Hodgkin's lymphoma， non-Hodgkin's lymphoma Lymphomas are a group of lymphoproliferative malignancies that can originate in B lymphocytes， T lymphocytes， or natu-ral killer (NK) lymphocytes. They are responsible for 3% of all cancer types.  Lymphoma is part of a diverse collection of lymphoreticular system cancers. Lymphoma cases have sky-rocketed in recent decades， and the spread of the HIV virus and the resulting decline in immune function is largely to blame. Over the past decade，lymphoma rates have risen worldwide， including in India.

【2】Lymphomas originate in the lymphatic system and some-times spread to non-lymphoid tissues. Hodgkin's lymphoma(HL) and Non-Hodgkin's lymphoma (NHL) are two types of lymphomas. The NHL is further categorized into low-grade and high-grade subtypes. Lymphoma is a disease whose clinical management and prognosis are strongly influenced by its classi-fication. The 2008 World Health Organization (WHO) classifica-tion of hematopoietic and lymphoid tumours was refined in 2016with a new framework due to better delineation of lymphoid ma-lignancy biology and increasing knowledge of molecular drivers of aggressive lymphomas.  This led to the development of the WHO's fourth edition classification， which was reviewed and published in Blood that same year. 

【3】Lymphoma symptoms and signs can include， but are not lim-ited to， unexplained fever， night sweats， enlarged liver spleen， or both；lymph node enlargement； painless or painful， soft to firm lesion(s) in various organs and tissues (extranodal lymphoma)； and so on.  Lymphomas have the potential to metastasize into the bone marrow (BM). Most cases of NHL manifest as extranodal lymphoma (ENL). The ENL may originate from any part of the body.One-quarter of all NHL cases are classified as extranodal lymphoma (ENL)， and its prevalence is rising. Additional information about lymphoma's classification and treatment options can be obtained from a bone marrow (BM) examination Since lymphadenopathy is a common presenting symptom of lymphoma ， the present study will involve histopatho-logical screening of surgically excised or biopsied specimens to determine the incidence of lymphoma in lymphadenopathy. In addition， one of the other goals of this research is to classify lym-phomas based on histopathological and immunohistochemical findings according to the new WHO classification of hematolym-phoid malignancies.

【4】Material and Methods

【5】The present cross-sectional study was carried out in the Depart-ment of Pathology， Bharati Vidyapeeth (DTU) Medical College and Hospital， Pune. A total of 71 cases of lymphomas (NHL and HL) were included in the study. All suspected， probable， and/or proven cases of lymphomas and cases with H & E his-tology suggestive of lymphoid malignancies were recruited. Pa-tients with non-hematolymphoid malignancies with or without metastasis and inadequate biopsies were excluded. The pa-tient's clinical details， histopathological reports， and status of lymphoma panel immunohistochemistry (IHC) were analyzed and recorded. There were no anticipated risk factors involved in this study except those occurring due to the natural process of disease progression.

【6】Methodology

【7】Patient selection was carried out based on the inclusion and exclusion criteria. Demographic details such as age， sex， biopsy site， clinical history of B symptoms， and clinical findings were recorded. Biopsy specimens were received in buffered formalin and processed for histopathology as per standard automated methods，and paraffin blocks were prepared. Freshly cut slides were prepared And stained with hematoxylin and eosin (H&E). First， slides of all the cases were studied， and a lymphoma diag-nosis was confirmed. After that， the cases were first segregated as Hodgkin's lymphoma and non-Hodgkin’s lymphoma. Then， WHO 2016 subtypes were used to make a preliminary diagnosis of the subtypes of HL and NHL based on their appearance.

【8】Immunohistochemistry (IHC)

【9】Appropriate tissue blocks were selected for IHC， and 3 to 4-micron thick sections were cut and taken on Poly L Lysine pre-coated slides for IHC staining. The slides were deparaffinized by dipping them in 2 changes of xylene for 15 minutes each. They were dried and dehydrated in two 15-minute ethanol changes. The Peroxidase antiperoxidase(PAP) method of IHC was used in this study. Antigen retrieval was carried out by microwaving in the Dako target solution at 90℃ for 2 cycles of 10 minutes each. After cooling the slides to room temperature， the slides were washed with distilled water for 3 cycles of 2 minutes each. Sec-tions were treated with hydrogen peroxide reagent on the slides for 30 minutes at room temperature. The slides were washed with PBS buffer. Each section was exposed to the required pri-mary antibodies used in this study separately. Slides were then exposed to the required primary antibodies for 2 hours at room temperature and washed with PBS buffer. At room temperature， these were treated with secondary antibodies for 1 hour and were washed with a working buffer. The slides were then treated with diaminobenzidine (DAB) chromogen with substrate buffer for 5 minutes at room temperature and washed with distilled water. Sections were counterstained with Harris haematoxylin for a minute， washed in distilled water， and mounted with DPX. As per manufacturer instructions， appropriate positive controls were also included in the batches of sections for staining. All the slides were evaluated and classified as per the WHO 2016lymphoma classification.

【10】Statistical analysis

【11】The histopathology and IHC analysis of tumours were done by visual assessment. The collected data were coded and entered into a Microsoft Excel sheet. The data were analyzed using SPSS(Statistical Package for Social Sciences) version 26.0 software. The results were presented in a graphical and tabular format. Various rates， ratios， and percentages (%) were calculated for qualitative data. A quantitative data average was calculated.

【12】Results

【13】In the present study， the age of the patients ranged from 1 to92 years， with a mean age of 44.58 years. The age range of the NHL was 1 to 92 years， with a mean ± SD of 46.05±24.28 years. The 61-80 year age group had the highest number of NHL cases， followed by the 41-60 year age group. In Hodgkin’s lymphoma， age ranged from 10 to 68 years， with a mean age of 35.60±24.86years. The 0-20-year age group had the highest number of HL cases. Among the 71 cases of lymphoma， 54 (76.1%) were male， and 17(23.9%) were female. Out of 61 total cases of NHL， 46(75.40%) were males， and 15 (24.60%) were females， as compared to cases of HL， where out of 10 cases，8(80%) were males， and 2(20%) were females.

【14】In this study， 71 cases of nodal and extranodal lymphomas were evaluated. Of 71 cases， 61 (85.9%) were NHL， and 10(14.1%) were HL. The NHL to HL ratio was 6.1：1. 61 cases of NHL were further divided into 32 cases (52.6%) of nodal and29 cases (47.4%) of extranodal lymphomas. No extranodal sites were found for Hodgkin's lymphoma in this study. Only clas-sical Hodgkin's lymphoma (CHL) was diagnosed in this study. Out of the 10 cases of CHL， 6 cases (60.0%) were of mixed cellu-larity classical Hodgkin's lymphoma (MCCHL)， 3 cases (30.0%) of nodular sclerosis classical Hodgkin's lymphoma (NSCHL) and 1 case (10.0%) of lymphocytic rich classical Hodgkin'slym-phoma (LRCHL). 

【15】Clinical presentation of NHL and HL (Symptoms)

【16】The most common symptom in NHL was anorexia/fatigue， noted in 93.4% (57/61) cases， followed by weight loss in 91.8%

【17】(56/61) cases， fever in 83.6% (51/61) cases， swelling in 72.1%(44/61) cases， night sweats in 45.9%(28/61) cases， dysphagia in37.7%(23/61) cases， and abdominal pain in 29.5%(18/61) cases. Anorexia/fatigue was again the most common symptom seen in90%(9/10) cases in HL， followed by fever in 80% (8/10) cases， weight loss and swelling in 70%(7/10) cases. 40% of cases had night sweats， 20% of cases had dysphagia， and the least common symptom was a pain in the abdomen， reported in 1 (10%) case.

【18】Clinical presentation (Sign) of NHL and HL

【19】The most common signs in NHL were lymphadenopathy (73.7%) and splenomegaly (73.7%). Apart from these， anaemia was seen in 72.1% of cases and hepatomegaly in 44.3% of cases. Oedema and effusion were present in 19.7% of cases，respectively. In HL， anaemia and splenomegaly in 40% of cases， respectively， were common in addition to lymphadenopathy， seen in all 10 (100%) cases. 

【20】The proportion of B cell and T cell neoplasms among NHL

【21】Among NHL (n= 61)， the majority was formed by B cell neo-plasms， constituting 72.1%， whereas T cell neoplasms constituted24.6%. Similarly， T-cell NHLs (15/61) were initially subjected to CD20 and CD3， followed by CD5， CD$ and CD8 as needed. Two61 cases wereT/NK cell NHL because they had T-cell markers and CD56 positivity.

【22】Morphological and immunohistochemistry (IHC) profiling This study identified eight of 61 NHL cases of lymphoblas-tic lymphomas， all of which showed diffuse monomorphic intermediate-sized cells. 4 of 61 cases of small lymphocytic lym-phoma (B-SLL/CLL) were identified， which showed monomor-phic diffuse small cell morphology. A male patient with a diffuse monomorphic large cell size， irregular nuclei， vesicular chro-matin， inconspicuous nucleoli， and a moderate cytoplasm was one of 61 cases of lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma (LPL). One of 61 cases of splenic marginal zone B-cell lymphoma (SMZL) was seen in a female patient with a diffuse monomorphic small cell size， round nuclei， vesicular chromatin， inconspicuous nu-cleoli， and a scant amount of cytoplasm. 15 of 61 cases were of follicular lymphoma. In this study， a 20-year-old male was re-ported to have pediatric-type follicular lymphoma. 13/61 cases of diffuse large B-cell lymphoma， not otherwise specified， were seen. 5 cases were of Burkitt lymphoma (BL).7/61 cases of pe-ripheral T-cell lymphoma， not otherwise specified， were seen in this study. Anaplastic large cell lymphoma， ALK-positive in a12-year-old male； Anaplastic large cell lymphoma， ALK-positive in a 55-year-old male's cervical lymph node； Mycosis fungoides in the skin； and hepatosplenic T-cell lymphoma (HSTL) in a 34-year-old female patient. Two cases were classified as T/NK cell lymphoma. 

【23】Ki67 expression was done in all 15 cases of FL. Of these， 1case of grade 1， 3 cases of grade 2， and all 02 cases of grade 3follicular lymphoma had a Ki67 index of more than 40%.  In classic Hodgkin'slymphoma， out of 10， 3 cases diagnosed were of nodular sclerosis classic Hodgkin's lymphoma. 6 cases were of mixed cellularity classical Hodgkin's lymphoma. 1 case was of lymphocyte-rich classical Hodgkin's lymphoma. 

【24】Lymphomas are a heterogeneous group of hematolymphoid malignancies， with each subtype having its own clinicopatho-logical and immunohistochemical features. The demographic details and relative frequencies tend to differ geographically. For example， greater cases are being reported from Europe and America compared to Asia.  Therefore， studying the fea-tures mentioned above helps better characterise and subtyping lymphomas. In settings with few resources， it has been hard to research because the panel of IHC markers is not always available.

【25】A total of 71 cases of nodal and extranodal lymphomas were studied in this study. Out of which， the majority were NHL， comprising 85.9%(61 cases)， and the remaining 14.1%(10 cases) were HL. This finding of the current study was the same as that found in other studies by Sharma M  et al.， Mushtaq S  et al.， Mukherjee M  et al.， Otrock ZK  et al.， Sader-Ghorra C  et al.， and Impana BD et al.

【26】In the present study， the mean age of all patients was 44.58years， while the mean ages of patients in the NHL and HL groups were 46.05 and 35.60 years， which is lower by a decade. The age group 61-80 years had the most cases of NHL， account-ing for 32.8%， followed by 41-60 years， accounting for 31.1%. Similarly， in HL， the maximum cases were in the age group of0-20 years， forming 50.0%， followed by 20% each in 41-60 and61-80 years. The male-to-female ratio was 3.2：1 for alllymphoma cases， with 54 (76.1%) cases in males and 17 (23.9%) in females. The male-to-female ratio for NHL was 3.1：1 and 4：1 for HL.

【27】In NHL and HL， clinical features are important as they give clues to the diagnosis and may also be helpful in subtyping. The present study studied the clinical features under the two broad headings of symptoms and signs. Some symptoms were swelling， abdominal pain， fever (body temperature above 38℃)， weight loss (more than 10% of TBW in the last six months)， night sweats， anorexia， fatigue， and trouble swallowing. These symp-toms constitute the B-symptoms seen in lymphoma (both NHL and HL). Similarly， signs were categorized into lymphadenopa-thy， anaemia， hepatomegaly，splenomegaly， oedema， and effu-sions. Anorexia and fatigue were the most common symptoms in both groups， followed by weight loss， fever， swelling， abdominal pain (mainly seen in cases with abdominopelvic involvement)， night sweats， dysphagia， and nodal involvement.

【28】As B-symptoms is constituted by the above symptoms， we found that these symptoms were more common in NHL than in HL， which was in contrast to other studies like Chakrabarti S et al. from India and Hingorjo MR  et al. from Pakistan， who stated that B-symptoms were more common in HL than in NHL. The reason for such a contrasting result can be attributed to the larger sample size of NHL compared to HL and the early diagnosis of HL in this study. Lymphadenopathy splenomegaly， and anaemia were the most common signs in both NHL and HL. Other signs， including hepatomegaly and effusion， were more prevalent in NHL than in HL. These findings were slightly lower than what Hingorjo MR  et al. found in their study， with both NHL and HL having anaemia as the most common sign， but higher than what Chakrabarti S  et al. reported. However， in the case of HL， data variation could be due to early disease diagnosis， better socioeconomic status， and an urban population.

【40】Morphological and Immunohistochemistry (IHC) profiling Lymphoma shows marked histomorphological variation； there-fore， immunohistochemistry has immense importance in diag-nosing and subtyping both NHL and HL. The morphologic assessment was done as described in the methodology. When abnormal cell populations are present， they are categorized as polymorphic or monomorphic. Further evaluation with geno-typic studies is required in certain cases due to aberrant expres-sion and prognostic significance. 

【41】Eight out of 61 NHL cases were identified as lymphoblastic lymphoma， showing similar histology. On IHC， four cases of B-cell LBL were identified. 3 of 4 cases were subtyped as pre-B-LBL， with all cases being CD10 negative. The remaining 1case was subtyped as common B-LBL with CD10 positivity. T-cell LBL constituted 4 out of 8 cases of all LBL. On IHC， 100%positivity for CD3 and CD5 was expressed. All T-cell LBL were TdT and CD34 positive. CD20 and CD23 were negative in these cases. These findings were similar to the findings reported by Rao IS . However， this finding did not correlate with the findings of Maitra A  et al.， who reported a higher number of T-cell LBL in their study. Thus， the present study reported an equal proportion of both B and T-cell LBL.

【42】4 of 61 NHL cases were identified as small lymphocytic lym-phoma (SLL)， which showed monomorphic small cells as de-scribed in the literature On IHC， all four cases (100%) were positive for CD20， CD79a，CD23， and LCA. All four cases(100%) of SLL were negative for CD10 and BCL2. A similar pro-file was described by Rao IS . There was 1 NHL case noted as lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma in a 66-year-old male showing monomorphic diffuse large cells. IHC showed CD20 and CD79a positive.CD3， CD5 and CD10 were all negative. It was positive for CD38 and CD138. The IHC finding correlates with what Rao IS . The case did not show Hepatitis C infection on screening， as studies  have reported higher rates in LPL cases. One case was of splenic marginal zone B-cell lymphoma (SMZL) seen in a61-year-old female patient with diffuse monomorphic small cell size. Morphology did not correlate with the findings mentioned in the literature . However， IHC showed positivity for CD20，CD79a，and BCL2. CD5， CD10，CD23， BCL6，and Cyclin D1 were negative.

【43】Among 61 cases of NHL， 15 cases were reported to be of fol-licular lymphoma (FL). Of these 15 cases， 5 (33.3%) and 8 (53.4%) cases were of grade 1 and grade 2 FL， respectively， which showed monomorphic round small cells， except 2 (13.3%) cases of grade3 FL， which showed monomorphic round large cells. 6 out of 15cases showed follicular architecture， 4 showed diffuse follicular architecture， 1 showed focally follicular/predominantly diffuse architecture， and 4 showed diffuse architecture. This was similar to what has been described by Sylvia MT  et al. in their study. On IHC， all 15 cases (100%) were positive for CD20， LCA， BCL2 and CD10. CD3 was negative in all 15 cases (100%). All15(100%) cases were negative for Cyclin D1. All 15 cases (100%) showed positivity for BCL2 and BCL6.

【44】One case of pediatric type follicular lymphoma was diag-nosed and was noted in a 20-year-old male in the cervical lymph node. Morphologically， it showed a diffuse follicular pattern with large cells. On IHC， CD20，CD79a， CD23， BCL6， LCA，and CD10 were positive. CD5 and BCL2 were negative， as reported in the literature . 13 NHL cases were of diffuse large B-cell lymphoma， not otherwise specified. Morphologically most cases showed diffuse monomorphic large cells with round nuclei， vesicular chromatin， multiple nucleoli， and a scant amount of cytoplasm. 2 out of 13 cases showed intermediate-sized cells；3 cases had inconspicuous nucleoli， and 2 cases had a moder-ate amount of cytoplasm. Most of the cases had centroblast polymorphic morphology， and a few of them had centroblasts variant morphology. On IHC， all 13 cases (100.0%) were positive for CD20， CD79a， and LCA. CD5 was positive in 02 cases (15.4%) and belonged to the ABC subtype. All 13 cases (100.0%) were negative for CD3， and 12 cases (92.3%) were negative for Cy-clinD1. Further molecular subtyping was done as per the Hans algorithm， and 09 cases (69.2%) were of the GCB subtype， with all 9 cases (100.0%) being CD10 positive.

【45】Five NHL cases were reported to have Burkitt lymphoma(BL). Morphologically they were diffuse， monomorphic， and intermediate-sized cells. Among those 5， 1 case had EBV infec-tion， and 2 cases had HlV， thereby corresponding to endemic BL and immunodeficiency-associated BL， respectively. Two cases tested negative for HlV and were of the sporadic variant. All five cases were in the 0-20 age group. 4 cases showed nodal involve-ment， and 1 case had extranodal involvement. Of the 3 cases showing bone marrow involvement， 2 were immunodeficiency-associated BL. On IHC， all 05 cases (100%) were positive for CD20， CD79a， BCL6， and CD10. TdT was negative in 4 cases(80.0%) and was not done in the fifth case. 5 cases (100.0%) showed CD5 and CD10 positive with variable intensity. BCL2was negative in all cases. All the cases of BL showed high Ki67， ranging between 95% and 100%. The findings were similar to what has been reported in the literature  and studies by Rao IS ， Miura Y  et al. EBV infection is closely associated with endemic BL. 

【46】The 7 NHL cases of peripheral T-cell lymphoma， not other-wise specified， were the most common T-cell NHL. They had diffuse， monomorphic， medium-sized cells. 3 out of 7 cases showed extranodal nasopharyngeal involvement， which is also frequently reported in the literature  and other studies by Mishra P  et al. On IHC， all 07 cases showed 100.0% positiv-ity for CD3 and LCA. Only four (57.1%) cases and two (28.6%) were positive for CD4 and CD5，respectively. In 4 cases (57.1%)， CD15 was positive. All 07 cases (100.0%)were negative for CD20and CD30， whereas 71.4% of cases were ALK-negative. ALK could not be done in 2/7 cases. The findings correlated with what Rao IS  had reported.

【47】One case of anaplastic large cell lymphoma， ALK-positive， was reported in a 12-year-old male with extranodal nasopha-ryngeal and bone marrow involvement. It shows large diffuse polymorphic large cells， which resembles the common pattern described in the literature  and other studies by Cairo M  et al. Even though Stein H  et al. did not find the nasopharynx a common site， 60% of cases had involvement out-side of the lymph nodes. The IHC showed positivity (100%) for CD5， CD4，LCA，CD30，and AKL，whereas CD20， CD3，and CD23 were negative. TdT and CK could not be done. Frequent bone marrow involvement was also reported by Chakrabarti S et al.， Mussolin L  et al.， and Mondal SK  et al. in their studies. One case had an anaplastic large cell lymphoma， ALK-positive， in the cervicallymph node of a 55-year-old male. It had diffuse polymorphic large cells， and bone marrow was not assessed IHC revealed positivity (100%) for CD3，CD5，CD4， LCA and CD30. Rao IS  also reported that CD20， CD23， CK， and ALK were negative. One case of Mycosis fungoides was seen in the skin of a 67-year-old male， which on microscopy showed diffuse monomorphic intermediate-sized cells with ir-regular nuclei， vesicular chromatin， inconspicuous nucleoli， and a moderate amount of cytoplasm， which was also similarly de-scribed by Munoz-Gonzalez H  et al. in his study. IHC showed positivity (100%) for CD3， CD5， CD4 and LCA.CD20and ALK were negative. Bone marrow was assessed in this case. In this study， 1 case of hepatosplenic T-cell lymphoma (HSTL) was seen in a 34-year-old female patient， which is similar to what has been reported in literature  and in a study by Pro B  et al. The spleen showed diffuse monomorphic intermediate-sized cells with round nuclei， fine chromatin， inconspicuous nucleoli， and a scant amount of cytoplasm. On assessment， bone marrow was involved， which correlated with the findings reported in the literature. On IHC， CD3 and LCA were positive. CD20， CD4， and CD5 were all negative.

【48】Finally， 2 NHL cases were classified as T/NK cell lymphoma. Both cases were seen as nasopharyngeal， occurring in 7 and 58-year-old males. Microscopically， it showed diffuse polymorphic intermediate-sized cells. IHC showed positivity (100%) for CD

【49】CD3 and LCA in both cases. CD4 was weakly positive in one case. Both cases were CD20 and CD79a negative. Because CD56was weakly positive in both cases， a clear distinction between T and NK cells could not be made， and further IHC and molecular studies were recommended.

【50】Ki67 was done in all 15 cases of FL. The study by Sylvia MT et al. concluded that even low grade (grade 1 and grade 2) FL can have high ki67(>40%). This subgroup has been found to behave as higher-grade lymphomas/DLBCL and requires high-dose chemotherapy. They reported that 22% of the cases had a high Ki67 index. In the present study， 26.7% of cases had a high Ki67 index， of which 1 case was grade 1 and 3 were grade2FL.

【51】The present study reported only classical Hodgkin's lym-phoma (CHL) cases. Out of those， MCCHL was the most com-mon. On IHC， Hodgkin’s Reed Sternberg (HRS) cells showed membrane and Golgi region positivity with CD15 and CD30. IHC was divided into three groups for ease of comparison：Group 1 (CD15+， CD30+， CD20-)， Group 2 (CD15-， CD30+， CD20-)， and Group 3 (CD15-， CD30+， CD20+). In this study， the most common pattern with 80.0% was Group 1(CD15+，CD30+， and CD20-)， representing the archetypical immunophenotype of CHL， which was consistent with the findings of Konkay K  et al. and Patkar N  et al.

【52】Comparison of subtypes of Hodgkin's lymphoma

【53】In the present study， only classical Hodgkin's lymphoma (CHL) was found， and no case of NLPHL was detected. Mixed cellu-larity classical Hodgkin's lymphoma (MCCHL) with 60.0% was the predominant subtype in this study， which was concordant with the findings of other Indian studies by Mukherjee M  et al.， Chakrabarti S  et al. Jain S  et al. Nodular sclero-sis classical Hodgkin'slymphoma， with 30.0%， was the second most common subtype to be reported in this study. Most studies done in India have shown that MCCCHL is the most common subtype.

【54】Conclusion

【55】Lymphoma diagnosis starts at the histomorphological level and is greatly helped by immunohistochemistry. Among both nodal and extranodal lymphomas， NHL was more common than HL. Males predominated in both the NHL and the HL. NHL occurred in older age groups compared to HL. In both NHL and HL， the cervical group of lymph nodes was most commonly affected. B symptoms were seen in both NHL and HL. Among NHL， follicular lymphoma (FL) was the predominant subtype. Mixed cellularity CHL is the most common subtype of HL.

【0】Background：

【1】Retroperitoneal teratoma is uncommon germ cell tumor presenting as abdominal mass in children and its incidence in adults is extremely rare. Symptoms of retroperitoneal teratoma are variable but in benign cases there is never an alteration of patient's general condition.

【2】Case Report：

【3】A 35 years old lady presented with history of persistent backache for the last 15 years for which she took analgesics. X-ray of the lumbar spine showed a calcifying shadow in left upper quadrant of the suprarenal area. CT scan confirmed the mass with calcifications and fluid levels containing predominantly adipose tissue. At surgery a retroperitoneal tumor was found adherent to the left adrenal gland but separate from the kidney. A histopathological diagnosis of primary mature retroperitoneal teratoma without any immature component was made and patient was followed up with serum alpha fetoprotein levels.

【4】Conclusions：

【5】Retroperitoneal teratomas are rare and difficult to diagnose because of nonspecific signs and symptoms. Ultrasonography and CT scan are helpful in diagnosis. Surgical excision is curative and recurrence is monitored by serum alpha fetoprotein in malignant cases.

【6】Key words： retroperitoneum· teratoma · germ cell

【7】BACKGROUND

【8】Retroperitoneal teratoma is uncommon germ cell tu-mor usually presenting as an abdominal mass in chil-dren. Its incidence in adults is extremely rare . It arises independently from the tissue in retroperitoneal space and not from adjacent organs or structures . Symptoms of retroperitoneal teratoma are variable but in benign cases there is never an alteration of the patient's general condition. Radiologically computed tomography (CT) scan outlines the tumor and its characteristics with its relationship to the surround-ing structures . Histopathological examination is the gold standard in the diagnosis by finding mature epithelial， mesenchymal and or neural tissue without element of any immature component .

【9】We came across the one such rare case at our institute which is therefore reported.

【10】CASE REPORT

【11】A 35 years old lady presented with history of per-sistent backache for the last 15 years for which she took analgesics for symptomatic relief. During one of her visits to the clinic she was advised an X-ray of the lumbar spine. A calcified shadow was seen in the left upper quadrant in the suprarenal area . A subsequent ultrasonography showed a separate mass above the left kidney. The mass was compress-ing the upper pole of the left kidney. A Computed tomography (CT) scan  showed a heteroge-neous hypo attenuating area in the left supra-renal region starting from the tail of pancreas reaching the upper pole of left kidney and displacing it inferiorly. Coarse calcific density shadows were noted along its posterior wall along with calcific foci along its anterior wall. Two third of the tumor was composed of fat. Fluid attenuation area was noted anteriorly in the upper part making fat fluid level. Multiple internal loculations were noted in the lesion. The mass displaced the gut loops anteriorly and spleen superiorly. Rest of the abdominal visceras were unremarkable.

【12】A provisional diagnosis of myolipoma was made keeping dermoid cyst and liposarcoma in the dif-ferential diagnosis. The patient was advised serum alpha fetoprotein and serum B-HCG levels which were within normal limits.

【13】At surgery a retroperitoneal tumor was found adherent to the left adrenal gland but separate from the kidney. It was not adherent to the surrounding structures. The tumor was removed completely and submitted for histopathological examination.

【14】Grossly the tumor was an encapsulated grey white nodular mass with a thin capsule having promi-nent vessels on the surface measuring 8x7x6 cm and weighing 95 grams. Adrenal gland was at-tached on the surface at one focus. Cut surface showed a variegated appearance. It was main-ly fatty in nature with areas showing cyst for-mation containing mucinous fluid. Calcified ar-eas were seen with multifocal grey white areas. Calcified areas were processed after decalcifi-cation.

【15】Microscopically the tumor showed adrenal gland separated by a capsule from the tumor. The tumor showed predominantly adipose tissue .There were scattered areas of mature glial and neural tissue positive for S-100 and GFAP proteins on immuno histochemistry . 【17】Teratomas arise form germ cells that fail to mature normally in the gonadal location. These totipotential cells differentiate into components that represent mesoderm， endoderm and ectodermal derivatives. The distribution in the decreasing order is ovary， testis， mediastinum， presacral， coccygeal areas and retroperitoneum . The migratory property of germ cells would explain the extragonadal occurrence of these teratomas .

【18】Approximately half of the patients are found in the first decade of life where they pose a diagnostic challenge from Wilm’s tumor， neuroblastoma and other intra-abdominal tumors . Less than 20%of these patients are over 30 years of age . The incidence of retroperitoneal teratomas in females is twice that of males . Retroperitoneal teratomas are rare and constitute less than 10% of all primary retroperitoneal tumors .

【19】Retroperitoneal tumors are often located near the upper pole of the kidney with preponderance on the left side . Patients present with compressive symptoms or abdominal distention， nausea and vomiting . Plain abdominal radiograph shows a mass with calcification within or in its wall. This is present in 53-62% cases and helps in the preop-erative diagnosis .Ultrasonography identifies solid， cystic and complex components with fat fluid levels . 【0】Background：

【1】Encapsulating peritoneal sclerosis (EPS) is a rare， life-threatening， and serious complication of long-term peri-toneal dialysis (PD). No evidence-based management strategy has been established until now. Surgical man-agement， including enterolysis and excision of the sclerotic and obstructing adhesions， should be considered as soon as conservative management fails to work. We report a case of EPS soon after transplantation in a pa-tient with end-stage kidney disease who had been on long-term PD.

【2】Case Report： A 26-year-old man had been found to have advanced chronic kidney disease secondary to glomerulonephritis on pre-employment investigation. He was on continuous ambulatory PD for 5 years， after which he underwent a living donor renal transplant from his full HLA-matched sibling. He did well postoperatively， with excellent graft function. One month after transplantation， he repeatedly presented to our Emergency Department with signs and symptoms of complete small-bowel obstruction. Computed tomography of the abdomen showed features of small-bowel obstruction secondary to interloop adhesions. The patient was initially managed conservatively； however， as his condition continued to deteriorate， an exploratory laparotomy was carried out. Operative find-ings were suggestive of early EPS localized to the terminal ileum. Total enterolysis along with peritonectomy was performed along with resection of the diseased and obstructing terminalileum. The patient did well， and he was discharged home day 10 postoperatively.

【3】Conclusions： EPS remains a serious and fatal complication of long-term PD. Early definitive diagnosis， treatment， and ultimate-ly surgical intervention may be required to prevent the morbidity and mortality associated with this condition.

【4】MeSH Keywords： Kidney Transplantation· Peritoneal Dialysis ·Peritoneal Fibrosis·Tissue Adhesions Encapsulating peritoneal sclerosis (EPS) was first described in1907 and linked to peritoneal dialysis (PD) only in 1978 . EPS can be classified as primary， if the underlying cause is unknown， or secondary. Secondary EPS has many etiologies， the most common being PD. EPS is a rare clinical syndrome characterized by an acquired， inflammatory fibrocollagenous membrane encasing or cocooning the abdominal contents， mainly the small intestine， resulting in signs and symptoms of bowel obstruction and malnutrition. EPS is defined by the International Society for Peritoneal Dialysis  as“a syndrome in which adhesions of a diffusely thickened peritoneum causes repetitive and intermittent signs and symptoms of intestinal obstruction." The incidence of EPS in PD patients has been re-ported to range from 0.7% to 7.3%. Studies have shown a direct relation between the incidence of EPS and the duration of PD. The preoperative diagnosis of EPS remains challenging and requires a high index of suspicion， and in many cases a definitive diagnosis is made at the time of the surgical pro-cedure. Medical treatment of EPS includes the use of tamox-ifen， steroids， or immunosuppressants. The failure of medical treatment to effect improvement is an indication for surgery. Owing to the rarity of the disease and high morbidity，we re-port a case of EPS in a patient with end-stage kidney disease who was on PD before undergoing kidney transplantation.

【5】Case Report

【6】A 26-year-old man had been found to have advanced renal im-pairment on pre-employment investigations and commenced dialysis soon after. A renal biopsy showed evidence of C3 glo-merulonephritis with severe interstitial fibrosis and tubular at-rophy. Further work-up based on serological and genetic test-ing confirmed complement dysregulation (factor H mutation).

【7】The patient was on continuous ambulatory PD for 5 years ， without any episodes of peritonitis. He had se-vere hyperparathyroidism with parathyroid hormone levels reach-ing 450 pmol/L (normal 1.6-6.9)，for which he underwent subto-tal parathyroidectomy in October 2018 with improvement in his parathyroid hormone levels to around 80 mmol/Lpretransplant.

【8】He underwent a living donor renal transplant in April 2019 from his full HLA-matched sibling. The transplant was done with a standard retroperitoneal approach， and no assessment of intra-abdominal findings was done because all the work was extra-peritoneal. The patient initially had delayed graft function and needed dialysis for a few days， but he subsequently started to produce urine and his creatinine gradually improved to com-pletely normal (60-70 umol/L). The PD catheter was removed2 weeks after the transplant.

【9】Postoperatively， the principles of enhanced recovery after sur-gery were applied. The patient was started on a normal diet on day 1 postoperatively in addition to early mobilization and physiotherapy. He tolerated his diet well up until his 10"h day after receiving the transplant， when he developed acute ab-dominal distension， nausea， and vomiting， with generalized tenderness and absent bowel sounds. An X-ray of the abdo-men showed an element of small-bowel obstruction. Computed tomography (CT) with oral contrast showed generalized dila-tation of the small-bowel loops， suggesting subacute small-bowel obstruction.

【10】The patient was managed conservatively with nasogastric de-compression， and he recovered fully within a few days and was subsequently discharged home. After discharge， he had persis-tent abdominal distension， anorexia， and nausea associated with decreasing weight. He was on a normal diet during this time but tolerating it poorly. He was readmitted in May 2019with abdominal distension， prerenal acute kidney injury (AKI， creatinine 149 pmol/L)， and significant elevation in C-reactive protein (CRP) without a focus of infection and negative cul-tures. Abdominal ultrasound was done， and it showed mod-erate ascites. The patient had no signs of bowel obstruction on that presentation； however， based on the constellation of his symptoms， as well as elevated CRP of 177 (normal 0-5) and the finding of ascites， EPS in an inflammatory phase was suspected. The patient's prednisolone dose was increased to25 mg once daily (0.5 mg/kg) and tamoxifen was added. He was discharged home a few days later in a stable condition. His creatinine completely normalized with intravenous (IV) vol-ume replacement (70 umol/L).

【11】Despite medical treatment for possible EPS， the patient pre-sented to our Emergency Department approximately a week later with worsening abdominal distension and further in-creases in his CRP  and AKI (creatinine 110 pmol/L) but without signs of obstruction. His ultrasound showed wors-ening ascites and hence paracentesis was carried out， which revealed a lymphocytic， culture-negative fluid and no malig-nant cells on cytology. CT with Ⅳ contrast showed angula-tion， tethering， and kinking of the small-bowel loops sugges-tive of interloop adhesions with persistent fecalization of the small bowel， suggestive of slow transit. The peritoneal mem-brane surrounding the loops had slight thickening， but there was no element of peritoneal calcification . His cre-atinine remained above his baseline despite lV fluids， hence a graft biopsy was performed， which showed no signs of re-iection or recurrent disease.

【12】Medical therapy with prednisolone and tamoxifen was contin-ued. Based on data suggesting that mTOR inhibitors may be of benefit due to their antifibrotic properties ， tacrolimus was switched to sirolimus. The patient had significant weight loss， requiring the administration of dietary supplements. A few weeks later， he developed a second bout of bowel obstruction， which was again managed conservatively with total parenter-al nutrition for a few days. After clinical improvement， he was again discharged， although he continued to have air-fluid lev-els on abdominal X-rays. Within 48 hours of discharge he was readmitted with his third episode of obstruction and high in-flammatory markers. Conservative management worked again， the radiologic signs resolved， and the patient was discharged in relatively good health.

【13】In June 2019， the patient presented with overt bowel obstruc-tion， confirmed on abdominal X-ray. This was managed con-servatively with nasogastric decompression and total paren-teral nutrition. During that admission， due to the recurrent obstructions without any clinical improvement， surgical in-tervention was considered. The patient was initially reluc-tant to undergo surgery. However， due to his continued clini-cal deterioration， he eventually underwent surgery 2 months after admission. Due to persistent bowel obstruction， as well as clinical evidence of malnutrition， total parenteral nutrition was started 1 month prior to his surgery through a periph-erally inserted central catheter No further small-bowel imag-ing was done at that point， as the diagnosis was clear. At lap-arotomy， there was grossly distended small bowel from the mid-jejunum to the distal ileum with a closed loop obstruc-tion. Thirty centimeters of distal terminal ileum approximate-ly 20 cm from the ileocolic junction was diseased with partial cocooning ， sclerosis， contraction， and gross features in keeping with early localized EPS. Total enterolysis was per-formed from the duodenojejunal flexure to the ileocecal junc-tion， and the diseased obstructed distal ileum was resected and re-anastomosed with a side-to-side ileocolic anastomo-sis. The abdomen was managed as a laparostomy with neg ative-pressure therapy using a homemade VAC system with a continuous negative pressure of -40 mmHg. After 48 h， the patient underwent a planned re-exploration， and the anasto-mosis was found to be intact and the abdomen was clean. It was closed in the midline in a standard fashion with 2 drains.

【14】Postoperatively， the patient was managed with continuous na-sogastric suction， deep vein thrombosis prophylaxis， and total parenteral nutrition. Over the next 14 days， there was a grad-ual return of gut function， oral feeds were introduced， and the patient was weaned off parenteral nutrition. His postopera-tive course was complicated by an episode of multi-drug-resis-tant Pseudomonas aeruginosa bacteremia for which a 10-day course of piperacillin-tazobactam and fosfomycin was given， with subsequent negative blood cultures. The patient was discharged home 2 weeks after surgery on tacrolimus， pred-nisolone (tapered dose)， and tamoxifen. Sirolimus had been stopped 1 month prior to surgery because it is known to im-pair wound healing. The patient remains very well 9 months after surgery， with no signs of recurrent disease， and he has gained more than 10 kg. Tamoxifen， which he was on for 6months， was recently stopped.

【15】Discussion

【16】EPS results in peritoneal thickening and bowel encapsulation leading to intestinal obstruction secondary to an exaggerat-ed fibrogenic response of the peritoneal membrane . Many factors have been implicated in its pathogenesis， including ex-posure to hypertonic glucose-containing solutions， long dura-tion of PD therapy (more than 5 years)， and repeated episodes of peritonitis . The 2-hit hypothesis highlights the balance between 2 factors： peritoneal damage due to chronic expo-sure to toxic PD fluids， which disrupts the natural peritoneal and mesothelial physiology (the first hit)， and a major inflam-mation stimulus (the second hit). Our patient was on PD for more than 5 years， which likely resulted in long-term changes to his peritoneal membrane (i.e.， first hit). Moreover， he was exposed to multiple potential inflammatory stimuli， which in-cluded renal transplant， removal of the PD catheter， and immu-nosuppressive medications， all of which may have potentially served as the second hit， leading to the development of EPS .

【17】The relationship between long-term exposure to PD and in-creased risk of EPS is not well understood. Animal models have shown that the secretion of different cytokines， includ-ing transforming growth factor p1 and vascular endothelial growth factor， by the macrophages and fibroblasts leads to mesothelial cell damage . However， EPS is a dynamic pro-cess in which fibrosis and neovascularization progress even after the triggering agent has been removed . For example， EPS can occur in kidney transplant patients who were previ-ously on PD， as in our case. A recent study has shown that kid-ney transplantation itself and the usage of calcineurin inhibi-tors in immunosuppressive regimens also increase the risk of EPS . Early EPS manifests with nonspecific symptoms， in-cluding nausea， diarrhea， and abdominal pain. These symp-toms may wax and wane and progress to more severe symp-toms， such as constipation， malnutrition， and weight loss. Our patient exhibited all the classical EPS signs and symptoms of gastrointestinal dysfunction， leading to obstruction.

【18】Due to the rarity of the disease， the diagnosis of EPS on imag-ing can be challenging and depends on underlying suspicion of the condition by the radiologist. According to recent litera-ture， an abdominal CT scan is the main imaging modality used to diagnose EPS ， and it was the main diagnostic method in our case. CT images often show thickened or calcified peri-toneum enveloping tethered small-bowel loops.Other radio-graphic features include loculated ascites， increased density of mesenteric fat， and localized or diffuse peritoneal calcifi-cation . In our patient， diagnostic features on CT included peritoneal thickening， proximal bowel loop dilation， and dis-tal small-bowel intestinal obstruction.

【19】EPS has been classified into 4 stages： pre-EPS， inflammatory， encapsulating， and chronic stages . Depending on the stage of the disease， the management and therapeutic approach dif-fer . For example， during the earlier stages (stages1-2)， the pathophysiology tends to be more inflammatory and the degree of sclerosis tends to be minimal. In the later stag-es (stages 3-4)， more advanced sclerosis may be present， and patients may start exhibiting signs and symptoms of partial or complete bowel obstruction . Medical treatment options for EPS include corticosteroids followed by immunosuppressive drugs such as azathioprine， sirolimus， tacrolimus， and antifi-brotic drugs such as tamoxifen .

【20】Surgical intervention is important if the medical treatment does not improve the clinical condition， and it should be con sidered before the patient's condition deteriorates while on medical therapy . Surgical techniques vary depending on the patient presentation. Some are done with curative intent， such as enterolysis (ablation of fibrotic tissue and lysis of ad-hesions)， while others address a specific complication， such as resection of perforated or ischemic bowel and limited lysis of adhesions.Although most cases respond to surgical treatment， poor surgical outcomes have been reported. The literature pro-vides varying outcomes with regard to the surgical manage-ment of EPS. In a large case series from Japan， 181 of 239 pa-tients underwent adhesiolysis with no complications in their long-term follow-up. In another case series， 45 EPS patients showed no response and partial deterioration to decapsula-tion； moreover， 3 of the 45 patients died . Outcome data are even more limited in posttransplant patients.

【21】The need for an enterectomy and anastomosis may be asso-ciated with a very high mortality rate. In a retrospective study of 106 patients with EPS in Japan， 9 out of 11 patients (82%) died after enterectomy and anastomosis. Conversely， only 2of 15 cases (13%) died after enterolysis alone . These re-sults suggest that enterolysis is preferred over enterectomy and anastomosis in EPS patients. Kawanishi  has also sug-gested that combining Noble plication (suturing the intestines to each other) with enterolysis reduces the rate of EPS recur-rence to 12.3%. During enterolysis， it is advised to tackle ob-structing areas at the end and to begin with segments where adhesiolysis can be performed easily .

【22】An important factor that determines the surgical outcome of EPS patients is the duration of PD， which correlates with the severity of peritoneal deterioration. It is technically less chal-lenging to operate on patients who have undergone PD for less than 10 years. Peritoneal calcification，especially visceral， is another factor that may increase the risk of intestinal per-foration and complicate the postoperative course .

【23】Small-bowel obstruction is an early postoperative complica-tion that usually happens secondary to prolonged bowel dis-section， and it frequently results in edema and fibrinous adhe-sions. These patients improve with conservative management， which includes bowel rest and parenteral nutrition. Steroids， somatostatin， and postoperative stenting of the intestinal loops may reduce the rate of postoperative bowel obstruc-tion . In a single-center review of 65 cases with abdomi-nal cocoon， intestinal stenting was performed for 46 out of 65patients using a tube that entered the intestine through the root of the appendix. These patients had a lower incidence of intestinal obstruction compared with those without stenting(P=0.005) . Surgical mortality， which was as high as 50%in the past， can be significantly reduced in experienced cen-ters managing a high case load . Our patient demonstrat-ed a classical posttransplant EPS in which medical therapy failed， but surgical intervention was successful. Nine months after surgery， the patient remains well.

【24】Conclusions

【25】EPS is a rare but serious complication of long-term PD， with high morbidity and mortality rates if not diagnosed early and managed properly. It is especially unfortunate when patients who were on PD for a long time develop EPS after a success-ful transplantation. Therefore， timely surgical management should always be provided as soon as the patient fails to re-spond to medical treatment.

【0】ABSTRACT Xanthelasma palpebrarum is the most common cutaneous xanthoma. It typically presents in middle-aged and older adults， characterized by yellowish plaques around the eyelids. The diagnosis can often be made based on clinical appearance. This article presents a 29 years old female with bilateral xanthelasma palpebrarum accompanied by subconjunctival lipoma.

【1】KEYWORDS Polymyositis， Systemic sclerosis， overlap syndrome， respiratory failure， proximal myopathy

【2】Introduction

【3】Xanthelasma palpebrarum (XP) is the most common type of xanthoma. The prominent feature of lesions is yellowish， flat， and soft. It is commonly found at the medial angle of the eyelid， symmetrical， bilateral and permanent. Although XP is a benign condition and almost does not cause the functional deficit， it is cosmetically disturbing. This typically presents in middle-aged and elderly people， often found in women.  Xanthelasma palpebrarum is highly associated with atherosclerosis， cardio-vascular disease， diabetes， obesity and pancreatitis.  Lesions progress slowly and do not regress without treatment. Therefore surgical excision has been the treatment of choice for decades. Xanthelasma palpebrarum may lead to ptosis if they enlarge excessively. The dermal layer of the face is the most common area where this can be spotted. Therefore， it can be removed through cosmetic treatment. This paper discusses the unique case of bilateral xanthelasma palpebrarum appearing with sub-conjunctival lipoma.

【4】Case report

【5】A 29-year-old female presented with bilateral circular yellowish patches around the upper and lower eyelids can also be seen in the sclera . The lesions started to appear one year before admission to the hospital， firstly seen at the medial aspect of the upper and lower eyelids and spread to the lateral sides and into the sclera. The patient felt itchy in the left and right palpebral. The patient complained that she felt difficulty opening her eye-lids and the devastating cosmetic appearance. This patient also complained about pain in the eyes， itchiness， redness and hyper lacrimation. There was no history of trauma on both eyes. How-ever， she experienced the same complained two years ago about the both superior palpebral and had been excised but recur and even grew larger.

【6】Based on the clinical manifestation alone， the diagnosis of XP can be established. The patient was compos mentis， vital signs were normal， and medical history was non-contributory. She had no medication history for hyperlipidaemia or cardiovascular disease. Her mother and two sisters had a history of mild XP limited only in both palpebral. On physical examination， she had the yellowish flat plaques involved both the upper and lower eyelids， resembling a pair of circles. The sizes were： 25x5mm in the right upper eyelid；20x5 mm in the right lower eyelid；28×8 mm in the left upper eyelid； and 23×10 mm in the leftlower eyelid. Similar lesions cannot be found elsewhere on the body. In the ophthalmologic examination， the doctor found a thick subconjunctival yellowish plaque on both eyes， medially and laterally .

【7】There was no limitation of the extraocular muscle move-ment. Complete blood count and urine analysis were within nor-mal range. The total cholesterol was 177 mg/dL， high-density lipoprotein (HDL) cholesterol 26 mg/dL，low-density lipopro-tein (LDL) cholesterol 140 mg/dL， and triglyceride levels 135 mg/dL. The histopathology result of the lesion in the palpe-bral and eye showed lymphocyte infiltration and dermis was diffusely infiltrated by large， foamy， and lipid-laden histiocytic called "xanthoma cells" between connective tissue and capillary filled erythrocyte. This patient was planned to have excision by an ophthalmologist for the subconjunctival lipid plaque follow with XP excision by a dermatologist.

【8】Discussion

【9】Xanthomas are deposits with high cholesterol content and are generally found in any part of the body. There is a case of11 years old boy suffered xanthoma in his left perilimbal con-junctiva extent into his sclera reported by Ali-Rhida et al.  Xanthelasma palpebrarum is a type of xanthoma that occurs over the eyelids， with the absence of xanthomas elsewhere.  Therefore this case report present a rare case of xanthoma which can be found not also in the eyelid as it manifest as xanthelasma palpebrarum but also in the sclera. Xanthomas can be associated with primary hyperlipidemias， such as types II and IV， having low high-density lipoprotein (HDL) levels， or secondary hyper-lipidemias， such as hypothyroidism， diabetes mellitus， drugs such as glucocorticoids， cyclosporine， cimetidine， estrogen， var-ious types of antihypertensive drugs， retinoids， antiepileptic drugs， anabolic steroids， tamoxifen， and foods that contain high saturated fat， cholesterol， and high alcohol. However， the exact pathomechanism is not fully understood.

【10】The prevalence of xanthelasma palpebrarum is estimated at4%， with an incidence of 1.1% in women and 0.3% in men. The most frequent age range for onset is from 15 to 73 years. In general， it will occur in their 40s or 50s. Approximately 50%of cases are caused by hyperlipidemia， and if it occurs before the age of 40 years， then screening must be done to prevent congenital disorders of the underlying lipoprotein metabolism. Xanthelasma palpebrarum can occur in normal lipid persons with low HDL levels.  In this patient， the total cholesterol level was normal， with low HDL and high LDL， and no history of any medication.

【11】Xanthelasma in the skin results from the deposition of fibro-proliferative connective tissue caused by histiocytes that contain lots of lipids or often referred to as foam cells. Histologically， these foam cells often appear in the middle and superficial lay-ers of the dermis in the perivascular and periadnexal areas， due to fibrosis and inflammation.  Commonly patients have lipid metabolism associated disorders， whereas xanthoma cells frequently accumulate around blood vessels imply that the ac-cumulated dermal lipid derives from the serum. Some studies found that atherosclerosis is rare in normolipidemia xanthomas and necrobiotic xanthogranulomas， but in high hyperlipidemic xanthomas， these are frequent.  Furthermore， cholesterol deposition in xanthelasma and atheroma plaque formation in vessels are experimentally similar.  Hypercholesterolemic xanthomas tend to result in a more nodular and tendinous type. As a result of local factors， eyelid dermis becomes thinner while pulsatile pressure causes dermal capillary pressure to be-come higher during nictitation， in this case， it can occur 10-30times/minute. This is allegedly supporting the deposition of fat in the eyelid. These local factors can result in the development of lesions on the eyelids. But the reason for this development limited to eyelids which is a phenomenon of leakage from capil-laries is not yet clearly known. Several suggestions can be made about this issue. This area has exceedingly rich vasculature. In systemic disease， fluid builds up in the eyelids. In this case， the disease in question is like nephrotic syndrome and congestive heart failure.

【12】Experiments indicate that LDL capillaries are twice as likely to leak in xanthomas because of physical movements and friction than in xanthomas at the immobilized skin site. The evelid experiences unchanging movement and friction， which is the reason that allows the development of XP in that section. It is also possible that the patient is intrinsically vulnerable to experiencing capillary leak.

【13】Xanthelasma palpebrarum is benign condition so it does not interfere body function， however， it is cosmetically disturbing. This problem can be overcome by consulting with a dermatolo-gist， ophthalmologist， or plastic surgeon so that the lesion can be removed.  There are several types of XP treatment such as simple surgical excision， cryotherapy， chemical peel using trichloroacetic acid (TCA)， radio frequency (RF)， and laser.
