【0】Background：

【1】Thyrotoxic hypokalemic periodic paralysis (THPP) is a medical emergency characterized by recurrent episodes of muscle weakness. In hypokalemic periodic paralysis， the muscle is normal between attacks and the diagnosis may be difficult if the attack is the first as seen in our patient.

【2】Case Report：

【3】We report a 23-year-old male patient who presented with acute flaccid paralysis associated with hypokalemia and thyroiditis in etiology. After he had eaten lots of chocolates in the evening， he was unable to walk in the next morning. He had a history of 3 similar episodes.

【4】Conclusions：

【5】Although there are lots ofreports about hypokalemic periodic paralysis related to hperthyroidism， hypokalemic periodic paralysis related to thyroiditis is rarely reported.

【6】Key words： thyroiditis· hypokalemia· periodic paralysis Thyrotoxic hypokalemic periodic paralysis (THPP) is characterized by recurrent episodes of muscle weakness and hypokalemia associated with thyroid hyperactivity . THPP is a medical emergency characterised by sudden onset of muscle weakness with hypokalemia that resolves with the treatment of hyperthyroidism . The pathogenesis of thy-rotoxic hypokalemic periodic paralysis (THPP) is unclear. It is well known that the attacks of paralysis no longer occur once thyrotoxicosis is cured； there-fore a necessary condition for the disorder is the presence of excessive amount of thyroid hormones in serum. Whatever the underlying mechanism， the fundemantal defect in THPP is increase in intracel-lular potassium with concomitant reduction of extra-cellular potassium. This influx of potassium into cells causes a failure in depolarisation of the muscle cell membrane . In this case report， we present a patient who took a diagnosis of thyroiditis， which was a rare condition in etiology， with episodes of hypokalemic paralysis.

【7】CASE REPORT

【8】A 23-year-old man was admitted to the emergency department of Diizce University Medical Faculty with generalised weakness. The attack occured after high carbohydrate meals (lots of chocolates) at dinner， the weakness was noted on waking in the next morning. In the neurological examination， the patient was alert with flaccid paralysis of the legs and arms and lower limbs were more affected by than upper limbs. Deep tendon reflexes were globally depressed. He was tachycardic with a pulse rate of 120/min， and blood pressure was 130/80 mmHg. His skin was sweaty. Examination of the neck revealed an enlarged smooth thyroid gland. He had a history of 3 similar episodes of which suffering from severe muscle weakness in the upper and lower limbs after eating lots of choco-lates. Initial laboratory evaluation demonstrated low level of serum potassium (1，5 mmol/L； Reference range = 3，7-5，4 mmol/L)， high level of glucose(241 mg/dL； Reference range = 65-115 mg/dL)， and low level of phosphate (1，3 mg/dL； Reference range=2，7-4，5 mg/dL). His hematologic parameters， renal function， sodium， calcium and liver function parameters were normal. ECG was performed and it was markedly abnormal. The changes consistent with ST depression and U waves in all derivates were seen. Electromyography examination revealed the axonal degeneration in the motor nerves of lower limbs. We made a clinical diagnosis of hypokalemic periodic paralysis and potassium chloride was administrered. The generalised weakness began to resolve within 6 hours from onset， and he had a complete recovery clinically after 24 hours. Serum potassium level on the following day was 4.6 mmol/L. Serum levels of cholesterol and creatine kinase were 160 mg/dL and 125 ug/dL respectively. Renal and gastroin-testinal system consultations and examinations were normal. The detailed laboratory assesment proved hyperthyroidism with a supressed thyroid stimulating hormone 0，015uIU/ml (reference range0，27-4，2 uIU/ml) and an elevated free triiodothyro-nine 21，4 pmol/L (reference range 2，8-7，1 pmol/L) and free thyroxine 42，9 pmol/L (reference range11，6-22 pmol/L). He had not previously ingested iodine or thyroid hormones. Serum levels of anti-thyroglobulin antibody， anti microsomal antibody and thyroglobulin were 20 IU/ml (reference range0-40 IU/ml)， 257 IU/ml (reference range 0-35 IU/ml) and 51.7 ng/ml (reference range 1.7-56 ng/ml) re-spectively. Thyroid ultrasonography examination revealed increased vascularization of gland paren-chyma in normal size. Thyroid scintigraphy showed increased uptake of 99mTc-pertechnetate inhomo geneously as seen in hyperthyroidism. From the clinical course and laboratory findings， he took a diagnosis of thyroiditis， probably an early stage with hyperthyroidism of chronic thyroiditis. On this oc-casion， he was commenced on Propylthiouracil and Propranolol.

【9】DISCUSSION

【10】THPP is not a common disease in Asian patients. Only 25% of thyrotoxic Asian men might present with this complication . THPP has been reported to occur in 4.3% to 8.2% of hyperthyroid Japanese males  and 12.9% of Chinese males . In our knowledge this is the second Turkish patient with THPP in English literature . Thyroiditis was the another and different feature of our patient.

【11】Attacks more commonly occur at night while the patient is in bed， following exertion or a high-carbo-hydrate meal as in our patient. Despite thyrotoxi-cosis being more common in women， THPP has a strong male preponderance with a male：female ratio estimated 20：1 and median age of third to fourth decade . Typical features of hyperthyroidism can be subtle or absent and the diagnosis of thyro-toxicosis usually postdates the onset of paralysis， and biochemical hyperthyroidism is usually confirmed at the time of presentation  as our case. The exercise test (ET) is a useful and sensitive diagnostic test for periodic paralysis in the presence of recent symptoms and no treatment. The test was always done during an inter-attack period when muscle strength was nor-mal. After strong muscle contraction for two to five minutes， abnormal reductions in combined muscle action potential amplitudes are seen during asymp-tomatic periods in all forms of periodic paralysis. Larger decrements are observed in affected subjects with recent attacks and in patients with thyrotoxic periodic paralysis. In thyrotoxic periodic paralysis， the ET was abnormal in the three of the four patients studied . In critism， it is a defect that we did not use ET although the first ENMG examination showed the low amplituded responses supporting the condition.

【12】Treatment of the acute episode of weakness is not standardized and usually includes potassium replace-ment. However there is a risk of significant rebound hyperkalaemia . Beta blocker therapy is ad- vocated to acutely terminate events and and prevent further episodes in THPP . Early diagnosis and prompt treatment prevent life-threatening compli-cations associated with hypokalemia and muscle weakness . To prevent recurrent episodes of paralysis treatment must be directed at restoring euthyroidism .

【13】CONCLUSIONS

【14】Thyrotoxic periodic paralysis should be considered in the differential diagnosis of sudden onset paralysis following exertion or a high-carbohydrate meal in young male patients. Determination of the plasma potassium levels and thyroid hormones help in the diagnosis .

【0】ABSTRACT Aim： India has reported a recent surge in Mucormycosis cases. Prevention of COVID-19-associated Mucormycosis needs to focus on aiming for better glycemic control in COVID-19 patients and monitoring the use of systemic corticosteroids in treating severe cases. This study attempts to evaluate various patient characteristics that could contribute to Mucormycosis among COVID and post-COVID patients. Materials and Methods： A retrospective observational study was carried out at a tertiary Care Hospital from April 2021-June 2021. After obtaining approval from the Institutional Ethics committee， various demographic and clinical details of all patients， such as diabetes mellitus， use of steroids in COVID-19 treatment， immunosuppressant drugs， oxygen therapy etc.， were noted. In addition， all Mucormycosis patients were treated with Amphotericin B and aggressive surgical treatment. Results： In the present study， most patients who developed COVID-associated Mucormycosis were treated in Private Hospitals(65，62.5%) for COVID -19 disease. About 78.89% of Mucormycosis patients were males. Most of the patient's onset of symptoms of Mucormycosis were seen during the first week(56%). Most patients were between 51-60 years(32.1%). Among risk factors， 91.7% had COVID-19 infection， 90.47% had received steroids， 80% had diabetes mellitus， and 47.11%had received oxygen. About 37% of patients presented in stage IlI， and 35% presented in stages I and II. In our study， mortality was very less compared to other studies( 12.35%.). Conclusion： There is a complex association between COVID -19 and Mucormycosis. The main predisposing factor was the use of steroids during the treatment of COVID-19， which led to uncontrolled diabetes mellitus predisposing to Mucormycosis.

【1】KEYWORDS COVID-19， Mucormycosis， Rhino Orbital Cerebral Mucormycosis，Diabetes

【2】Introduction

【3】Mucormycosis is a serious but rare fungal disease caused by fungi belonging to the family of Mucormycetes or Zy-gomycetes. These fungi are commonly found in the envi-ronment and soil. It is non-contagious and does not spread by direct or indirect contact. Instead， the disease occurs when a sus-ceptible person comes in contact with spores in the environment.

【4】The global incidence rate of mucormycosis varies from 0.005to 1.7 per million. Whereas in India， it is estimated at 140 per million population， which is about 80 times higher than the prevalence in developed countries. In a systemic review and meta-analysis of 851 case reports published in 2018， Case fatality was observed to be highest among patients with disseminated mucormycosis(68%) and lowest in those with cutaneous dis-ease(31%)

【5】The most common causative agents of mucormycosis include Rhizopus species， Mucor， Cunninghamella， Apophysomyces，

【6】Lichtheimia(formerly Absidia)， Saksenaea， R hizomucor， and other species.

【7】Coronavirus disease 2019 patients are at risk of secondary infections with a wide range of opportunistic bacterial and fun-gal infections. Aspergillus and Candida are the main fungal pathogens for co-infection in people with COVID-19. Recently India has witnessed an increased number of Mucormycosis cases among COVID patients， especially post-COVID diabetic patients. Other contributing factors include hypoxia，steroid-induced hy-perglycemia， high iron levels， and decreased phagocytic activity of white blood cells(WBC) due to immunosuppression(SARS-CoV-2 mediated，steroid-mediated or background comorbidities) and prolonged hospitalisation and ICU stay.

【8】Following the surge of COVID-19-associated mucormycosis and the Government of India directive， several states in India made Mucormycosis a notifiable disease in May 2021. Current trends indicate that the most common predisposing risk factors in most patients are pre-existing diabetes， systemic corticos-teroids， and COVID-19.

【9】This study attempted to evaluate various patient characteris-tics like diabetes， treatment with steroids and other immunosup-pressants， COVID status， commonest site of involvement and outcome of the disease after treatment.

【10】Methods and Materials

【11】Ethical statement and informed consent

【12】During the pandemic， we conducted a retrospective cross-sectional observational study at AIG Hospitals -a tertiary care centre. The study was approved by the Institute’s Ethics commit-tee(Approval Number： AIG/IEC-Post BH&R 15/06.2021-04).

【13】Study Design

【14】A retrospective cross-sectional observational study was con-ducted on all patients admitted to AIG Hospitals to treat COVID-associated Mucormycosis from May to June 2021.

【15】Patient demographic details， COVID status， Co-morbidities， Clinical and treatment details， location of Mucor-mycosis and outcome were collected from case sheets of all patients admitted to AIG Hospitals and the data was subsequently analysed.

【16】Diagnosis of Mucormycosis was based on European Con-federation of Medical Mycology guidelines for diagnosing and managing mucormycosis.

【17】Inclusion criteria

【18】All cases of mucor-mycosis in COVID and Post-COVID cases admitted to AIG Hospitals for treatment were included in the study.

【19】Exclusion criteria

【20】Any case of Mucormycosis without COVID or only COVID positive patients were excluded from the study.

【21】Case definitions

【22】A case of mucormycosis was defined as laboratory identifica-tion of Mucorales by culture， histopathology， or polymerase chain reaction in a patient with a clinical diagnosis of invasive mucormyCOSlS.

【23】Cases were considered COVID-19-associated if the patient received a positive reverse transcription-polymerase chain reac-tion or antigen test result for SARS-CoV-2(the virus that causes COVID-19) during the 60 days preceding the mucormycosis diagnosis.

【24】Data was collected and analysed using SPSS(Statistical Package for the Social Science) software. Quantitative data with normal distribution were expressed as mean +/- Standard deviation. Nominal data were given as a number(n) and percentage(%). Chi 2 test was implemented on such data. P-value < 0.05 was considered as significant.

【25】Results

【26】Out of a total of 109 cases of mucormycosis，100(91.74%) were COVID positive(confirmed by RTPCR)， and 9 were post-COVID and RTPCR negative( 8.25%) at the time of admission. The majority of the patient’s onset of symptoms of mucormycosis was seen during the first week(56%) and 4 weeks after COVID-19 in 22(22%) patients. Most patients who developed COVID-associated Mucormycosis were treated in Private Hospitals(65，62.5%) for COVID-19 disease.

【27】Out of the 109 patients， 86(78.89%) were males， and 23(21.1%) were females. The age group ranged from 24 to 75 years in the study group. Most patients were between 51-60 years(32.1%) fol-lowed by 41-50 years(23.85%). The mean age of the study group with males and females was 50.34 yrs and 48.78 yrs， respectively.\[Table11

【28】This study showed that mucormycosis was predominantly seen in males(78.89%) in the age group of 41-50 yrs. Steroid use for the treatment of COVID -19 was the single most important risk factor observed in most cases(95，90.47%) of Mucormycosis in people with COVID-19. The majority of them were on Ⅳsteroids(55.96%)， and the duration of use of steroids was 1-2weeks in most of the patients， 42(38.8%). History of diabetes was present in 84 cases， followed by remdesivir(74.75%)， Plasma therapy(93.2%) and tocilizumab(0.97%). Pre-existing diabetes was seen in 80% of the cases.

【29】The majority of the patients were on plain oxygen(49，47.11%)， out of which 7(6.73%) were on NIV， 3(2.8%) were on a ventilator， and 30 were not on oxygen(28.8%).

【30】Of the 60 patients， 35% had stage 2 mucormycosis involving nasal cavities and sinuses. Stage 3 mucormycosis was seen in37% of patients. 2% had invasive stage 4 mucormycosis involv-ing CNS， and only 1 patient had stage 1 mucormycosis limited to the nasal cavity. Only 3 patients(3%) had Pulmonary Mu-cormycosis. Overall mortality was noted in(12.35%) of the cases.\[Table1T

【31】Refer to Table  for statistical analysis of patient character-istics. Tables  show an analysis of statistical significance between patient variables like gender， stage of mucormycosis， and the effect of surgery and diabetes on clinical outcomes. The results of the present study have been compared with other studies. 

【32】Discussion

【33】There were three major factors： COVID -19， pre-existing diabetes or uncontrolled diabetes and systemic corticosteroid treatment in large proportions of patients.

【34】Possible theories for CAM-related to immune and inflamma-tory processes include：

【35】 COVID-19 causes significant lymphopenia， leading to a reduction in the availability of CD4+ and CD8+ T cells and predisposing to opportunistic fungal infections；

【53】 increased pro-inflammatory markers in patients with severe COVID 19 disease； and

【54】 Severe damage to lungs by COVID-19 favours invasive fungal diseases， particularly Mucormycosis.

【55】It is now a well-known fact that the 2nd wave of COVID-19 is due to new variants which can gain entry into host cells through additional routes like GRP 78 receptors . In-silico studies have shown stable interaction between the RBD domain of spike protein(C480-488) with that of GRP 78， predicting its role in endocytosis. It is to be noted that mucormycosis also have the same port of entry， i.e. GRP78 into the nasal and paranasal sinus mucosa through its coat protein Cot H3.20 T. One hypothesis for overexpression of GRP78 is high glucose and iron content found during DKA and second dexamethasone-induced GRP78expression and thus may facilitate the invasion of mucormycosis into target cells for further proliferation.

【56】There is still a less explored reason for GRP78 overexpression， namely endoplasmic reticulum(ER) stress. In normal healthy people， the protein folding ability of the endoplasmic reticulum matches the body's protein synthesis ability. But， in stress con-ditions， e.g. virus infection， cells accumulate excessively high numbers of unfolded viral structural proteins in ER， leading to overexpression of GRP78 at the cell surface， making the cells vulnerable to fungal pathogens， e.g. MM.

【57】78% of COVID-19-associated mucormycosis cases reported in our study occurred in male patients. The prevalence of the disease was common in males， similar to other studies .

【58】Further studies are needed to investigate whether this gender imbalance might result from differing susceptibility-confirming what was recently observed in a diabetic ketoacidosis mouse model(in which female mice were more resistant to Mucorales infection than male mice).

【59】Our study observed that steroid use was a predominant risk factor for COVID-associated mucormycosis compared to oth-ers. In most cases， steroids were given for 1-2 weeks. But it is difficult to establish a causal relationship between COVID -19and Mucormycosis concerning steroids as no studies compared mucormycosis patients in non-diabetic COVID-19 who did not receive steroids versus COVID-19 patients who received steroids and developed mucormycosis.

【60】The frequent use of corticosteroids that exacerbate glucose homeostasis may predispose patients to Mucormycosis. In ad-dition， corticosteroid use is a key risk factor for opportunistic mycoses， including Mucormycosis.

【61】Uncontrolled hyperglycemia and metabolic acidosis are a result of corticosteroid intake. Low pH due to acidosis is a favourable medium for mucor spores to germinate. Steroid use impairs the phagocytic activity of WBC(both first line and second line defence mechanism)， making a diabetic patient ex-ceptionally vulnerable to mucormycosis.

【62】Pre-existing Diabetes was seen in most patients， similar to other studies. The presence of DM is an independent risk factor for mucormycosis and is often associated with increased severity of COVID-19. The phagocytes of immunocompetent hosts kill spores of Mucorales by producing oxidative metabolites. Hyper-glycemia due to DKA can change this immunologic response， reducing neutrophilic phagocytosis with a modified neutrophilic response. Glycosylation of transferrin and ferritin resulting from hyperglycaemia reduces iron binding， allowing increased free iron. Free available iron is an ideal resource for Mucormycosis.

【63】In our study， many patients were on Remdesivir(74.75%)but very few on Tociluzimab(0.97%).

【64】Dr Ravindra Mehta， chief of pulmonology， Apollo Hospital， said that they found mucormycosis in several patients who received tocilizumab and remdesivir.

【65】Tocilizumab， an anti-IL-6 receptor monoclonal antibody， is India's only immunosuppressant drug permitted for off-label use. Increased use of tocilizumab in patients with COVID-19may be a significant risk factor for contracting CAM.

【66】"The infection mostly occurred 14 days after contracting COVID". In our study， it was observed that in April and June， cases presented during 1 st week of COVID. In May， cases pre-sented late，i.e.>4 weeks after onset of COVID.

【67】It was observed that 47.11% of the patients in our study were on oxygen therapy. Oxygen therapy for a longer duration causes exposure to humidified air. Also， if the water in the humidifier is not sterile， it increases the exposure of sinuses to infection.

【68】In India， Rhino-orbital cerebral mucormycosis is more com-mon compared to the Pulmonary form. It occurs more frequently outside the ICU setting and， possibly， in patients with less severe COVID-19 than other forms of COVID-19-associated mucormy-cosis.

【69】Unfortunately， mucormycosis patients have a significant mor-tality rate even through adjunct surgery. However， our study's mortality rate( 12.35%) was less compared to many other stud-ies.

【70】Probably this was because most patients presented within the first week of onset of symptoms and underwent debridement with effective anti-fungal treatment.

【71】Limitations of our Studv

【72】In this retrospective observational study， we could not compare various risk factors among COVID-associated Mucormycosis with Non-COVID patients to establish a causal association.

【73】We could not gather information about all variables as data in case sheets was incomplete.

【74】Conclusion

【75】There is a complex association between COVID -19 and Mu-cormycosis. The main predisposing factor was the use of steroids during the treatment of COVID-19， which led to uncontrolled diabetes mellitus predisposing to Mucormycosis. In addition， Rhino orbital mucormycosis was more common than other Mu-cormycosis forms.

【76】There is little awareness of COVID 19 associated Mucormy-cosis among the public. Countries with a high incidence of diabetes and COVID-19(e.g.， Bangladesh， India， Pakistan， Iran， Mexico，China， Russia， Indonesia， and the USA) should monitor patients closely for a month after recovery from COVID-19，as most cases of COVID-19-associated mucormycosis are detected within this time period. This would help in the early diagnosis of cases.

【77】Indiscriminate use of Corticosteroids for the treatment of COVID should be stopped.

【78】Mortality was less in our subjects than in other studies as most patients presented with Rhino orbital mucormycosis against pulmonary mucormycosis. A careful management plan for COVID-19 Disease can help prevent rhino-orbital cerebral disease. Combined Medical and surgical management exhibited better outcomes.

【0】ABSTRACT Aim： India has reported a recent surge in Mucormycosis cases. Prevention of COVID-19-associated Mucormycosis needs to focus on aiming for better glycemic control in COVID-19 patients and monitoring the use of systemic corticosteroids in treating severe cases. This study attempts to evaluate various patient characteristics that could contribute to Mucormycosis among COVID and post-COVID patients. Materials and Methods： A retrospective observational study was carried out at a tertiary Care Hospital from April 2021-June 2021. After obtaining approval from the Institutional Ethics committee， various demographic and clinical details of all patients， such as diabetes mellitus， use of steroids in COVID-19 treatment， immunosuppressant drugs， oxygen therapy etc.， were noted. In addition， all Mucormycosis patients were treated with Amphotericin B and aggressive surgical treatment. Results： In the present study， most patients who developed COVID-associated Mucormycosis were treated in Private Hospitals(65，62.5%) for COVID -19 disease. About 78.89% of Mucormycosis patients were males. Most of the patient's onset of symptoms of Mucormycosis were seen during the first week(56%). Most patients were between 51-60 years(32.1%). Among risk factors， 91.7% had COVID-19 infection， 90.47% had received steroids， 80% had diabetes mellitus， and 47.11%had received oxygen. About 37% of patients presented in stage IlI， and 35% presented in stages I and II. In our study， mortality was very less compared to other studies( 12.35%.). Conclusion： There is a complex association between COVID -19 and Mucormycosis. The main predisposing factor was the use of steroids during the treatment of COVID-19， which led to uncontrolled diabetes mellitus predisposing to Mucormycosis.

【1】KEYWORDS COVID-19， Mucormycosis， Rhino Orbital Cerebral Mucormycosis，Diabetes

【2】Introduction

【3】Mucormycosis is a serious but rare fungal disease caused by fungi belonging to the family of Mucormycetes or Zy-gomycetes. These fungi are commonly found in the envi-ronment and soil. It is non-contagious and does not spread by direct or indirect contact. Instead， the disease occurs when a sus-ceptible person comes in contact with spores in the environment.

【4】The global incidence rate of mucormycosis varies from 0.005to 1.7 per million. Whereas in India， it is estimated at 140 per million population， which is about 80 times higher than the prevalence in developed countries. In a systemic review and meta-analysis of 851 case reports published in 2018， Case fatality was observed to be highest among patients with disseminated mucormycosis(68%) and lowest in those with cutaneous dis-ease(31%)

【5】The most common causative agents of mucormycosis include Rhizopus species， Mucor， Cunninghamella， Apophysomyces，

【6】Lichtheimia(formerly Absidia)， Saksenaea， R hizomucor， and other species.

【7】Coronavirus disease 2019 patients are at risk of secondary infections with a wide range of opportunistic bacterial and fun-gal infections. Aspergillus and Candida are the main fungal pathogens for co-infection in people with COVID-19. Recently India has witnessed an increased number of Mucormycosis cases among COVID patients， especially post-COVID diabetic patients. Other contributing factors include hypoxia，steroid-induced hy-perglycemia， high iron levels， and decreased phagocytic activity of white blood cells(WBC) due to immunosuppression(SARS-CoV-2 mediated，steroid-mediated or background comorbidities) and prolonged hospitalisation and ICU stay.

【8】Following the surge of COVID-19-associated mucormycosis and the Government of India directive， several states in India made Mucormycosis a notifiable disease in May 2021. Current trends indicate that the most common predisposing risk factors in most patients are pre-existing diabetes， systemic corticos-teroids， and COVID-19.

【9】This study attempted to evaluate various patient characteris-tics like diabetes， treatment with steroids and other immunosup-pressants， COVID status， commonest site of involvement and outcome of the disease after treatment.

【10】Methods and Materials

【11】Ethical statement and informed consent

【12】During the pandemic， we conducted a retrospective cross-sectional observational study at AIG Hospitals -a tertiary care centre. The study was approved by the Institute’s Ethics commit-tee(Approval Number： AIG/IEC-Post BH&R 15/06.2021-04).

【13】Study Design

【14】A retrospective cross-sectional observational study was con-ducted on all patients admitted to AIG Hospitals to treat COVID-associated Mucormycosis from May to June 2021.

【15】Patient demographic details， COVID status， Co-morbidities， Clinical and treatment details， location of Mucor-mycosis and outcome were collected from case sheets of all patients admitted to AIG Hospitals and the data was subsequently analysed.

【16】Diagnosis of Mucormycosis was based on European Con-federation of Medical Mycology guidelines for diagnosing and managing mucormycosis.

【17】Inclusion criteria

【18】All cases of mucor-mycosis in COVID and Post-COVID cases admitted to AIG Hospitals for treatment were included in the study.

【19】Exclusion criteria

【20】Any case of Mucormycosis without COVID or only COVID positive patients were excluded from the study.

【21】Case definitions

【22】A case of mucormycosis was defined as laboratory identifica-tion of Mucorales by culture， histopathology， or polymerase chain reaction in a patient with a clinical diagnosis of invasive mucormyCOSlS.

【23】Cases were considered COVID-19-associated if the patient received a positive reverse transcription-polymerase chain reac-tion or antigen test result for SARS-CoV-2(the virus that causes COVID-19) during the 60 days preceding the mucormycosis diagnosis.

【24】Data was collected and analysed using SPSS(Statistical Package for the Social Science) software. Quantitative data with normal distribution were expressed as mean +/- Standard deviation. Nominal data were given as a number(n) and percentage(%). Chi 2 test was implemented on such data. P-value < 0.05 was considered as significant.

【25】Results

【26】Out of a total of 109 cases of mucormycosis，100(91.74%) were COVID positive(confirmed by RTPCR)， and 9 were post-COVID and RTPCR negative( 8.25%) at the time of admission. The majority of the patient’s onset of symptoms of mucormycosis was seen during the first week(56%) and 4 weeks after COVID-19 in 22(22%) patients. Most patients who developed COVID-associated Mucormycosis were treated in Private Hospitals(65，62.5%) for COVID-19 disease.

【27】Out of the 109 patients， 86(78.89%) were males， and 23(21.1%) were females. The age group ranged from 24 to 75 years in the study group. Most patients were between 51-60 years(32.1%) fol-lowed by 41-50 years(23.85%). The mean age of the study group with males and females was 50.34 yrs and 48.78 yrs， respectively.\[Table11

【28】This study showed that mucormycosis was predominantly seen in males(78.89%) in the age group of 41-50 yrs. Steroid use for the treatment of COVID -19 was the single most important risk factor observed in most cases(95，90.47%) of Mucormycosis in people with COVID-19. The majority of them were on Ⅳsteroids(55.96%)， and the duration of use of steroids was 1-2weeks in most of the patients， 42(38.8%). History of diabetes was present in 84 cases， followed by remdesivir(74.75%)， Plasma therapy(93.2%) and tocilizumab(0.97%). Pre-existing diabetes was seen in 80% of the cases.

【29】The majority of the patients were on plain oxygen(49，47.11%)， out of which 7(6.73%) were on NIV， 3(2.8%) were on a ventilator， and 30 were not on oxygen(28.8%).

【30】Of the 60 patients， 35% had stage 2 mucormycosis involving nasal cavities and sinuses. Stage 3 mucormycosis was seen in37% of patients. 2% had invasive stage 4 mucormycosis involv-ing CNS， and only 1 patient had stage 1 mucormycosis limited to the nasal cavity. Only 3 patients(3%) had Pulmonary Mu-cormycosis. Overall mortality was noted in(12.35%) of the cases.\[Table1T

【31】Refer to Table  for statistical analysis of patient character-istics. Tables  show an analysis of statistical significance between patient variables like gender， stage of mucormycosis， and the effect of surgery and diabetes on clinical outcomes. The results of the present study have been compared with other studies. 

【32】Discussion

【33】There were three major factors： COVID -19， pre-existing diabetes or uncontrolled diabetes and systemic corticosteroid treatment in large proportions of patients.

【34】Possible theories for CAM-related to immune and inflamma-tory processes include：

【35】 COVID-19 causes significant lymphopenia， leading to a reduction in the availability of CD4+ and CD8+ T cells and predisposing to opportunistic fungal infections；

【69】Unfortunately， mucormycosis patients have a significant mor-tality rate even through adjunct surgery. However， our study's mortality rate( 12.35%) was less compared to many other stud-ies.

【70】Probably this was because most patients presented within the first week of onset of symptoms and underwent debridement with effective anti-fungal treatment.

【71】Limitations of our Studv

【72】In this retrospective observational study， we could not compare various risk factors among COVID-associated Mucormycosis with Non-COVID patients to establish a causal association.

【73】We could not gather information about all variables as data in case sheets was incomplete.

【74】Conclusion

【75】There is a complex association between COVID -19 and Mu-cormycosis. The main predisposing factor was the use of steroids during the treatment of COVID-19， which led to uncontrolled diabetes mellitus predisposing to Mucormycosis. In addition， Rhino orbital mucormycosis was more common than other Mu-cormycosis forms.

【76】There is little awareness of COVID 19 associated Mucormy-cosis among the public. Countries with a high incidence of diabetes and COVID-19(e.g.， Bangladesh， India， Pakistan， Iran， Mexico，China， Russia， Indonesia， and the USA) should monitor patients closely for a month after recovery from COVID-19，as most cases of COVID-19-associated mucormycosis are detected within this time period. This would help in the early diagnosis of cases.

【77】Indiscriminate use of Corticosteroids for the treatment of COVID should be stopped.

【78】Mortality was less in our subjects than in other studies as most patients presented with Rhino orbital mucormycosis against pulmonary mucormycosis. A careful management plan for COVID-19 Disease can help prevent rhino-orbital cerebral disease. Combined Medical and surgical management exhibited better outcomes.

【0】Background： Carotid cavernous fistulas (CCFs) are rare potentially sight-threatening abnormal connections between carot-id artery and cavernous sinus.

【1】Case Report：

【2】We report a case of CCF in an 83-year-old female， who presented with swollen and painful right eye. The patient was initially treated with empiric antibiotics for suspected peri-orbital cellulitis， as noted clinically and in com-puted tomography (CT) orbits. However， lack of clinical improvement， physical finding of orbital bruit/thrill，and enlarged superior ophthalmic vein in magnetic resonance (MR) orbits suggest alternate diagnoses. Eventually CT angiogram (CTA) and carotid-arteriography confirmed the diagnosis of right-sided direct CCF， which was subsequently treated with endovascular embolization. Not only does this case highlight the importance of CCF， which could be a differential diagnosis of swollen red eye， it also addresses the vital importance of physical ex-amination in modern medicine despite the seemingly promising technologies.

【3】Conclusions：

【4】Internists should have a low threshold of clinical suspicion for CCF in a patient with swollen red eyes in order to provide timely and proper management.

【5】MeSH Keywords： Carotid-Cavernous Sinus Fistula·Endovascular Procedures ·Exophthalmos·Orbital Cellulitis

【6】Carotid cavernous fistulas (CCF) are abnormal connections be-tween the carotid artery and cavernous sinus， which can be ei-ther direct (high flow) or indirect (low flow) communication. It may occur spontaneously or due to secondary causes. We re-port a case of right-sided direct CCF that could be a diagnos-tic challenge for internists.

【7】Case Report

【8】An 83-year-old female with hypertension and dyslipidemia presented to emergency depaitment (ED) with worsening pain and swelling over the right eye. A week ago， the patient visited the ED for the similar complaint without vision chang-es and she was discharged with a short course of oral pred-nisone for “allergic conjunctivitis". Back then， she recalled having right eye itching shortly after eating shrimp. Then the next morning， she woke with a swollen right eye and inabil-ity to open it. She denied any known history of food or drug allergy. At the present visit， the patient complained of right-sided blurred vision. Her vital signs were stable and physical examination showed chemosis and tenderness over the right orbit . Both pupils were equal and reactive. Visual acuity was 20/30 for both eyes with corrective lens. Because of severe chemosis，ophthalmoplegia was difficult to assess for the right eye. Otherwise， the examination was normal. Workup showed normal white count without left shift，erythrocyte sed-imentation rate， C reactive protein， ferritin and thyroid func-tion test (TFT). Computed tomography (CT)-orbits-sella showed pre-septal cellulitis without evidence of abscess. She was em-pirically treated with antibiotics (vancomycin and piperacillin-tazobactam) and topical o.2-adrenergic agonist (brimonidine). Ophthalmology was consulted.

【9】Despite empiric antibiotics， the patient did not show improve-ment on the following day. There continued to be no evidence of infection (no fever， leukocytosis). So， further imaging was pursued. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the brain was unremarkable. Additionally， MR-orbits， face and neck， showed right pre- and post-septal orbital cellulitis and enlarged right superior ophthalmic vein with concern for non-occlusive venous thrombosis . However， MR venogram (MRV) of the head showed no evidence of intracranial venous sinus throm-bosis. Additionally， MR angiogram (MRA) of the head showed normal circle of Willis. Further blood work including quantif-eron test， treponemal antibody test， thyrotropin receptor an-tibody， thyroid stimulating immunoglobulin (TSI)， rheumatoid factor (RF)， anti-neutrophil cytoplasmic antibody (ANCA)， and anti-nuclear antibody (ANA) were negative.

【10】On repeat examination of the eye， a bruit with palpable thrill was noted over the right eyeball. Tonometry readings were 38mm Hg and 22 mm Hg on right and left eyes respectively and visual acuity remained unchanged. Brominidine was stopped and topical brimonidine/timolol (combigan) was initiated. Given the orbital bruit/thrill and enlarged superior ophthalmic vein， CCF was suspected.Eventually， CTA of the head showed exten-sive arterial filling of the cavernous sinus and arterial opacifi-cation with bilateral superior ophthalmic veins， right greater than the left . Subsequently， carotid angiogram re-vealed early filling of the cavernous sinus and bilateral superi-or ophthalmic veins with more enlargement on the right than the left upon injection of the right internal carotid artery (ICA)， confirming the diagnosis of right-sided direct CCF . No filling of the cavernous sinus was seen on the injection of the left ICA. So， antibiotics were discontinued and endovascu-lar obliteration was planned. However， because of the tempo rary unavailability of neuro-interventionist at our facility， the patient was transferred to a tertiary facility for endovascular embolization of the right CCF. The patient tolerated the pro-cedure and follow-up at our facility within four weeks showed normal eye examination with stable vision.

【11】Discussion

【12】of the cavernous sinus with branches of the cavernous carot-id artery (Type B)， or dural branches of external carotid artery(Type C)， or both the branches of external and internal carot-id arteries (Type D) .

【13】Carotid cavernous fistulas (CCFs) are rare， abnormal connec-tions between the carotid artery and cavernous sinus， which can be either direct (high flow) or indirect (low flow) com-munication. Barrow et al. reported a classification of CCFs as follows： direct (high-flow) communication of the carotid ar-tery and cavernous sinus (Type A)， indirect communications

【14】The CCFs may occur spontaneously or following secondary causes (trauma， vascular aneurysm or malformations and ve-nous thrombosis). Direct CCFs are often caused by head trauma or rupture of intra-cavernous aneurysm or head surgery .

【15】There is limited data regarding the incidence of CCFs， either primary or secondary types. However， through retrospective analysis， Liang et al. reported that the overall incidence of trau-matic CCF was 3.8% among patients with basilar skull frac-tures . Sudden increase in pressure within the internal ca rotid artery (ICA) may be the mechanism for the development of direct CCF . Based on the different types， the presenta-tion of CCFs is high ly variable. Direct CCFs mostly present with orbital bruit (80%)， proptosis (72%)， chemosis (55%)， abdu-cens nerve palsy (49%)， and conjunctival injection (44%). Vision loss is one of the most fearful complications of CCFs. Sight threatening complications may occur in direct CCF due to severe exposure keratopathy， corneal ulcerations， and pos-sibly central retinal artery occlusion . Currently， no data is available for incidence of vision loss if the direct CCF is not properly and timely treated.

【16】Indirect CCFs often occur spontaneously and are more com-mon in older women . The cause of indirect CCFs is un-known and their presentations can vary widely by the patterns of venous drainage and the speed of blood flow. Indirect CCF especially of anterior drainage pattern may threaten the vi-sion through increased intraocular pressure (due to venous congestion) .

【17】The differential diagnoses of CCFs are cerebral aneurysms， vas-cular malformations of eyes， inflammation of orbits，retro-or-bital cellulitis， thyroid exophthalmos， retrobulbar hemorrhage， tumor of lacrimal gland， cavernous sinus thrombosis， and vas-culitis . CCFs may be suggested by clinical evaluation and imaging studies， especially MR-orbits and CTA or MRA of the head. However， the gold standard test for CCFs remains carot-id digital arteriography . Treatment decision depends on the severity of clinical presentations . Generally， treatment of CCFs is suggested if there are worsening visual function， se-vere proptosis， cranial nerve palsies， intractable bruit，intraoc-ular pressure of more than 25 mm Hg， and increased filling of cortical veins on angiography . The prognosis of CCFs is excellent after endovascular treatment .

【18】Our patient was initially treated with empiric antibiotics for suspected peri-orbital cellulitis， as noted clinically and in CT orbits. However， lack of clinical improvement， physical find-ing of orbital bruit/thrill， normal leukocytes and inflammatory markers， and enlarged superior ophthalmic vein in MR-orbits suggest alternate diagnoses. Vascular malformations and ve-nous thrombosis were unlikely given normal MRA and MRV respectively. Normal ANCA， ANA， RF， TFT， and TSl make vascu-litis and thyroid ophthalmopathy unlikely. Eventually， CTA and carotid-arteriography confirmed the diagnosis of right-sided direct CCF， which was subsequently treated with endovascu-lar embolization. It is likely that her direct CCF was related to a head trauma two years ago. The patient had no recurrent symptoms at regular follow-up at one and three months. Not only does this case highlight the importance of CCF， which could be a differential diagnosis of swollen red eye， it also ad-dresses the vital importance of physical examination in mod-ern medicine despite the seemingly promising technologies. We were able to provide the correct diagnosis and treatment for a potentially sight-threatening disease.

【19】Conclusions

【20】CCFs are rare potentially sight-threatening abnormal connec-tions between carotid artery and cavernous sinus. Clinicians should have a low threshold for investigation of CCF in a pa-tient with red swollen eyes in order to provide timely and proper management.

【0】Background： Cervical spine deformities can occur because of genetic， congenital， inflammatory degenerative， oriatrogenic causes.

【1】Case Report：

【2】We report a 45-year-old woman who presented to our clinic with complete paralysis of the left upper extrem-ity 5 months after C4-C6 discectomy and fusion surgery. The electrodiagnostic and EMG reports 3 months af-ter her previous surgery revealed left C5-C7 polyradiculopathy involving the upper trunk， lateral and posterior cords， and atrophy of the left deltoids， triceps， and biceps muscles. She underwent the following nerve transfer procedures with the senior author (RKN)： The median nerve fascicles were transferred to the biceps and bra-chialis branches of the musculocutaneous nerve. Radial nerve triceps branches were transferred to the deltoid and teres minor branches of the axillary nerve. The patient could fully abduct her left shoulder to 170°，and the LUE functions were restored to nearly normal 17 months after the surgery.

【3】Conclusions：

【4】Neurolysis combined with nerve transfer might be the most effective treatment for cervical spinal root inju-ries. Advances in peripheral nerve rewiring， transcranial magnetic stimulation， brain-computer interface robot-ic technologies， and emerging rehabilitation will undoubtedly increase the possibility of reviving the extremi-ties in patients with central pathology by restoring the descending motor signals through the residual neural network connections.

【5】Keywords： Cervical Spine Fusion Anomalies ·Brachial Plexus Neuropathies · Nerve Transfer·Range of Motion， Articular Cervical spine deformities can occur because of genetic， con-genital， inflammatory， degenerative， or iatrogenic causes. The most common single cause reported is postsurgical (iatrogen-ic) cervical spine injury . ACDF is an effective procedure to treat cervical spine diseases . However， spinal cord inju-ry (SCI)， nerve root impairment， and other complications have been reported following ACDF . Even the most experienced cervical spine surgeon with great care can inadvertently cause an iatrogenic cervical spine injury. Patient positioning， distrac-tor placement， amount or extent of decompression， type of in-strumentation， selection or placement of the bone graft， and use of postoperative immobilization are all suggested risks that may result in postoperative cervical spine deformity .

【6】The reported incidence of iatrogenic neurological injury rang-es from 3.2% to 0.3% after cervical spinal surgery . The C5 root is at a higher risk of iatrogenic injury because of its short course as it exits the spinal cord . C6 injuries can oc-cur simultaneously due to the proximity to the C5 root. C5-C6palsies are reported in 5-10% of patients after cervical spine surgery .

【7】Injury to C7-T1 or C8 and T1 roots is a rare occurrence in spine surgery， in which shoulder and elbow movements remain nor-mal， but weakness of the hand can occur . Despite its low incidence， iatrogenic neurological deterioration can cause se-vere functional limitations， such as complete loss of func-tional movements in this patient’s left upper extremity (LUE).

【8】Case Report

【9】We report the case of a 45-year-old woman who presented to us with complete paralys is of the LUE and 0° in shoulder ab duction 5 months after an anterior cervical discectomy and fu-sion (ACDF) surgery， specifically a C4-C6 discectomy and fusion.

【10】Three days before her ACDF surgery， the patient felt a sud-den onset of excruciating pain from the neck radiating into her left arm， and she came to the emergency room (ER) at 4AM the next day. An X-ray was taken and found no patholo-gy； she was discharged with pain medication. The patient lat-er received an MRl， revealing C4-C6 compression and nerve impingement. The patient underwent an ACDF procedure 3days after her ER visit. According to her previous medical re-cords，and her statement， she could not lift her left arm after waking up from the surgery. She was in the acute rehabilita-tion unit (ARU) for 1 week and received physical therapy for 3months. She had left shoulder abduction of 1/5 MRC and left elbow flexion of 0/5 MRC strength during her 3-month follow-up evaluation with the previous surgeon. However， her left wrist extension and flexion were 5/5 and her left-hand grip was 5/5. The surgeon referred her to a peripheral nerve spe-cialist for axillary nerve transfer.

【11】The patient contacted our clinic 3 months after her prior ACDF surgery， as her previous surgeon referred her to a peripheral nerve specialist. However， she visited our clinic 5 months after her pre-vious surgery. She stated she had difficulties in activities of dai-ly living. Her shoulder became dislocated regularly， and she was able to put it back in. She had multiple imaging (X-ray， MRl， and EMG) analyses before and 3 months after the ACDF and before nerve transfer surgeries. The electrodiagnostic report 3 months after the ACDF surgery revealed left C5-C7 polyradiculopathy in-volving the upper trunk and lateral and posterior cords. The EMG results 3 months after the previous surgery showed atrophy of the left deltoids， triceps， and biceps muscles， and she was un-able to activate these muscles volitionally. She reported having arm pain (7/10) but no neck pain pre-operatively.

【12】The patient has undergone the following surgeries with the se-nior author (RKN) 5 months after she had ACDF surgery at an-other hospital. The first nerve transfer was done with the trans-position of the 2 major fascicle groups of the median nerve to the biceps and brachialis branches of the musculocutaneous nerve. The second nerve transfer was done with the transpo-sition of radial nerve triceps branches (1 and 2) to the deltoid and teres minor branches of the axillary nerve. The appropri-ate nerves in the surgery (median， radial， and axillary nerves) were neurolyzed. Additionally， latissimus dorsi and teres ma-ior muscle contractures were released.

【13】The patient was brought to the operating room， where she underwent general anesthesia. The left arm and chest were prepped and draped in the usual sterile fashion. An incision was created immediately parallel to the scapular border in the lateral chest. Contractures of the latissimus and teres major were released. The superomedial border of the triceps was dis-sected and found the axillary nerve.

【14】The neurological changes during the surgery were monitored. A free-running EMG was performed to test the motor system's integrity and nerve/root irritability. A continuous electroen-cephalogram (EEG) was monitored via a modified 10-20 mon-tage throughout the procedure to monitor the cortical function and depth of anesthesia. Stimulated EMG was used to identi-fy neural structures， and CMAP responses were communicat-ed to the surgeon (RKN). There were no CMAP responses in the axillary nerve to the deltoid， and in the musculocutane-ous to the biceps and brachialis at 5mA. The radial nerve was dissected in the roof of the axilla and identified as a triceps branch. Through external and internal neurolysis，the branch was found to have 2 terminal ends， and each was separately dissected for use as axillary nerve donors.

【16】The axillary nerve underwent external and internal neurolysis to separate its 2 motor branches. One terminal end of the radial tri-ceps branch was sutured to the deltoid branch and the other to the teres minor branch using a 9-0 nylon microsuture. Through a new proximal medial arm incision， the branches of the brachi-al plexus were able to be accessed. The left ulnar F-waves were absent. The median nerve had good electrical continuity and un-derwent external and internal neurolysis. The musculocutaneous nerve was identified within the substance of the biceps muscle， and it had zero electrical conductivity in the brachialis or biceps branch. At this time， 2 group fascicles of the median nerve were dissected free with a Jacobsen hemostat and then transected.The distal end of one group fascicle was transposed and sutured to the musculocutaneous branch of the brachialis. The second group fascicle was then sutured to the branch of the biceps muscle.

【17】All procedures were done with meticulous microsurgical tech-niques and under high magnification. All wounds were closed， and Dermabond was applied. The patient was stable and awake without problems after surgery.

【18】She was instructed to use a sling for 3 weeks， followed by reg-ular therapy. Physical therapy was prescribed 5 times weekly for 3 months and included teaching home exercises. Protocols for managing complex regional pain syndrome (CRPS) were also provided.

【19】Discussion

【20】Distal nerve transfers are a powerful treatment option for proxi-mal nerve injuries. Addressing nerve root injuries in the context of severe cervical spinal cord injuries resulting in complete pa-ralysis of the extremities has been challenging. Distal-targeted nerve transfers have been successfully performed as a preferred alternative to the site of a proximal injury  since the re-generation distance will be much shorter and， therefore， the recovery will be faster. Additionally， in cases of iatrogenic sur-gical injuries at the proximal cervical spinal level (ACDF)， as in the present case report， the distal operative area will have no scarring from previous surgeries， allowing for technical preci-sion in reconstructive efforts.

【21】The meta-analysis article by Makel et al  summarized the results of 15 articles on distal nerve transfer for brachi-al plexus injury. They compared the effectiveness of the radi-al nerve transfer to the intercostal nerve. The best outcome reported was a mean ROM of 106° with the radial nerve Vs80° with the intercostal nerve. Of the 15 included study re-ports， the best outcome with an average of 134° ROM was from 2 of the 5 patients in the study by Uerpairojkit et al . Uerpairojkit et al  used the spinal accessory and the radi-al nerve to the long head of the triceps. The intercostal nerve transfer is performed in cases of total brachial plexus injury or involvement of the C7 root . The disadvantages of intercostal nerve transfers are the need for extensive prepa-ration for harvesting them and the risk of iatrogenic pneumo-thorax . The contralateral C7 nerve root transfer is an al-ternative for pan-plexus injuries. Despite higher axon content for use， the reported outcomes have been inconsistent， with common complications18.

【22】Malungpaishrope et al  showed that shoulder abduction improved to 71° after the simultaneous transfer of the spinal accessory nerve (SAN) and intercostal nerves to supraspinatus and triceps muscles， respectively. Chuieng-Yi Lu et al  report-ed that the maximum degrees of shoulder abduction achieved was 61.9±38.7° in patients with phrenic and 51.1±37.3°with SAN nerve transfers. The phrenic nerve is an alternative for shoulder or elbow reanimation in patients with limited donor options. In a case-control study， Maldonado et al  compared2 groups of patients (axillary nerve injury or brachial plexus inju-ry). These 2 groups achieved 52+69° of shoulder abduction (suc-cessful group) and 27±30° (failure group) after the triceps mo-tor branch transfer to the anterior division of the axillary nerve.

【23】Songet al  compared the results of ipsilateral C7 (IC7) plus SAN transfers with those of triple nerve transfers (TNT)， which involved transferring the long head of the triceps nerve branch to the anterior branch of the axillary nerve and transferring one fascicle of the ulnar nerve to the biceps motor branch . Their patients achieved an average of 105° (IC7 plus SAN) and89° (TNT) in shoulder abduction . Fasce et al  showed a mean of 135° in shoulder abduction with triple nerve trans-fers. In comparison to recently reported double nerve transfer procedures to reanimate shoulder abduction  or elbow flexion ， as well as triple or multiple nerve transfers ， our surgical outcome (double nerve transfers with neurolysis and muscle contracture release) was more effective， as it re-stored all UE functional movements (shoulder abduction and elbow flexion) to nearly normal .

【24】Better outcomes have been shown when surgeries are per-formed at less than 6 months (before developing significant muscular atrophy and fibrosis)， as the reinnervation possibil-ities are greater. Fasce et al  reported that patients under age 25 years have better outcomes due to their higher regen-erative capability. Solla et al  reported that older patients had worse outcomes. However， our patient was older (45 years) but still achieved all UE functions 17 months after the nerve transfer surgery， as she had external and internal neurolysis of the involved nerve fascicles and release of muscle contrac-tures. Additionally， she had surgeries within 5 months after her iatrogenic injury. Neurolysis can provide excellent to good out-comes， as shown recently in 82% of the 73 Serratus anterior palsy patients . Neurolysis during nerve transfer surgery re-mains the best treatment for spinal root avulsion injuries .

【25】Solla et al  reported that their patients shoulder abduc-tion improvements were excellent (>60°) and good (>40°) af-ter SAN to SSN， whether they were associated with axillary nerve reconstruction strategies or not， respectively. Four pa-tients who had SAN to SSN combined with radial to axillary nerve transfer demonstrated a statistically significant increase in the range of abduction (median， 90° vs 42.5°， respective-ly) compared with those who had SAN to SSN transfer alone. Improvements in shoulder abduction after SAN to SSN trans-fer are comparatively smaller . The supraspinatus is not recruited earlier， as commonly believed， but was found to be recruited consistently with many other shoulder muscles， including the deltoid， and work synergistically in abducting the shoulder . The SAN to SSN transfer also failed to pro-vide useful recovery of external rotation . Moreover， the transfer of SAN to SSN via the traditional supraclavicular an-terior approach often leads to partial denervation of the tra-pezius muscle .

【26】Conclusions

【27】Neurolysis combined with nerve transfer might be the most ef-fective treatment for cervical spinal root injuries. Advances in peripheral nerve rewiring， transcranial magnetic stimulation， brain-computer interface robotic technologies， and emerging rehabilitation will undoubtedly increase the possibility of re-viving the extremities in patients with central pathology such as hemiplegia or stroke by restoring the descending motor sig-nals through the residual neural network connections.

【0】Background：

【1】Intravesical administration of Bacillus Calmette-Guerin (B CG) has been used effectively for treatment of superficial carcinoma of the bladder. Although well tolerated in the majority of patients adverse local and systemic side effects have been described.

【2】Case Report：

【3】We report the case of a 58 year old man who developed granulomatous prostatitis and interstitial pneumonitis following intravesical instillation of B CG for recurrent superficial bladder cancer. Prostate biopsies showed tuberculoid granulomatous inflammation， whereas mycobacterial cultures of sputum were negative. A high resolution computed tomography scan revealed interstitial fibrosis with reticular pattern. The patient received antituberculous treatment and corticosteroids with complete remission.

【4】Concluslons：

【5】This was a rare presentation of granulomatous prostatitis and interstitial pneumonitis following immunotherapy with BCG. Both a hypersensitivity reaction and an infection mechanism should be considered in this particular case.

【6】Key words： BCG vacclne ·bladder neoplasms · prostatltls · pneumonltls Intravesical Bacillus Calmette-Guerin (BCG) is an attenuated strain of Mycobacterium bovis that has been used effectively in the treatment of patients with superficial bladder cancer. BCG has been shown to eradicate residual tumour in more than 60% of patients with papillary disease and in over 70% of patients with carcinoma in situ . The intravesical instillation of BCG induces local as well as systemic immunological response that is required to effectively eradicate cancer cells . Although the majority of the patients tolerate BCG intravesical treatment well， anumber ofadverse effects have been described. Patients usually experience low grade fever， dysuria， heamaturia and malaise. More serious complications include granulomatous prostatitis， pneumonitis and hepatitis and sepsis. We report a case of granuloma-tous prostatitis and interstitial pneumonitis following intravesical BCG instillation that required antiturb-erculous treatment and corticosteroids for cure.

【7】CASE REPORT

【8】A 58-year old， non-smoking， immunocompetent man was referred to our clinic for assessment of granulomatous prostatitis. Eight years previously he was diagnosed with papillary tumour of the bladder for which he underwent transurethral resection and received chemotherapy with complete remission. Five years later the patient presented with hematuria and repeated cystoscopy with bladder biopsy showed recurrence of carcinoma in situ. The patient was then treated with suspensions of 81 mg of BCG in50 ml of saline instilled into the bladder at 6 weekly intervals. After the sixth dosage he developed night fevers (39°C) and polyarthralgia. His erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) was 74 mm/h， C-reactive protein (CRP) was positive and was noted to have slightly elevated Prostatic Specific Antigen (PSA) of 4.3 ng/ml (normal values 0-4 ng/ml). Transrectal ultrasound of the prostate demonstrated a 2.1x0.7 cm hypoechoCIIlic lesion in the right zone. Prostate biopsies revealed chronic inflammatory infiltration with formation of tuberculoid granulomatous struc-tures .

【9】Upon physical examination he had bibasilar inspira tory rales， whereas all other systems were normal. His family history was negative for cancer or other chronic conditions， whereas from his past medical history the only thing of interest was an operation performed ten years previously for a left varicocele. Routine blood tests and thyroid function tests were normal. His oxygen saturation (SaO2) was 97%. Mantoux test was performed with positive result (20 mm). Mycobacterial cultures of sputum and urine were negative. A bronchoscopy with trans-bronchial lung biopsy and bronchoalveolar lavage(BAL) demonstrated lymphocytosis and activated T helper cells (33%). Biopsy specimen revealed areas of interstitial inflammatory infiltration . Cytology specimens were negative for tumour and cultures for fungi and acid fast bacilli were also n亡ga-tive. Pulmonary function tests (PFT) with diffusion were normal. Chest radiography displayed peripheral microreticulonodular opacities in the middle and lower lung fields. A chest high resolution computed tomography (CT chest HR) scan identified areas with interstitial fibrosis . CT scan of abdomen was normal and gallium citrate scan was negative for active lung disease.

【10】The patient was started on aregimen of oral rifam-picin (600 mg daily)， isoniazid (300 mg daily) and ethambutol (1200 mg daily) for two months and continued rifampicin and isoniazid to complete a six-month course， but refused to start corticoste-roids. One month after the beginning of antituber-culous treatment the urologists repeated intravesi-cal treatment with BCG at three monthly intervals. Six months later the patient underwent transrectal ultrasound of prostate that was normal with disap-pearance ofthe right side lesion whereas cystoscopy revealed no signs of relapse. The patient remained well until five months later when he visited our clinic again complaining of gradually worsening dyspnoea on exertion. A marked decrease in diffu-sion (Dco=71.5%) was noted but a new CT chest HR showed no significant changes compared to the previous one. The patient still declined treat-ment with corticosteroids. Four months later， his dyspnoea was much worse and the patient revisited our clinic. A new PFT revealed a further decrease in diffusion (Dco=67.6%). A repeated CT chest HR showed worsening compared to the previous one， with appearance of honeycomblung in all lung fields and bronchiectasic areas in the middle lobe. the lingula and the upper parts of the lower lobes. The patient finally agreed to begin treatment and he was started 40 mg prednisone daily with complete resolution of dyspnoea. Two months later a new CT chest HR was markedly improved and a repeated PFT showed increase in diffusion (Dco= 83.4%). The patient remains well and is now on 20 mg pred-nisone daily.

【11】DISCUSSION

【12】Immunotherapy with intravesicular BCG for patients with superficial transitional carcinoma ofthe bladder is associated with side effects of moderate severity that are generally well tolerated. In the multi-center series reported by Lamm et al  granuloma-tous prostatitis was observed in 1.3% of the patients whereas serious complications defined as hepatitis or pneumonitis occurred in 0.9% with affected patients presenting with fever， chills， night sweats， malaise， dyspnoea and cough. Local side effects occur either as an inflammatory reaction to BCG instillation or due to an infection secondary to contact with BCG contaminated urine 

【13】In this report， we describe a case in which a patient treated with intravesical BCG because of transitional cell carcinoma of the bladder developed prostatic tuberculosis and interstitial pneumonitis. In granu-lomatous prostatitis PSA levels are often elevated and ultrasound typically shows diffuse hypoechoic areas . This was the case in our patient， with tuber-culoid granulomas on prostate biopsy confirming that attenuated mycobacteria are the causative factor for these lesions.

【14】Concerning the pulmonary involvement， it is un-settled whether a hypersensitivity reaction due to BCG antigens or an actual pulmonary infection due to haematogenous spread of mycobacteria provokes lung reaction . There is in fact some consensus that both mechanisms play a role . According to some authors， the reticulonodular opacities on chest radiographs， lymphocytosis on BAL with elevated T一AT T4/T8 ratio on BAL， the detection of interstitial pneumonitis on lung biopsy， a favourable response to corticosteroids in selected patients and the ab-sence of granulomatous inflammation on the lung biopsy specimens are regarded as the main features of pulmonary localization of hypersensitivity reactionFor this reason， recommended treatment for patients with M.bovis infections in the acute setting is a combination of isoniazid plus rifampicin for three to six months with the addition of prednisone 40 mg daily .

【15】Although an actual infectious process cannot be excluded regarding the pulmonary involvement in our patient， we have evidence for a hypersensitiv-ity reaction. The findings on CT chest HR were consistent with diffuse interstitial pneumonitis and mycobacterial cultures were negative. In addition， increased activated alveolar lymphocytes on BAL analysis and the rapid recovery of the patient with corticosteroids are also suggestive of a hypersensi-tivity mechanism.

【16】CONCLUSIONS

【17】In conclusion， we have reported an interesting case of granulomatous prostatitis following intravesical BCG therapy. The patient received antituberculous treat-ment for his prostatitis with full recovery. However， during antituberculous treatment he developed in-terstitial pneumonitis. In this regard， corticosteroids appear to be the appropriate treatment as was in our patient.

【0】Background：

【1】Drug induced lupus erythematosus is considered an autoimmune entity which is precipitated by medications. Hydrochlorothiazide has been recognized to cause subacute cutaneous lupus erythematosus， but very few cases of systemic drug induced lupus systemic erythematosus have been reported.

【2】Case Report：

【3】A 57-year-old Caucasian male with a past medical history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia presented with recurrent fevers， chest pain， and dyspnea. Initial evaluation revealed diffuse ST elevations， small pericardial ef-fusion， anemia， and leukopenia. He was initially treated with nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs and pred-nisone for pericarditis. Six months later， he reported fatigue， arthralgias， morning stiffness， weight loss， fevers， and night sweats. Laboratory tests revealed persistent anemia and leukopenia. Extensive workup， including bone marrow biopsy and infectious evaluations， was negative. Autoimmune workup， however， revealed pos-itive antihistone and antichromatin antibodies despite negative antinuclear antibody. A diagnosis of drug in-duced lupus secondary to hydrochlorothiazide was made. The medication was stopped， and prednisone was initiated resulting in marked improvement in his symptoms and hematologic abnormalities.

【4】Conclusions：

【5】This report is one of the few known cases of systemic lupus erythematosus most likely induced by hydrochlo-rothiazide. Based on our finding， hydrochlorothiazide should be considered a possible offending agent when a patient presents with symptoms suspicious of drug induced lupus.

【6】MeSH Keywords： Abnormalities， Drug-Induced·Hydrochlorothiazide · Lupus Erythematosus， Systemic Drug induced lupus erythematosus (DILE) is a rare， lupus-like syndrome which is caused by offending medications in patients with no prior history of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). Symptoms and laboratory results mimic those of SLE. There are no formal diagnostic criteria for DILE， but it is widely accepted that symptoms should start after initiation or modification of a medication and resolve after cessation of that agent . Certain serological findings such as positive antinuclear anti-body (ANA)， antihistone antibody， and antichromatin antibody are also seen . The pathogenesis is thought to be mul-tifactorial. Treatment is usually limited to cessation of the of-fending medication with resolution of symptoms. To date， over80 medications have been associated with DILE . Notable agents include procainamide， hydralazine， tumor necrosis fac-tor inhibitors， isoniazid， and methyldopa . Although hy-drochlorothiazide is considered as a“possible”agent which causes DILE， very few cases have been described in literature. Herein， we report a case of hydrochlorothiazide-induced DILE with new onset pericarditis and severe inflammatory arthritis， leukopenia， neutropenia， repeatedly negative ANA， but strongly positive antihistone and antichromatin antibodies.

【7】Case Report

【8】A 57-year-old male presented to the Emergency Department with sudden onset of severe substernal chest pain. The pain was intermittent， non-radiating， worsened by exertion， and im-proved with rest and aspirin. One week prior to presentation he reported occasional shortness of breath and a fever of 38.3℃(101°F) which resolved. Past medical history included hyper-tension and hyperlipidemia. He had no surgeries in the past. Current medications were losartan 100 mg daily， hydrochloro-thiazide 25 mg daily (started 15 years prior)， aspirin 81 mg daily and atorvastatin 20 mg daily. There were no recent dose adjust-ments or new medications. Family history was nonsignificant. He denied tobacco， alcohol， or illicit drug use. Vitals on admis-sion were blood pressure 105/58 mmHg， pulse 81 beats/min， temp 36.5℃ (97.7°F)， respiratory rate 20 breaths/min， SpO299% on room air and body mass index (BMI) 30.68 kg/m2. His physical examination was within normal limits.

【9】Electrocardiogram (ECG) showed diffuse ST elevations. Laboratory tests showed anemia， leukopenia， and elevated inflammatory markers. Peripheral blood smear showed leuko-penia with absolute neutropenia， microcytosis， and anisocytosis with normal platelets. ANA screen by immunofluorescence and titer was negative. Echocardiogram showed normal left ventricular size and systolic function with ejection fraction of55-60%.A small circumferential pericardial effusion was noted without evidence of cardiac tamponade. Chest x-ray (CXR) was unremarkable and troponin was negative. Two sets of blood cultures showed no growth.

【10】The patient was initially treated with aspirin and nitroglycerin for presumed acute coronary syndrome. He was seen by the in terventional cardiologist and underwent coronary angiography which showed normal coronaries with preserved ejection frac-tion. Because of the small pericardial effusion and diffuse ST elevations in ECG， he was started on nonsteroidal anti-inflam-matory drugs and steroids for pericarditis. On day 2， he de-veloped asymptomatic atrial fibrillation and was started on a diltiazem drip. Gastroenterology was consulted for the micro-cytic anemia and recommended outpatient colonoscopy. The patient's last colonoscopy was 5 years prior and showed 1 tu-bular adenomatous polyp in the ascending colon with the rec-ommendation for follow-up endoscopies. In addition， patient was seen by hematology/oncology for the anemia and leuko-penia who recommended bone marrow biopsy if the blood counts did not improve in a few weeks. Patient improved symptomatically with steroids and was discharged home with a 5-day steroid taper， diltiazem， nebivolol and his home med-ications were resumed.

【11】Five days after discharge， the patient was admitted again with recurrent chest pain. Repeat echocardiogram showed small/moderate pericardial effusion suggestive of recurrent pericar-ditis which was presumed to be from premature cessation of steroids. Laboratory tests revealed persistent anemia and ele-vated inflammatory markers. He was discharged home on pred-nisone 30 mg daily for 2 weeks and colchicine 0.6 mg twice daily. Two weeks after discharge， he followed up with his car-diologist who proceeded with a slow prednisone taper over4 weeks (20 mg daily for 2 weeks followed by 10 mg daily for2 weeks). Repeat C-reactive protein (CRP) was checked to as sess response and remained elevated. His colchicine was con-tinued for 3 months.

【12】Six months following initial presentation， he presented to his primary care physician with complaints of fever， fatigue， joint pain and swelling， morning stiffness， unintentional 40-pound weight loss， loss of appetite， low grade fevers， night sweats， and shortness of breath. Physical examination revealed swelling of bilateral metacarpophalangeal (MCP) and proximal interpha-langeal joints (PIP). Range of motion in his joints was severely reduced. Repeat laboratory tests showed anemia and leuko-penia with persistent severe neutropenia . ECG showed sinus rhythm. He was referred to oncology with concern for malignancy and admitted for further workup.

【13】Given the constellation of symptoms of malaise， weight loss， loss of appetite， low grade fever， joint pains， anemia，leuko-penia， and neutropenia， the differential diagnosis was broad.
