【69】1.1 Laser-activated irrigation： Laser-activated irrigation consists of a combination of the chemical action of the irrigant and laser irradiation. The 4 studies included in this review reported the improved antibacterial ac-tivity of sodium hypochlorite when activated with Diode， Er： YAG and Er， Cr： YSGG. This agrees with the study's results by Preethee et al. ， who achieved100% complete disinfection of bacteria using 908nm diode laser irradiation followed by root canal irriga-tion with 0.5% NaOCl and 17% EDTA. In addition， Neelakantan et al.  also showed effective eradica-tion of bacterial biofilm by Er： YAG laser activation with a PIPS system compared to conventional syringe irrigation. This antimicrobial effect is explained by the cavitation effect induced by the physical mechanism of laser-activated irrigation. Indeed， the activation of the laser in an aqueous environment generates large bubbles that expand and then explode； this expan-sion causes a high pressure that pushes the fluid into the deep dentinal tubules and kills the bacteria . Compared to direct laser irradiation， laser-activated irrigation gives a better bactericidal effect because the latter includes photoacoustic activation in addition to thermal effects . Moreover， erbiums combined with sodium hypochlorite give a superior bactericidal effect to conventional irrigation with NaOCl and di-rect irradiation with Nd： YAG，Nd： YAP and diode laser.

【70】1.2 Photoactivated disinfection： The mechanism of action of photodynamic therapy (PDT) or photoactivated dis-infection consists of the destruction of bacterial mem-branes by cytotoxic species released upon activation of the photosensitizer by laser energy . This photo-active therapy with a diode laser effectively eradicates bacteria and gives better results than conventional ir-rigation in eliminating E. Faecalis . Therefore， photodynamic therapy is a promising approach in root canal disinfection.

【71】2\. Postoperative endodontic pain Reducing postoperative pain after conventional endodontic treatment is a challenge for dentists， and its management by laser has been exten-sively researched：

【72】2.1 Conventional laser-assisted endodontics： Er： YAG-activated irrigation using the PIPS protocol reduces postoperative pain due to the low risk of irrigant ex-trusion caused by the low intracanal pressures gener-ated during laser-activated irrigation not exceeding the central venous pressure of 5.88 mm Hg (thus not exceeding the apical tissue pressure) . Diode and Nd： YAG irradiation results in lower pain levels than conventional root canal treatment J.Kaplan et al.  also reported significantly less pain at 24 and48 hours in the DIODE group compared to the con-ventional treatment group. This could be attributed to the sedative effect of Nd： YAG at 1440 mm on the peri-odontal ligament's peripheral C-fibres， and the diode lasers' strong antibacterial effect .

【73】2.2 Photodynamic therapy： Photodynamic therapy (PDT) has less postoperative pain at 24- and 72-hour inter-vals compared with conventional irrigation. This could be explained by the antimicrobial action of PDT being more effective compared to NaOCl irrigation alone， which should therefore result in less extrusion of bacterial residues and less pain perception.

【74】2.3 Low-level laser therapy LLLT： LLLT may be an ef-fective alternative to using NSAIDs to control post-endodontic pain . The analgesic effects of this therapy explain this result；low-level laser stimulation inhibits the release of mediators from injured tissues， decreases the concentration of chemical agents such as histamine， acetylcholine， serotonin， H+ and K+， all of which are pain mediators， also inhibits the concentra-tion of acetylcholine， causes vasodilatation and finally thanks to its electromagnetic energy the metabolism of the injured tissues is increased .

【75】3\. Smear layer elimination and debris removal The studies included in our review  have shown that laser-activated irrigation techniques effectively remove dentin sludge due to the cavitation effect . Maximum efficiency is obtained with NaOC1+EDTA activated with Er： YAG and Er， Cr： YSGG . No significant difference was detected between these two lasers. However， Er： YAG using the PIPS protocol shows a higher efficiency than Er， Cr： YSGG due to the shock wave effect induced by the PIPS proto-col with secondary cavitation . Regarding root canal debris removal， activation of the irrigant with Er： YAG at2940nm and Diode at 980nm significantly improves debris removal in the root canal compared to conventional irriga-tion . Indeed，laser-activated irrigation has a more powerful activating effect， a violent fluid dynamic caused by the expansion and explosion of bubbles near the laser fibre tip .

【76】4\. Sealer penetration in dentinal tubules Hermetic sealing with a biocompatible material is another key objective of root canal treatment after proper chemomechanical preparation. The obturation materials must provide a root seal which can be achieved by penetration of root canal cement into the dentinal tubules. The results of the study by Akcay et al.  and Gu et al.  showed that activation of the irrigant by Er： YAG and Nd： YAP achieves higher pene-tration of the root canal sealing cement into the dentinal tubules compared to conventional irrigation. Furthermore， the penetration depth of root canal cement is improved with DIODE and Nd： YAG . The implosion of the vapour bubbles generated at the end of the fibres and the shock wave effects of the laser explain the high penetration into the dentinal tubules.

【77】5\. Pulp capping Lasers have become increasingly popular in direct pulp capping treatment . This can be explained by：

【78】1\. Their ability to stimulate cell proliferation， activate dentin protein gene expression and accelerate the dif-ferentiation of pulp cells into functional odontoblasts.

【79】2\. An excellent capacity to ablate soft and hard tissues.

【80】3\. Effective healing potential by forming a dentine bridge and repairing dentine.

【81】4\. Finally， their hemostatic， bactericidal， and coagulant effects.

【82】All types of laser evaluated in this review improved the prog-nosis of direct pulp capping compared to treatment assisted by conventional capping agents. Indeed， the success rate was significantly different between the conventional group (a resin modified glass ionomer cement) 60%， and the 808 nm diode-assisted group (100%) . This high success rate of laser treat-ment is attributable to their biostimulation， decontamination， hemostatic and coagulant effects. Erbiums have excellent soft and hard tissue ablation capability with minimal thermal effects， as they can be efficiently absorbed by water molecules and hy-droxyapatite， unlike diodes， which are primarily used for soft tissue surgery and are not effective for hard tissue ablation .

【83】Conclusion

【84】This study aimed to review previously published studies and evaluate the efficacy of the laser in endodontics. The selected studies varied widely in terms of laser parameters， specimen preparation and analytical methods used. Nevertheless， the re-sults showed that the use of the laser significantly improved disinfection and removal of dentinal sludge in the root canal system， penetration of sealing materials into the dentinal tubules and the prognosis of direct pulp capping. In addition， using a laser with appropriate parameters can be proposed as a treat-ment modality to manage post-endodontic pain. However， most of the studies are performed in vitro， which does not allow meaningful conclusions to be drawn. Further， in vivo studies are needed to validate the utility of lasers as an innovative tech-nology in modern endodontics.

【0】Background：

【1】Malignant melanoma is the most commen cancer to metastasize to the gastrointestinal tract. Only2-4% of patients with melanoma will be diagnosed with gastrointestinal metastasis during the course of their disease. Gallbladder metastasis is rarely the first site of recurrence (ca. 15% of all gastro-in testinal metastases) and is associated with a very poor prognosis.

【2】Case Report：

【3】The case of a 53-year-old man with a metastatic gallbladder melanoma is reported who presented with a clinical history of symptoms that mimicked chronic cholecystitis with epigastric and right hypochondrial pain until the development of acute cholecystitis.

【4】Conclusions：

【5】This case emphasizes the need for awareness of the possibility of gallbladder involvement in mel-anoma patients and underlines the necessity of meticulous investigation of unclear lesions of the gallbladder and biliary tree in patients with a past history of malignant melanoma.

【6】key words： gallbladder· malignant melanoma · metastasis

【7】BACKGROUND

【8】Malignant melanoma is an aggressive tumor with a pro-nounced tendency for distant metastases to numerous GI-gans. Only 2 to 4% of patients with melanoma will be di-agnosed with gastrointestinal metastasis during the course of their disease. The most common sites of gastrointesti-nal metastases of melanoma include the small bowel (35-67%)， colon (9-15%)， and stomach (5-7%)， with a medi-an survival of 6-10 months after surgery and 18% survival at five years. Brasfield et al. found gastrointestinal metasta-ses in more than 50% of 125 patients dying from dissemi-nated malignant melanoma. Both primary and metastatic melanoma of the gallbladder are rare. Involvement of the gallbladder occurs in about 15% of all gastrointestinal met-astatic locations in post-mortem case records .The ma-jority of patients were in the fourth or fifth decade of life at the time of diagnosis . We report the case of a patient with melanoma of the abdomen developing in the course of metastatic involvement of the gallbladder as the first site of recurrence， with symptoms of acute cholecystitis treated by open cholecystectomy.

【9】CASE REPORT

【10】A 53-year-old man presented with an atypical pigmented le-sion on the left side of his abdomen and a presumptive di-agnosis of melanoma was made. The lesion was excised in2002 and revealed malignant melanoma， superficial spread-ing type， invasive to Clark's anatomical level II and to a mea-sured depth of 1.6 mm. Preoperative staging with chest X-ray and abdominal ultrasound did not reveal signs of systematic disease. The patient was submitted to regular follow-up ev-ery three months with physical examination and X-ray and abdominal ultrasound in first two years of observation and every six months after that.

【11】Seventy-two months after the primary melanoma excision he presented with a six-week history of progressive epigas-tric pain with radiation to the mid-chest and nausea. On examination the patient was febrile and there was tender-ness on palpation of the epigastrium and right upper quad-rant of the abdomen. His pain was unrelated to food intake. Blood values and liver function tests were normal. The pa-tient was admitted to the Department of General Surgery in Rybnik in November 2008 as an acute cholecystitis case. Abdominal ultrasound showed hyperdistension of the gall-bladder wall， with diffuse， hyperechoic content interpret-ed as being consistent with acute cholecystitis. A comput-erized tomographic (CT) scan of the abdomen confirmed hyperdistension of the gallbladder wall， which was filled with a solid pathological mass. CT of the pelvis and chest were negative for metastatic disease.

【12】The

【13】Ppatient underwent open cholecystectomy. Intraoperatively， the gallbladder was noted to be acutely inflamed and thickened， measuring 9x5.5×3 cm. On opening the resected gallbladder， the mucosa was rough-ened and numerous grey-black lesions projected into the lumen . Histologically， malignant tumor was present， invading through the gallbladder wall and extend-ing up into the lamina propria. Necrotic tissue and malig-nant tumor were also present in the gallbladder lumen. Immunohistochemical examination confinmed the diagnosis of metastatic melanoma of the gallbladder. Postoperatively， the patient’s course was uncomplicated， and he was dis-charged home. No adjuvant chemotherapy was offered at this time by our oncologists.

【14】Three months later， abdominal ultrasound examination showed metastatic lymph nodes in the mesentery and peri-toneum. Eight months after the cholecystectomy， the pa-tient was urgently readmitted to the neurological depart-ment because of unexpected loss of consciousness with severe hypotension. A CT scan of the brain showed the presence of alarge metastasis 6 cm in diameter in the fron-tal right cerebral lobe. Lumbar puncture showed he had neoplastic meningitis with melanoma cells in the cerebro-spinal fluid. Physical examination showed the presence of multiple cutaneous and subcutaneous nodules on the ab-domen wall and back. One week later the patient died of widespread disease.

【15】DISCUSSION

【16】Malignant melanoma can metastasize to almost any organ. The most common initial sites of distant metastases from cu-taneous melanoma are the skin and subcutaneous tissue and， less frequently， the brain， lung， and gastrointestinal tract. Metastatic melanoma of the gallbladder， although rare， ac-counts for over 50% of tumor metastases found in this organ. Furthermore， autopsy reports have shown that 15% of patients with gastrointestinal metastases also have gallbladder metastases . The majority of primary melanomas metas-tasizing to the gallbladder arise from the skin， but the prima-ry lesion can also occur at other sites where melanin-contain-ing cells are present， such as the oral cavity， anus， urethra， and vagina . The time interval between the diagnosis of the primary lesion and gallbladder metastasis ranges from a few months to 13 years . In our case it was 72 months. The median age of patients at initial presentation with gall-bladder disease is 45-50 years . The most common pre-sentation of gallbladder metastatic melanoma is cholecystitis with or without cholelithiasis， likely due to obstruction of the cystic duct by the tumor mass . Other reported symp toms and signs of gallbladder metastatic disease were weight loss， food intolerance， nausea， vomiting， and diarrhea .

【17】Most patients show gallbladder involvement as part of wide-spread disease， with few patients having the first metastasis limited to the gallbladder . This was the case in our pa-tient， who had a long history of symptoms that mimicked cholecystitis. The mortality of melanoma metastasis to the gastroinestinal tract is dismal， with a median survival of6-10months after detection . Our patient developed wide-spread disease and died eight months after the diagnosis of gallbladder metastasis. The treatment options in metastatic cases depend on the extent of the disease and the clinical status of the patient. Although surgical management is of ten possible， complete excision of tumor metastases is feasi-ble only in about one third of patients . The role of cho-lecystectomy is not well defined in an asymptomatic patient. There are reports in the literature of prolonged survival af-ter resection of isolated metastatic disease to the gallbladder， as well as the liver  and lung .Ostik and Haqqani  described a patient who benefited from complete excision of her gallbladder metastases， remaining disease-free one year after surgery. Our patient survived over80 months after his initial diagnosis of Clark’s stage II mel-anoma and 8 months after cholecystectomy. Dong et al. re-ported a 12-month survival rate of 100% (n=6) in patients whose tumors were amenable to complete resection， with two patients living nine years after their initial diagnoses .

【18】Surgical excision， when feasible， appears to be the key to a good outcome. The role of adjuvant therapy remains unde-fined. The presence of multiple metastases frequently lim-its the treatment options available， with the majority of pa-tients requiring systematic chemotherapy， which is so for of limited efficacy .

【19】CONCLUSIONS

【20】We reported this case to emphasize the need for aware-ness of the possibility of gallbladder involvement in mel-anoma patients and to underline the necessity of metic-ulous investigation of unclear lesions of the gallbladder and biliary tree in patients with a past history of malig-nant melanoma.

【0】Background：

【1】Serous cystic pancreatic tumours are unique among all pancreatic cystic neoplasms in that they are almost always benign and the diagnostic challenge for the surgical pathologist is to recognise the spectrum of architectural variations that may lead to misdiagnosis either pre or postoperatively. They are more frequently identified as the imaging techniques improve in time.

【2】Case Report：

【3】We present two cases of pancreatic serous microcystic adenoma both of which were diagnosed incidentally during clinical and radiologic evaluations for unrelated reasons.The first patient referred to the clinic with epigastric pain and nausea. During clinical evaluation a cystic mass in distal pancreas was noted. Second patient had two cystic lesions in liver and one cystic lesion in the pancreatic head which were considered as consistent with hydatid cysts by radiologists. Distal and proximal pancreatectomies were performed for the first and second patient respectively. Histopathologic diagnosis of the specimens was serous microcystic adenoma of pancreas.

【4】Conclusions：

【5】Despite their rarity， serous cystadenomas should be kept in mind by pathologists and radiologists in the differential diagnosis of the cystic neoplasms of pancreas.

【6】Key words： Pancreas · serous microcystic adenoma · surgery Cystic neoplasms of the pancreas are a rare but important group because of their special clinical presentation and biology . Serous cystic neo-plasms (SCN) are the most common cystic tumors followed by mucinous cystic neoplasms， solid pseudopapillary neoplasms，and intraductal papillary-mucinous neoplasms . SCN of pancreas are rare cystic epithelial neoplasms composed of glycogen-rich ductular-type epithelial cells that produce a wa-tery fluid similar to serum. Most are benign (serous cystadenomas) either serous microcystic adenoma(SMA) or serous oligocystic adenoma (SOA) . SMAs usually have innumerable tiny cysts that are lined by uniform， glycogen-rich cuboidal epithelial cells. SOAs have a countable number of cysts， which are usually greater than 2 cm in diameter . A solid variant of serous cystadenoma (SSA) has also been described .

【7】They account for about 25% of all cystic tumors of the pancreas which collectively are considered relatively rare . It has been reported that serous cystic tumors alone comprise about 1 to 2% of all exocrine pancreatic neoplasm . In addition to sporadic cases， an association with von Hippel-Lindau disease has been reported . The mean age at presentation is 66 years (range 18 to 91 years) with a predominance of women (70%). The neoplasms occur most frequently in the body or tail； the remaining tumors involve the head of the pancreas . About one third of the neo-plasms present as an incidental finding at routine physical examination or at autopsy. Modern imaging techniques have increased the frequency with which they are now discovered . We present two cases of SMA of pancreas both of which were diagnosed incidentally during clinical and radiographic evalu-ations for unrelated reasons.

【8】CASE REPORT

【9】Case 1

【10】A 61 year old woman referred to the surgery depart-ment of Harran University Medical Faculty with epigastric pain， dispeptic complaints and nausea for the past six months. She did not have a prior history of major disease， operation， trauma， smoking or al-cohol consumption. On physical examination， there was epigastric sensitivity and pain. Blood chemistry， hemogram and tumor markers were all within normal limits. On abdominal ultrasonography (US)， a 9x8x7cm mass with cystic component was detected at the tail of pancreas. A dynamic contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) scan was performed and a mass with lobulated contours and of heterogenous density con-taining multiple cysts was detected. The splenic artery， superior mesenteric artery， superior mesenteric vein were all normal and without any signs of compression or invasion. Distal pancreatectomy was performed and the patient recovered uneventfully.

【11】The specimen sent to our pathology department was10x8.5x7 cm of distal pancreatectomy material. The cut surface showed a well circumscribed 9x8x6 cm mass composed of numerous tiny microcysts giving the tumor a spongious appearance .The central portion of the mass involved a stellate shaped fibrous dense area. On histopathologic evaluation， a micro-cystic tumor lined by epithelial cells of cuboidal shape and clear cytoplasm with normochrom small round nuclei was seen . These microcysts were em-bedded in a fibrous stroma rich of vascular structures. The cells lining the microcysts showed strong PAS positivity and stained diffusely with low molecu-lar weight keratin (LMWK). With these findings the lesion was diagnosed as SMA of the pancreas. The patient is well and without any complications for the last four years in her routine clinic controls.

【12】Case2

【13】A 71 year old man referred to the surgery depart-ment of Harran University Medical Faculty with abdominal pain and gradually increasing jaundice for the last two months. He was a farmer and had no history of smoking， alcohol abuse， prior major illnesses， or surgical interventions. On physical exami-nation， his skin， scleras were jaundiced and he had right abdominal pain on palpation. Blood chemistry revealed total bilirubin： 7.6mg/dl； direct bilirubin：6mg/dl； ALP： 365 mg/dl； SGOT： 75 mg/dl； SGPT：93mg/dl； CA19.9：1000 IU/ml. On abdominal CT scan and magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography(MRCP)， 2 cystic lesions of 6x5x4 cm and 4x3x2 cm were detected in right liver lobe. These cystic lesions were in relation with bile ducts. Besides， a 2 cm diam-eter cystic lesion was detected at the head of pancreas which lacked communication to pancreatic duct on MRCP. The patient was operated with a diagnosis of possible hydatic cyst disease. The cysts in liver were excised and choledocothomy and T-tube drainage were performed. Total excision was done for the mass at pancreatic head.

【14】The specimens from the liver were 6x5x4 cm and 4x3x2cm soft cystic lesions of white gelatinous appearance. The cysts contained yellow colored watery fluid. The specimen excised from pancreas was 2.5x2x0.7 cm grayish-yellow firm nodular mass with a spongy ap-pearance on cut surface. On histopathologic evalua-tion， the cysts removed from liver were diagnosed as hydatid cyst'and mass from pancreas as SMA with similar histomorphologic findings as the first case. The mass was composed of microcysts lined with cuboidal epithelial cells which were PAS positive， embedded in a fibrous stroma. The patient recovered uneventfully and is well for the last two years in his controls.

【15】DISCUSSION

【16】Serous cystadenomas are benign cystic tumors of pancreas. Although rare cases of serous cystadeno-carcinomas have been reported， the interpretation of these cases as malignant is controversial. They are seen more commonly in women. The two thirds of patients present with symptoms such as abdominal pain， abdominal mass， nausea， and vomiting or weight loss. The remaining one third of the tumors is dis-covered incidentally on routine physical examination or at autopsy . Both of our patients had nonspecific general symptoms like abdominal pain， nausea and second patient had jaundice. Our male patient’s jaundice was related to the big hyda-tid cysts in his liver. Most of the tumors occur in the tail or body of the pancreas however， they are also described in the head of the pancreas . In our case 1， the lesion was located at the tail and in case2， at the head of the pancreas. In both patients， the lesions were well circumscribed and did not cause any specific related signs or symptoms. Diagnosis of SMAs relies mainly on imaging techniques such as US， CT and MRCP. Despite these multiple modalities， except in centers having great experience in pancreatic imaging， an accurate preoperative diagnosis of SMA can be made in only 40% of the patients . In our patients， preoperative accurate radiologic diagnosis of SMA couldn’t be done and correct diagnosis was set by histopathological examination. Grossly， they are well demarcated and usually have a central scar. In our cases， the macroscopic features of case 1 were more typical whereas in case 2 only a firm spongy mass was observed. The microscopic features of SCO both cases were typically the same as described in literature. Immunohistochemically， SMAs are posi-tive for cytokeratims 7，8， 18 and 19. In addition， the neoplastic cells may focally Express CA 19.9 and B72.3. They are uniformly negative for CEA，tryp sin， chromogranin-A， synaptophysin，S-100 protein， demsin， vimentin，factor VIII-related antigen and actin. Both of our patients were positive for LMWCK. In a recently published study， MUC1， MUC6 and inhibin positivity of the neoplastic cells is stated to support the centroacinar origin of this tumor . The aetiology and pathogenesis of the neoplasm are unknown. An association with von Hippel-Lindau disease has been reported and confirmed by recent genetic molecular investigations . Ultrastructurally， the epithelial cells lining the microcysts show similar features to those of centroacinar cells and contain numerous glycogen granules， however， zymogen and neurosecretory granules are absent . In both of our cases the cell cytoplasms were clear or pale eosinophilic； and they showed strong PAS positivity that is removed by diastase digestion. Both the gross and the microscopic appearances of SMAs are so distinctive that an accurate diagnosis is possible on routine examination in almost all cases . The dif-ferential diagnosis of SMA is narrow and includes lymphangioma， hemangioma and metastatic renal cell carcinoma. If the epithelial lining of microcysts is flat， and resembles a hemangioma or lymphan1- gioma the distinction canDV De be made by performing endothelial and epithelial markers . Microscopically， the presence of clear cytoplasm and acinar growth pattern of SMA may resemble renal cell carcinoma. But the nuclear irregularity， distinct nucleoli， mitotic activity and coexpression ofvimen-tin and keratin typical of renal cell carcinoma help to make the differential diagnosis . Lastly， serous cystadenocarcinomas，which are very rare tumors of the pancreas， have histologic features similar to that of SMAs. Although mild nuclear pleomorphism and perineural invasion suggest a diagnosis of carcinoma， the distinction on histologic grounds alone may be quite challenging when the morphologic anaplastic criteria are subtle and usually may depend on extra positive findings； such as， the presence or absence of metastasis . Since there is only a minimal risk of malignant transformation， the prognosis of patients with this neoplasm is excellent . Surgical removal of the mass is suggested only when the tumor is symptomatic. But， conservative management has the risk of progressive growth and development of complications .

【17】CONCLUSIONS

【18】In both of our cases， the preoperative accurate radio-logic diagnosis of SMA was not done and our male patient had additional hydatid cysts that needed to be removed. In conclusion， SMAs of pancreas are more frequently identified with the progressions in radiologic imaging techniques. The differential diagnosis from other cystic tumors as well as from non-neoplastic cysts is very important because of the differences in their management and histo-pathology is still the most reliable method in the diagnosis.

【0】Letter to the Editor

【1】Minimally invasive enucleation with zero ischemia for malignancies. The Cluj Napoca experience We read， with great interest， the article “Laparoscopic enu-cleation of a giant submucosal esophageal lipoma. Case re-port and literature review"， published by Tsalis et al. The authors present an important surgical approach for the man-agement of benign tumors of the esophagus， by performing a laparoscopic enucleation of a lower esophageal lipoma. By presenting the surgical experience of our university hospital， we wish to emphasize that minimally invasive enucleation is not only applicable for benign tumors， but also for malignant ones with comparable results regarding recovery of the pa-tient， as well as long term survival.Minimally invasive enucle-ation is recommended for symptomatic benign tumors and for those greater than 5 cm， as presented by this surgical team， but lately this technique was applied also for malignancies be-cause it has proven it's usefulness regarding the delay in can-cer progression and the reduction in surgical discomfort of the patient. Large clinical trails lack， but some reports have been published， as is the case of nephrectomy for the management of a secondary metastasis carried out by Cochetti et al. In their case， minimally invasive surgery allowed the preserva-tion of renal function， as well as the possibility for the medi-cal oncologists to continue adjuvant therapy. Consistent data from human clinical trails lacks， but these reports were preced-ed by animal studies，a s the one presented by Zhang et al.

【2】They approach small renal cell carcinomas by suggesting the use of a laparoscopic simple enucleation， followed by coagu-lation on the tumor bed using an argon beam coagulator， with excellent results regarding recovery and blood loss. Nephron sparing surgery is accompanied by adjuvant solutions such as the thallium laser assistance  or microwave ablation ， with superior results in comparison with the radical nephrec-tomy for pTla and pT1b carcinomas . Apart from renal ma-lignancies and rare benign tumors， as is the case of esophageal ones， laparoscopic enucleation with zero ischemia was also at-tempted by Makdissi et al.  in the case of four hepatocellu-lar carcinoma cases and two benign liver tumors， with free pa-thology surgical margins and excellent post-surgical recovery. Our experience confirmed the usefulness of minimally inva-sive enucleation with minimal ischemia especially in the case of the patients where renal preservation is crucial because of pre-operative insufficiency or multiple renal lesions.The long-term survival is comparative with a standard partial nephrec-tomy， even if sometimes the histopathology results showed a pseudo capsule tumor invasion. Thus， minimally invasive enu-cleation should be performed not only for benign tumors， but also for aggressive cancers if the lesion is locally confined on preoperative imaging， easily delineated intraoperatively and does not seem to growly invade beyond the pseudocapsule.

【0】Background：

【1】Primary tracheal schwannoma is a rare neurogenic tumor. Early stage presents with nonspecific symptoms， and asthma is sometimes misdiagnosed. However， as the tumor grows， it presents with obstructive symptoms of the tracheal lumen. This tumor has been managed by open resection surgery until recently when endoscop-ic excision became an option. The endoscopic excision reduces complications， operative time， and postopera-tive recovery period and is indicated in nonrecurrent surgical cases in which tumors are up to 2 cm in size， are pedunculated， and have no extratracheal extension， or in cases of poor cardiopulmonary status. We present a rare case of primary tracheal schwannoma managed by endoscopic excision.

【2】Case Report：

【3】A 37-year-old man was referred to our clinic with progressive shortness of breath and wheezing that started 3months prior to presentation. Computed tomography showed a well-defined rounded， solid intraluminal tra-cheal mass at the proximal segment (at the level of the thoracic inlet). There was no extratracheal extension or enlarged cervical lymph nodes. The patient underwent endoscopic excision of the mass. A sickle knife， mi-cro scissor， and suction diathermy were used for incision， stripping， and hemostasis done through the tumor pedicle. The first postoperative visit after 2 weeks showed subjective symptom improvement， and the flexible bronchoscope showed a completely healed surgical site with patent airway. Histopathological examination and immunohistochemistry confirmed the diagnosis of primary tracheal schwannoma.

【4】Conclusions： Primary tracheal schwannoma is rare. An endoscopic excision is an excellent option， but patients need to be appropriately selected and followed up to avoid recurrence.

【5】Keywords： Neurilemmoma· Tracheal Neoplasms· Endoscopy· Case Reports Primary tumors of the trachea are commonly malignant. Squamous cell carcinoma and adenoid cystic carcinoma are the most common and account for 75% of cases. The remain ing 25% are tumors of multiple histological subtypes， including benign， intermediate， and malignant tumors. Among them is a rare tumor， primary tracheal schwannoma， which is con-sidered a neurogenic tumor， including schwannoma and neu-rofibroma. In its early stage， this tumor presents with non-specific symptoms， and asthma is sometimes misdiagnosed. However， as it grows， it presents with obstructive symptoms of the tracheal lumen. This tumor was managed by open re-section surgery until recently， when endoscopic excision be-gan being used . We present a rare case of primary tra-cheal schwannoma that was managed by endoscopic excision.

【6】Case Report

【7】A 37-year-old man was referred to our clinic by our thoracic surgery colleagues. The patient had progressive shortness of breath and a wheezy chest that started 3 months prior to pre-sentation. There was no associated history of dysphonia or dys-phagia. The patient was seen in another local hospital， where asthma was diagnosed and treated accordingly. He reported temporary improvement with the usage of bronchodilator med-ication. The patient was a lifelong nonsmoker. He had no med-ical or surgical history and was not on any regular medications. The family history was unremarkable， with no history of can-cer. The patient was single and working in the food industry.

【8】The patient was admitted to the hospital. Lung auscultation revealed a prolonged expiratory phase and wheezing over the cervical trachea in the expiratory phase. Multiplanar recon-structions and a contrast-enhanced computed tomography(CT) scan showed a well-defined rounded， solid intraluminal tracheal mass at the proximal segment (at the level of the tho-racic inlet). It had homogeneous density and was enhanced by the contrast agent. It was adherent to the right tracheal wall and measured 17×19×22 mm in maximum mediolateral. anteroposterior， and circumferential dimensions， respective-ly. There was no extratracheal extension and no enlarged cer-vical lymph nodes . Prior to the surgical man-agement， flexible bronchoscopy was done， showing a round， smooth surface， and tan-colored mass in the proximal part of the trachea. It was 3 cm distal from the vocal cords， almost 2cm in maximum diameter， and occluding approximately 90%of the tracheal lumen . Discussion between the anesthetist， thoracic surgeon， and head and neck surgeon was done for the surgical plan. A difficult airway was antic-ipated in our patient， as the trachea was found to be nearly completely occluded by the tumor. The plan was to proceed with fiberoptic intubation and perform an awake tracheosto-my if it failed. The airway was secured by awake tracheostomy， as the fiberoptic intubation was unsuccessful. Given that the mass was in the cervical trachea opposite the second， third， and fourth tracheal ring， low tracheostomy was done in the fifth tracheal ring， where a horizontal incision was made and endotracheal tube size 7 was cuffed， inserted， and secured. The patient then underwent endoscopic excision of the mass. Bronchoscopy was used for the operation. A sickle knife， mi-cro scissor， and suction diathermy were used where incision， stripping， and hemostasis were done through the tumor ped-icle . After the tumor was removed complete-ly， the tracheostomy was closed， and endotracheal intubation was done in the same sitting. Postoperatively，the patient was kept in the Intensive Care Unit for 24 h and extubated there. Immediately after extubation， the patient reported improve-ment in the shortness of breath. On postoperative day 3， the patient was discharged home. The first postoperative visit af-ter 2 weeks showed subjective improvement in preoperative symptoms， and the flexible bronchoscope showed a complete-ly healed surgical site， with a patent airway.

【9】Histopathological examination of the mass showed spindle cells with elongated palisading nuclei， representing an Antoni A growth pattern， negative for increased mitotic activity or ne-crosis. The tumor demonstrated diffuse and strong nuclear and cytoplasmic positivity of S-100 protein . Both the histopathological examination and immunohistochemis-try confirmed the diagnosis of primary tracheal schwannoma.

【10】Discussion

【11】Primary neurogenic tumors of the trachea， which include schwannoma， are rare. Schwannoma arises from the periph-eral nerve sheath； it is less common than neurofibroma . Between 2015 and 2022， 10 cases of primary tracheal schwan-noma were reported in English-anguage literature . It is a benign tumor that is more commonly seen in the dis-tal one-third of the trachea， followed by the upper one-third and then the middle one-third of the trachea . The cause of its development is unknown. It is rarely associated with von Recklinghausen disease .

【12】Primary tracheal schwannoma is a slowly growing tumor commonly seen in young adults， with a female predilection. Its clinical presentation depends on the site， size， extent of the tumor， and degree of airway obstruction . In the early stage of the tumor， most patients reported coughing， wheez-ing， and dyspnea and were misdiagnosed as having asthma and treated accordingly . This led to the delay of diagno-sis and more severe airway symptoms， which were reported to be 17 months on average from the onset of symptoms .

【13】Imaging plays a significant role in diagnosing tracheal tumors and surgical planning. A chest X-ray is not helpful in this con-text， as it is normal in up to 75% of cases . CT of the chest is the main imaging that can evaluate the presence of a mass， its location， size， the degree of airway obstruction， and if there is an extra tracheal extension. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is superior for imaging the trachea， especially when assessing the extratracheal extension. However， based on the reported literature， MRI did not add more information， and the chest CT was enough for this evaluation . For further evaluation， flexible bronchoscopy is used to visualize the mass，and a bi-opsy can be taken . To confirm the diagnosis of schwan-noma， an immunohistochemical analysis must reveal diffuse positivity of S-100 protein and vimentin .

【14】In patients presenting with obstructive symptoms， compre-hensive multidisciplinary perioperative airway management is critical for effective treatment and uneventful outcomes. Most of the national guidelines for the management of difficult air-ways recommend methods that maintain spontaneous respira-tion while trying to secure a definitive airway. These methods mainly include awake tracheal intubation or awake tracheos-tomy . In our case， fiberoptic intubation failed， and further intubation attempts can cause bleeding and fragmentation of the tumor. Consequently， an awake tracheostomy was chosen to secure the airway.

【15】The criterion standard management of tracheal schwannoma is open surgical tracheal resection with end-to-end anastomosis.

【16】However， it is not suitable for long segmental tracheal resec-tion . Reports of the use of endoscopic excision of this tu-mor have increased in recent literature . The endoscop-ic approach includes laser resection， electrocautery snaring， argon plasma coagulation， cryotherapy， endoscopic excision， microdebridement， and high frequency gamma knife . Chen et al  described a different approach using video-as-sisted thoracoscopic window resection with a good postoper-ative outcome. However， it was limited to tracheal tumors OC-cupying less than one-third of the tracheal circumference and less than 1.5 cm in the vertical dimension.

【17】The choice of open surgical vs endoscopic management of tracheal schwannoma is influenced by the size of the tumor， pedicle of the tumor (sessile vs pedunculated mass)， extra tra-cheal component， and cardiopulmonary function of the pa-tient. Endoscopic management is indicated when the tumor size is up to 2 cm， it is a pedunculated mass， there is no extra tracheal extension， or the patient has poor cardiopulmonary function . We believe that successful endoscopic removal depends on appropriate tumor visualization and the ability to remove the tumor with an adequate margin. This applied to the present case，which met the criteria to be managed endo-scopically， as the tumor was pedunculated with a clear base， completely within the trachea， and less than 2 cm.

【18】Although endoscopic management is superior to open surgi-cal management in terms of reducing complications，operative time， and patient recovery period， recurrence after endoscop-ic excision is an issue. In our case， the follow-up period was short， but as reported by Sharma et al  and Gibb et al ， postoperative bronchoscopic surveillance showed no recur-rence in 8 and 18 months， respectively.

【19】On the other hand， Ge et al  found recurrence by broncho-scopic examination 2 weeks after endoscopic excision， which was managed by open surgical excision. We believe this ear-ly recurrence can be attributed to an incomplete excision of the mass， according to their report， in which 75% of the mass was excised by the endoscopic technique . Once recurrence of this tumor occurs， the choice of open surgical trachealre-section becomes absolute. The onset of recurrence is variable. and 1 case reported late recurrence 12 years after endoscop-ic excision . Given this fact and the slow-growing nature of the tumor， it is preferable to have annual imaging， including CT chest， magnetic resonance， or positron emission， to detect recurrence， or to perform imaging when the patient becomes symptomatic again. Other modalities include bronchoscopic surveillance for recurrence detection .

【20】The general prognosis of primary tracheal schwannoma man-aged surgically or endoscopically is excellent .

【21】Primary tracheal schwannoma is rare. Imaging， including chest CT or MRl， needs to be considered once upper respiratory symp-toms are persistent. Endoscopic excision is an excellent option for primary tracheal schwannoma with no extra tracheal ex-tension， up to 2 cm in size， and pedunculated mass. Patients need to be appropriately selected to avoid recurrence.

【0】Background：

【1】Kikuchi-Fujimoto disease (KFD) is an enigmatic disease， with a distinctive histopathology and a benign and self-limited course. It is more frequent in young Asian women. Autoimmune diseases are identified as one of its triggers； primarily SLE， which may precede， be concomitant with， or develop after the diagnosis of KFD. Patients with KFD should receive periodic follow-up for several years to detect possible evolution of SLE. The main feature of KFD is lymphadenopathy， and cervical lymph nodes are involved in 50% to 98% of cases. Other symptoms such as fever， fatigue， weight loss， and arthralgias are also reported. Differential diagnosis between KFD and SLE is a challenge. When KFD and SLE coexist， a lymph node biopsy may be diagnostic. Treatment should be symptomatic with analgesics and anti-inflammatories， with complete resolution in 3 to 4 months. Corticosteroids and immunosuppressive therapy are justified only in cases concomitant with SLE.

【2】Case Report： We report a case of KFD in a 28-year-old woman who was initially negative for anti-nuclear antibodies (ANA) and anti-double-stranded deoxyribonucleic acid antibodies (anti-dsDNA)， but who became antibody-positive and presented with lupus nephritis 2 months later.

【3】Conclusions： We present a case of a patient with KFD who developed SLE 2 months later； highlighting the importance of recognizing its association and its possible progression to monitor for future development of SLE and provide timely treatment to avoid complications. We also compared the clinical， laboratory， and histological similari-ties between the 2 entities.

【4】Keywords： Histiocytic Necrotizing Lymphadenitis· Lupus Erythematosus， Systemic· Pathology， Molecular Kikuchi-Fujimoto disease (KFD) is a rare autoimmune-mediat-ed entity with a benign and self-limiting course . It pres-ents with a higher prevalence in Asia； however， it has been reported worldwide， it is more frequent in young women and has been associated with neoplastic， genetic， infectious and autoimmune states， specifically systemic lupus erythemato-sus (SLE) which may precede， coexist with， or occur subse-quent to the diagnosis of KFD. Patients with the initial diagno-sis of KFD should be screened for SLE， and periodic follow-up is recommended to detect possible evolution of SLE . Some clinical and biochemical manifestation of KFD can be shared by SLE and some diagnostic criteria of SLE can be present in KFD . The association between KFD and SLE is rare； out of 330 cases reported between 1991 and 2005， only 28 pa-tients with KFD met the diagnostic criteria for SLE. A Medline search revealed that， between 2005 and 2012， there were only 9 additional cases of SLE associated with KFD reported around the world j. Its association with SLE was reported by Kucukardali et al， who found SLE and KFD occurred concom-itantly in 13% of cases . In a systemic search that included113 patients， SLE had been diagnosed before KFD in 18% of cases，simultaneously in 51%， and after KFD in 31%，and sev-eral cohorts with prolonged follow-up have shown that many patients develop SLE over time .

【5】The main characteristics of KFD are lymphadenitis (50% to98%)， fever (30% to 67%)， and headache (17% to 33%) . The skin is an extra-lymphatic organ that is affected in 10%to 40% of cases . The most frequent laboratory findings are increased acute-phase reactants， leukopenia with thrombocy-topenia ， and， in 7% of the cases， anti-nuclear and anti-DNA antibodies are present . The histopathology finding is histio-cytic necrotizing lymphadenitis. SLE is a multisystem autoim-mune disease， and lymphadenopathy occurs in approximately40% of patients， mainly in young women . Differential diag-nosis between KFD and SLE is a challenge because SLE close-ly simulates the clinical and histopathologic features of KFD. Fever and lymphadenopathy are common clinical presenta-tions in both conditions ， so their discrimination is based on clinical course， histopathological findings， immunohisto-chemistry，and determination of antibodies . Treatment is symptomatic， with analgesics and anti-inflammatories . Corticoids and immunosuppressive therapy are justified in cas-es with concomitant SLE.

【6】The aim of this report is to present the case of a 28-year-old woman with KFD who developed lupus nephritis 2 months lat-er. We highlight its association and the importance of follow-up to detect possible progression， and compare the clinical， laboratory， and histologic similarities between these 2 entities.

【7】The patient was a 28-year-old woman who did not have a family or personal history of autoimmune disease. Herillness started 1 month before her hospital admission， with fever of39℃， predominantly nocturnal，accompanied by sweating， fa-tigue， severe headache， anxiety， and agitation. She had weight loss of 10 kg， accompanied by decreased appetite， nausea， and foul-smelling， greenish， loose stools without mucus or blood.

【8】A physical examination on admission showed hypotension， tachycardia， polypnea， and fever of 39℃. She was conscious， agitated，talkative， and anxious. She had alopecia and her face had papules， pustules， vesicles with hypopigmentation， melic-eric crusts， and lichenification . The oral cavity had red， non-painful ulcers， candidiasis， and painful bilateral pa-rotid hypertrophy. The neck had left-side adenopathy fixed to deep planes of 2x2 cm， of hard consistency， painful on palpa-tion ， without airway compromise. Precordial ar-eas were without alterations， and she had bilateral pleural ef-fusion syndrome of approximately 40%. The right axillary had adenomegaly of 1 cm of rubbery consistency not fixed to deep planes and painful. Her abdomen was soft and depressible， without signs of rebound tenderness. There was hepatomeg-aly without splenomegaly. The genital area had transvaginal bleeding. She had edema in lower extremities， normal pulses， and reflexes， and no arthritis.

【9】Initial laboratory tests  showed acute kidney involve-ment， cholestatic hyperbilirubinemia， hepatocellular affection， and pancytopenia， with negative antinuclear and anti-DNA an-tibodies， hypocomplementemia， elevation of acute-phase re-actants， negative viral panel and TORCH， urine culture and blood culture without bacterial growth. Plain neck tomography was performed， showing right cervical adenomegalies， form-ing conglomerates radiologically diffuse and heterogeneous. Ultrasound of the liver and bile ducts showed grade Il hepatic steatosis and spleen with normal size and echogenicity. Suspecting a lymphoproliferative syndrome， bone marrow aspirate was performed with normal cellularity for age. Excisional lymph node biopsy reported necrotizing histiocytic lymphadenitis and immunohistochemistry with the streptavi-din-biotin system showed presence of CD 68-positive and CD123-negative in macrophage cells ； therefore， KFD was diagnosed.

【10】After ruling out infectious， lymphoproliferative， and autoim-mune processes such as SLE， she received symptomatic treat-ment with paracetamol and naproxen. She presented complete clinical and biochemical remission during a period of 60 days. Later， a stormy course was observed， with appearance of renal involvement . Given the high suspicion of lupus nephri-tis， the renal biopsy reported class III lupus nephropathy and an immunological profile consistent with positive ANA (1：160) and anti-dsDNA， hypocomplementemia (C3 29 mg/dl， C46 mg/dl)， and lymphopenia (500 109/L). The patient met the American College of Rheumatology criteria for SLE. Therefore， induction to remission was initiated with pulses of methylprednisolone at a dose of 1 g/day for 3 days and cyclophosphamide with a cumulative dose of 7.1 g. The maintenance therapy was per-formed with prednisone， mycophenolate mofetil， and chloro-quine. By the eighth month of treatment， the glomerular fil-tration rate and serum creatinine normalized with a decrease of proteinuria and recovery of serum albumin and the other laboratory parameters . After 2 years of follow-up， she remains in remission.

【11】The etiology of KFD remains unknown， although a viral or au-toimmune pathogenesis， such as systemic lupus erythemato-sus (SLE)， has been suggested . The exact physio-patholog-ical relationship between these 2 diseases is still unclear . Kucukardali et al reported 28 cases of SLE-associated KDF that met the diagnostic criteria for SLE； of those， only 6 were diag-nosed with SLE after KFD . Santana et al reported a total of35 cases of SLE-associated KFD， in which 14 patients were di-agnosed with SLE after a diagnosis of KFD . Goldblatt et al reported 4 cases in which KFD preceded a clinical and immu-nological diagnosis of SLE by between 3 and 14 months  and Patra et al reported a case of a woman who developed SLE2 years after KFD . Sopena et al reported that only 25 of (ESR) at the beginning， and these can be found in both enti-ties . Our patient also had diarrhea， which is rarely 113 patients with KFD-SLE had lupus nephritis， and of those， only 8 develop lupus nephritis after KFD. Therefore， in patients with KFD-SLE， the prevalence of lupus nephritis is lower in pa-tients with classic SLE . In our case， KFD was present before lupus nephritis， and the time of progression was 2 months. Some authors have postulated that KFD is prodromal for SLE， and this is supported by the fact that microscopic features of KFD can be similar to those found in lupus lymphadenitis ； therefore， periodic follow-up is recommended to detect pos-sible evolution of SLE .

【18】Our patient had common symptoms and laboratory findings of KFD， such as fever， fatigue， arthralgias， pancytopenia，espe-cially severe anemia，increased erythrocyte sedimentation rate reported in KFD. In this regard， Giardia lamblia， Brucella meli- tensis， and Entamoeba histolytica have been reported as trig-gering agents for KFD  and they should be considered in the differential diagnosis of fever and malaise associated with cervical lymphadenopathy . Nevertheless， in our case， there were signs of infectious disease， and the cause of diar-rhea remained uncertain.

【19】KFD skin lesions are nonspecific (eg， macules， papules， plaques， facial malar erythema， erosions， patches， and nodules) and have been observed in up to 40% of cases and may be simi-lar to those observed in lupus. Kim et al found that SLE-KFD patients tend to have high incidence of skin manifestations ， and patients with KFD and skin lesions can develop SLE . Therefore， clinical features of SLE and KFD can be similar； nev-ertheless， definite discrimination between those 2 diseases is based on histopathological findings. Histopathologic features that support SLE include an increased number of plasma cells， hematoxylin bodies， DNA deposits in the vascular walls， neu-trophilic infiltration， and varying degrees of coagulative necro-sis with Azzopardi phenomenon . The histopathology of KFD is sufficiently distinctive to allow its recognition as a spe-cific entity ； the absence of hematoxylin bodies and neutrophils and CD68+ histiocyte infiltrate indicate KFD rath-er than SLE， and our patient showed definite features of KFD. With respect to autoantibodies， it is important to note that in KFD they are only present in 7% of cases  whereas in SLE they are positive in over than 98% of cases. In KFD， lab-oratory findings are nonspecific， including elevated ESR， neu-tropenia， lymphocytosis， mildly elevated transaminase，elevat-ed LDH and ANA， and reduced C3 values. These findings were observed in our patient， and have been reported in the litera-ture . Table 2 provides a comparison of clinical， laborato-ry， and histological findings between KFD and SLE.

【20】Regarding treatment of KFD， 64 to 80% of cases do not require specific therapy， whereas SLE patients need immunosuppres-sive management to modify its course and prognosis. In KFD， treatment is symptomatic with nonsteroidal anti-inflammato-ry drugs (NSAIDs) with a short course of steroids. When KFD coexists with SLE， it can show a more aggressive course， and the treatment is aimed to prevent relapse . After 2 years of follow-up， our patient is in remission of lupus nephritis and she remains in disease remission.

【21】The presence of histiocytic necrotizing lymphadenitis， the ab-sence of ANAs， double-stranded DNA antibodies， and the fa-vorable clinical response with symptomatic management al-lowed us to rule out the diagnosis of SLE at the beginning of the disease. Subsequently， recurrence， stormy course， presence of pancytopenia， hypocomplementemia， erythematous skin le-sions， and rapid and progressive deterioration of renal function confirmed by renal biopsy substantiated the diagnosis of SLE.

【22】Conclusions

【23】We present the case of a 28-year-old woman with KFD who was initially negative for antibodies and developed SLE 2 months later. Differential diagnosis between these 2 entities is diffi-cult due to the similar spectrum of clinical manifestations； therefore， biopsy， immunohistochemistry， and antibody deter-mination are necessary. We emphasize the importance of rec-ognizing the association of these 2 entities and possible pro-gression to provide timely treatment and avoid complications.

【0】Background：

【1】Tracheobronchopathia osteochondroplastica (TO) is a rare disorder characterized by cartilaginous or ossified submucosal nodules of unknown etiology that project into the tracheobronchial lumen. TO is often accompa-nied by endotracheal stenosis from cartilage proliferation and is often detected by difficult endotracheal intu-bation incidence.

【2】Case Report：

【3】Here we report the case of a patient (67-year-old man) with TO scheduled to undergo robot-assisted total prostatectomy for prostate cancer. The tracheal lumen was especially narrow at an area 1 cm below the glot-tis， with the smallest lumen diameter being 9 mm. After rapid induction， the bronchoscope passed through the stenosed region， and a 6.5-mm spiral endotracheal tube (ETT) was inserted with bronchoscopic assistance. However， because of resistance， the spiral ETT could not pass through the stenosed area. After changing to a6.5-mm normal ETT， intubation was successfully performed with gentle rotation. Owing to the rotation， the tip entered and gained access to the gap between nodules. With use of a bronchoscope， we confirmed that the tip of the ETT was advanced 10 cm from the glottis， where the site of maximum stenosis was not covered by the tube cuff， and where the tip did not cross the bifurcation. After surgery no bleeding or edema was found on bronchoscopy.

【4】Conclusions：

【5】In patients with TO， it is important to assess the airway condition and prepare for difficult intubation. In this case，tracheal intubation was performed with rotation using a bronchoscope and normal ETT.

【6】MeSH Keywords： Airway Management · Anesthesia · Intubation， Intratracheal Tracheobronchopathia osteochondroplastica (TO) is a rare dis-order characterized by cartilaginous or ossified submucosal nodules of unknown etiology that project into the tracheo bronchial lumen. The condition is usually asymptomatic but can， in rare cases， result in upper respiratory symptoms . These respiratory symptoms can be identified via computed tomography (CT) results and confirmed with bronchoscopy . Although TO was reported in 0.4% of performed bronchosco-pies ， its frequency is actually higher  since TO can be as-ymptomatic or present with nonspecific respiratory symptoms such as chronic cough and wheezing， often leading to misdi-agnosis . TO is also one of the rare causes of difficult intu-bation. This case report illustrates the importance of appro-priate airway management for a patient with TO.

【7】Case Report

【8】A 67-year-old man (height， 168 cm； weight， 70 kg) with TO was scheduled for robot-assisted total prostatectomy for prostate cancer. At 51 years old he was diagnosed with TO via bron-choscopy. At age 64， he was scheduled for intracardiac repair of an atrial septal defect (ASD). However， intubation could not be performed because of considerable endotracheal tube(ETT) resistance， although mask ventilation was possible. A few months later， the patient was successfully intubated with a 6.5-mm inter-diameter \[ID\] normal ETT using an ETT intro-ducer， and the ASD repair surgery was completed.

【9】(B) CT scan image 1 cm beneath the glottis； (C) CT scan image 3 cm beneath the glottis.

【10】In the latter procedural attempt， the anesthesia was carefully planned on the basis of his medical history. Preoperative exam-ination revealed no significant complications other than TO. He had no respiratory symptoms， had normal respiratory function， and airway stenosis was not detected on chest X-ray imaging. A chest CT scan revealed endotracheal stenosis due to bony nodules under the glottis protruding from right and left  into the tracheal lumen 2 cm away. The lumen was especially narrow at an area 1 cm below the glottis， with 9 mm being the smallest lumen diameter. The distance from the stenotic site to the tracheal bifurcation was 9 cm. There was no apparent change in the TO status between the period before ASD surgery and this time. Since mask ven-tilation and intubation with a thin tube was possible in previ-ous anesthesia induction， we planned for rapid induction with propofol injection. After that， and after confirming mask ven-tilation， we planned to administer muscle relaxants and intu-bate with an ID 6.5-mm (outer diameter \[OD\]， 8.9 mm) spiral ETT under bronchoscopic (OD， 5.5 mm) (Ambu， Copenhagen， Denmark) guidance with a McGRATH@ (Medtronic， UK) video laryngoscope. Since the arm of the machine is close to the ETT in robotic surgery， we planned to use a spiral tube to prevent bending or kinking of the ETT. Using the McGRATH， part of a subglottic nodule became visible . On bronchosco-py， the nodules were confirmed on both sides of the tracheal lumen below the glottis. The bronchoscope passed through the stenosed region， and the 6.5-mm spiral. ETT was inserted with bronchoscopic assistance. However， due to resistance，the spi-ral ETT could not pass through the stenosed area . Next， a 6.5-mm normal ETT was successfully inserted with gen-tle rotation. Owing to the rotation， the tip entered and gained access to the gap between nodules. Specifically， we rotated the ETT clockwise and unidirectionally to reduce resistance to pass through the stenosis. The tip of the ETT was advanced10 cm from the glottis， where the site of maximum stenosis was not covered by the tube cuff， and where the tip did not cross the bifurcation . No bleeding was noted on bronchoscopy.

【11】Intraoperatively， the tube tip was confirmed to be in front of the tracheal bifurcation in the Trendelenburg position. There was no difficulty with mechanical ventilation， despite some air leakage and formation of foamy saliva due to the imperfect seal caused by the diffuse tracheal nodules. After the patient awakened， the ETT was removed. The bronchoscope， howeV-er， was only removed after ensuring the absence of bleeding or stenosis due to tracheal edema . The general an-esthesia time was 451 min， of which 287 min were spent in the Trendelenburg position. The patient had an uneventful re-covery with no respiratory symptoms after general anesthesia.

【12】Discussion

【13】Inserting the ETT with rotation into the trachea was a good idea in this case since， with rotation， the tip pressure did not concentrate in a single place. Because major nodules existed on both sides within short distance ， ETT inser-tion into the trachea was not possible with a normal intubation technique. Additionally， the selection of a normal tube instead of a spiral one was useful because of its stiffness， which helped to transfer the entry force， moving the ETT forward. Moreover， the information that mask ventilation had been previously un-eventful， and that an ID 6.5-mm ETT could pass with the as-sistance of a bougie， was helpful for surgery planning. Unlike tracheomalacia， the airway lumen after muscle relaxant ad-ministration is generally not changed or narrowed. Although awake intubation may be necessary if there is a risk of “can’t intubate， can't ventilate" in a predictably difficult airway man-agement situation， we confirmed that we could mask venti-late with rapid induction. Undoubtedly， estimating the size and shape of the tracheal lumen on CT images preoperative-ly was useful； because of bronchoscopy， the intubation was performed gently. Bronchoscopic assistance helped to confirm stenosis， distance to the tracheal bifurcation， and the location of the ETT cuff. Using the bronchoscope after extubation， we were able to confirm the absence of bleeding.

【14】Bony TO nodules might cause ETT cuff rupture . A previous report used a laryngeal mask to prevent massive air leak . In our patient， cuff rupture was avoided by evaluating the cuff position and stenosis by bronchoscopy. Although some air leak-age was observed， it did not affect the ventilation conditions.

【15】When confronted with a patient with TO， avoidance of airway manipulation seems ideal but may not always be prudent. A supraglottic airway device， i.e.， the laryngeal mask airway， has been successfully applied to patients who required general an-esthesia for intra-abdominal procedures . However， endo-tracheal intubation is typically necessary when positive air-way pressures are needed for ventilation . As this patient was expected to undergo prolonged laparoscopic surgery in the Trendelenburg position， considering the risk of aspiration， endotracheal intubation was chosen over a supraglottic air-way device. In patients with severe intra-airway projections， preoperative bronchoscopic interventions such as dilation and removal of obstructive spurs should be considered .

【16】Conclusions

【17】In a patient with TO， tracheal intubation with rotation was performed using a bronchoscope. For safe anesthetic man-agement of patients with TO， it is important to anticipate a difficult airway， which requires appropriate airway assess-ment and planning.

【0】ABSTRACT Introduction： Stroke causes a variety of neurological signs and symptoms， which vary depending on the extent， area of involvement， and underlying cause. Coma， hemiplegia， paraplegia， monoplegia， cranial nerve palsy， speech disturbance， and sensory impairment are examples. Hemiplegia is the most common， affecting approximately90% of patients. Objectives： To investigate the prevalence of metabolic syndrome in stroke patients. In addition， to investigate the role of various components of metabolic syndrome in stroke development. Methods： During the study period of 2 years， all patients with stroke aged more than 30 years and less than 60 years were admitted to Darbhanga Medical College and Hospital， Bihar， India. A minimum of 50 stroke patients must be over the age of 30 and under the age of 60. We used simple random sampling. For analysis， SPSS (22.0) was used. A detailed history of all subjects will be taken， particularly a family history of hypertension， diabetes mellitus， weight gain， alcohol use， and a history of other cerebrovascular disease risk factors. Results： Out of 50 stroke patients， 28 had metabolic syndrome. The prevalence of metabolic syndrome in stroke patients was 56%. 70% were men and 30% were women. When compared to males， females had a higher incidence of metabolic syndrome. It is， however， not statistically significant. The most common mode of presentation in both strokes with and without metabolic syndrome was weakness， followed by deviation of the angle of the mouth， aphasia， and loss of consciousness. Conclusion： Long-term follow-up population-based studies have shown that healthy people with Metabolic syndrome have a significantly increased risk of major cardiovascular events， such as stroke and cardiovascular mortality.

【1】KEYWORDS Coma，hemiplegia， hypertension， hyperlipidemia， stroke

【2】Introduction

【3】Stroke is defined by the World Health Organization as "rapidly developing clinical signs of focal or global disturbance of cere-bral function， lasting more than 24 hours or leading to death， with no apparent cause other than vascular origin" . Stroke causes a variety of neurological signs and symptoms， which vary depending on the extent， area of involvement， and under-lying cause. Coma， hemiplegia， paraplegia， monoplegia， cranial nerve palsy， speech disturbance， and sensory impairment are examples. Hemiplegia is the most common of these， affecting approximately 90% of patients. According to a WHO collabo-rative study conducted in 12 countries， stroke incidence rates ranged from 0.2 to 2.5 per 1000 population per year .

【4】According to an analysis of data from major urban university hospitals in India，stroke accounts for nearly 2% of all hospital cases， 4.5 percent of medical cases， and 20% of neurological admissions . Every year， approximately 15 million new acute onset stroke events occur worldwide. Two-thirds of these people live in low and middle-income countries such as India. It is predicted that 80% of stroke events will occur in these areas by 2050. Stroke is the leading cause of death and disability in developing countries， with an average age of presentation 15years younger than in developed countries .

【5】In recent years， metabolic syndrome has received much at-tention， with various medical societies proposing more than five definitions . For example， the new International Diabetes Federation definition is appropriate for the Indian population because it provides different waist circumferences for different ethnic groups. According to studies， the prevalence of metabolic syndrome in developed countries ranges between 22 and 39%， with India having a strikingly high prevalence rate when com-pared to the rest of Asia approaching developed countries 

【6】According to studies， metabolic syndrome accounts for 30%of all ischemic strokes in women and 4% in men . Metabolic syndrome is linked to an increased risk of acute ischemic stroke in the elderly， with significant contributions from each compo-nent. HDL cholesterol loses its protective role against ischemic stroke in the presence of metabolic syndrome . Unfortu-nately， metabolic syndrome is a common condition， and it may represent an independent risk factor in addition to its compo-nents， necessitating aggressive behavioural and possibly phar-macologic management to prevent future stroke events.

【7】Materials and Methods

【8】All stroke patients over the age of 30 who were admitted to Darbhanga Medical College and Hospital， Bihar， India， between two years were included in the study.

【9】Sample size

【10】Minimum of 50 subjects of a stroke aged more than 30 years and less than 60 years.

【11】Inclusion criteria

【12】1\. Male and female patients with stroke-related neuroradio-logical features. The clinical diagnosis of stroke was based on the criteria established by the Darbhanga Medical Col-lege and Hospital Committee of the national institute of neurological diseases and blindness.

【13】2\. Patients over the age of 30 but under the age of 60.

【14】Exclusion criteria

【15】1\. Patients aged less than 30 and more than 60 years

【16】2\. The neurological deficit that does not meet the above clini-cal/radiological stroke criteria Data was collected using a pretested proforma that met the study's objectives. A thorough history has been taken， as well as a physical examination and necessary investigations. The study's purpose was explained to the patient， and informed consent was obtained. Data will be analysed using appropriate statistical methods. The study has been approved by an ethical committee.

【17】Details of the study subjects

【18】A detailed history of all subjects will be taken， particularly a family history of hypertension，diabetes mellitus， weight gain， alcohol use， and a history of other cerebrovascular disease risk factors (including obesity， smoking， hyperlipidemia， and dia-betes). To rule out atherosclerosis， all subjects underwent a thor-ough physical examination that included all peripheral pulses， including carotids. In addition， waist and hip circumferences were measured， an optic fundoscopic examination for hyperten-sive changes， and cardiovascular， respiratory， abdominal， and CNS examinations.

【19】At least three supine blood pressure measurements with the same standard mercury sphygmomanometer and Littman's stethoscope.

【20】Statistical analysis

【21】The collected observations were analysed with SPSS software(Version 22.0). For analysis， the Chi-Square test was used.

【22】Results

【23】According to table 1， most of the 50 stroke patients with metabolic syndrome were between the ages of 51 and 60(38%). As a result， it is statistically significant. In addition， 70% were men， and 30% were women. When compared to males， females had a higher incidence of metabolic syndrome. It is， however， not statistically significant.

【24】According to table 2， both diabetes mellitus and hypertension were statistically significant risk factors for stroke associated with metabolic syndrome. Finally， the history was the same in strokes with and without metabolic syndrome.

【25】According to table 3， all of the components， such as waist circumference， triglycerides， fasting blood sugar， diastolic blood pressure， systolic blood pressure， and HDL， were found to be sta-tistically significant (p<0.05)， implying that these components played a significant role in patients suffering from metabolic syndrome.

【26】According to table 4， all of the components were significantly(p <0.05) more common in strokes with metabolic syndrome than in strokes without metabolic syndrome.

【27】Discussion

【28】The study included 50 stroke patients admitted to Darbhanga Medical College and Hospital， Bihar， India， within the previous two years. All cases met both the inclusion and exclusion cri-teria. The current study found that 56% of stroke patients had metabolic syndrome， comparable to studies by Boden-Albala et al.  and Simon-Cronin et al. However， compared to other studies conducted by Rodriguez-Colon et al.  and Boden-Albala et al. ， males predominated in patients with both metabolic syndrome and stroke without metabolic syndrome.

【29】Diabetes and hypertension were found to be significant risk factors in our study. However， hypertension is more common than diabetes mellitus in studies conducted by Rodriguez-Colon et al.  and Simon-Cronin et al. When compared to studies conducted by Rodriguez-Colon et al. ， Ashtari F et al. and Kazunori Kayabaet al. ， both smoking and alcohol con-sumption contributed as independent risk factors with 60.7%and 57.1%， respectively. In our study， waist circumference was the most common component of metabolic syndrome among all patients admitted with stroke.

【30】The next most common component was high triglycerides(75% of strokes with metabolic syndrome and 27.3% without metabolic syndrome). Finally， waist circumference was a mi-nor component in studies conducted by Rodriguez-Colon et al. ， Simon-Cronin et al. ， and Ashtari F et al.  be-cause they used NCEP ATP-III criteria， which underestimated waist circumference. In our study， we used the International Diabetes Federation New Definition 2005 for defining metabolic syndrome B， which considers ethnicity and specific values.
